items.title: NASA Science
items.summary: On November 17, fans of interstellar spaceflight around planet Earth were invited to shine a message into the night sky. Traced by a flashlight beam switched on and off, the dashes and dots of a Morse code message captured in this time exposure from the Emirates Astronomical Observatory, are read V-G-R. That's a call sign for the Voyager 1 spacecraft currently in interstellar space some 26 billion kilometers away. How long did it take the message to reach humanity's most distant interstellar spacecraft? Traveling at the speed of light, the answer is one day. In fact, the Voyager 1 spacecraft was confirmed to reach its one light-day distance milestone on November 18, at 10:16:07 UTC, nearly 50 years after launch in 1977.

items.author: Bailey Light

items.title: Entropy Products and the Extremal Limit That Never Comes
items.summary: Two regular black hole horizons need not have an entropy product fixed by the charges and couplings. In Einstein--Maxwell--scalar theory, we construct asymptotically flat branches with products above or below the squared extremal entropy. Regularity selects their horizon scalar values, and different branches can share the charges, couplings, and asymptotic scalar. Each product stays constant as mass and asymptotic scalar vary. The horizon areas stay apart and no extremal limit is reached: the temperature vanishes only where the mass diverges. We prove local existence.
items.author: Kevin Goldstein, Vishnu Jejjala, Suresh Nampuri

items.title: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training substantially improves the visual quality, text rendering, and compositional accuracy of diffusion transformers. Because capabilities such as rendering requested text or composing multiple objects are inherently prompt-dependent, a natural hypothesis is that improving them requires learning complex, input-dependent transformations. To isolate how much of these gains an input-independent shift explains, we probe each RL-tuned model with a deliberately simple parameterization: a fixed set of steering vectors added to the block outputs of the frozen base model. On SD3.5-M, these vectors hold 65x fewer parameters than the RL-tuned LoRA (0.29M against 18.8M). We fit them to match the velocity predictions of public RL-tuned checkpoints, with no reward in the objective.
items.author: Tuna Han Salih Meral, Kaan Oktay, Alec Helbling et al.

items.title: High-temperature Gibbs states are uniformly Markovian and trivial
items.summary: We prove that, above a constant temperature threshold, Gibbs states of local noncommuting qudit Hamiltonians exhibit exponential decay of mutual information and conditional mutual information (CMI). Specifically, we prove exponential decay of the CMI for arbitrary spatial tripartitions $A \sqcup B \sqcup C$ which need not comprise the entire system, thereby establishing a \textit{uniform Markov property} for high-temperature Gibbs states. A central obstruction to proving such bounds is that conventional cluster expansions for the logarithm of reduced Gibbs states can fail to converge due to noncommutativity. Our main insight is to construct a classical representation of the Gibbs state using an overcomplete basis.
items.author: Andrew D. Kim, Tai Hsuan Yang, Jong Yeon Lee

items.title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
items.summary: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. Starting from an initial game, PlayCraft alternates between playing and crafting. In the playing stage, a player agent watches the game screen, uses the controls, and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes while retaining memory. After each episode, it reports its progress, outcomes, decisions, and reflections.
items.author: Weihao Cheng

items.title: Little Red Dots from Primordial Vacuum Bubbles
items.summary: Quantum tunneling transverse to the inflaton trajectory can produce $10^6$--$10^8M_\odot$ primordial black holes at the abundance of JWST's little red dots, without the enhanced curvature perturbations excluded by limits on CMB spectral distortions. Rare vacuum bubbles nucleate during a brief interval of inflation and later form black holes, with adjustable mass and abundance and a narrow mass spectrum of percent-level width. The leading constraint, from accretion, is satisfied for a population matching the bright little red dots even if all the emitted radiation escapes as hard X-rays.
items.author: Miguel Barroso Varela, Katherine Freese, Matthew Kleban et al.

items.title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming
items.summary: Hybrid architectures have become mainstream among open-weight language models. Their global-attention and bounded-state layers maintain heterogeneous caches whose demands vary with context length and concurrency. We present TideCache, a serving system on CPU--GPU superchips with three components for allocating GPU memory among caches and managing their residency across GPU and host memory. The Transparent Cache Pool redistributes physical pages among cache components behind fixed virtual addresses, preserving cache layouts and backend interfaces. The Cache Streamer uses computation intervals provided by bounded-state layers to prefetch the next global-attention layer's prefix into GPU slots shared across global-attention layers, reducing GPU residency while overlapping layer-wise transfers with computation.
items.author: Jinbin Luo, Xiaozhe Yao, Shang Yang et al.

items.title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
items.summary: Videos reveal how the world changes, but rarely the actions that cause those changes. Latent action learning recovers such supervision from visual transitions, yet often learns the underlying dynamics largely from scratch. We ask whether a pretrained video generator can instead provide the prior for both inverse and forward dynamics. We introduce O$^{2}$LaF, built on a simple principle: one prior, two dynamics. We initialize both models from the same pretrained video DiT and adapt them to their distinct roles: a feed-forward transition encoder with learnable action queries for inverse dynamics, and a causal, action-conditioned video generator for forward dynamics. By controlling information access and optimizing both dynamics end-to-end through a compact bottleneck, O$^{2}$LaF learns transferable actions from unlabeled videos.
items.author: Yuxin Jiang, Wenqiang Sun, Jiaqi Li et al.

items.title: Fractional Charge at Dislocations from Band-Inversion Cancellation
items.summary: Band inversions with opposite Chern numbers cancel in the Hall response and yield counterpropagating boundary modes that can gap out. However, a bulk probe of the topology that survives such a cancellation is lacking. We here show that dislocations in inversion-symmetric two-band crystals with cancelling band inversions bind a half-integer charge, which reveals the quantized bulk polarization of the bond-centered obstructed atomic limit realized by such crystals. To demonstrate this, we continuously deform a broad class of two-band lattice models into decoupled chains, without closing the bulk gap or breaking the inversion symmetry, where the dislocation charge follows from a count of occupied bonds.
items.author: Vladimir Juričić, Rodrigo Soto-Garrido

items.title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
items.summary: Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives. However, existing benchmarks report only episode-level success rates, which show neither how these agents succeed nor where they fail. In this paper, we present a systematic action-level analysis of frontier agents on direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks. We introduce AgentRoboCritic, an intent-grounded critique framework in which the policy agent states a local intent alongside each action, and a critic evaluates the action's outcome and failure mode against this intent. Our action-level analysis demonstrates the promising capabilities of frontier agents on direct robot control, including closed-loop recovery from local execution failures, reliable semantic grounding across diverse scenes, and strong zero-shot manipulation without task-specific adaptation.
items.author: Yiyang Du, Yuxuan Kuang, Qitao Zhao et al.

items.title: Field theory and the biquadratic spin-1 chain
items.summary: The antiferromagnetic biquadratic spin-1 chain is gapped, $SU(3)$ symmetric, and integrable. Standard arguments suggest that its low-energy physics is described by the $\mathbb{CP}^2$ nonlinear sigma model at $θ=π$. Using the Bethe ansatz, we show that its low-energy excitations can be interpreted as deconfined domain walls, just as in the sigma model. However, the lattice model is integrable, whereas the field theory is generally believed not to be. We propose a solution to this mystery by finding an integrable field theory with the same low-energy limit but which is not Lorentz invariant. The integrability-preserving scaling limit is obtained by adding a higher conserved charge and tuning the chain to criticality.
items.author: Luisa Eck, Paul Fendley

items.title: Local velocimetry for atomic superfluids: from Riemann rarefaction waves to quantized vortices
items.summary: We demonstrate local velocimetry for atomic superfluids in two dimensions (2D). Using matter-wave interferometry based on Raman--Bragg beam splitters, we map the local gradient of the phase of the superfluid's wavefunction onto displacement of the interference fringes and reconstruct the 2D velocity field. We illustrate the capabilities of this technique by applying it to two canonical problems. First, we directly observe the self-similar evolution of the velocity field in 1D Riemann rarefaction flows. Second, we map out the full 2D velocity field around quantized vortices, explicitly demonstrating the quantization of velocity circulation.
items.author: Yansheng Zhang, Yi Jiang, Feiyang Wang et al.

items.title: Bio-PM-Guided Synthetic IMU Generation
items.summary: Collecting and labeling inertial measurement unit (IMU) data for human activity recognition (HAR) is expensive, and models trained on one group of subjects often fail to generalize to unseen individuals. Even with balanced data, classifiers struggle to distinguish dynamically similar activity classes and benefit from targeted augmentation. We explore whether synthetic IMU data generated in the representation space of a pretrained biosignal encoder, Bio-PM \cite{b1}, can serve as a practical augmentation source. Rather than synthesizing raw signals, we leverage Bio-PM's frozen encoder to convert 10-second IMU windows into token embedding sequences and train class-conditional decoders in this space: (1) an autoregressive transformer decoder that predicts tokens sequentially, and (2) a diffusion decoder that learns the token distribution through a denoising objective.
items.author: Deepali Singh, Deepesh Parpani, Aviral Gupta

items.title: Query-Optimal Quantum Minimum Finding from Numerical Estimators
items.summary: We propose a quantum minimum-finding algorithm for objectives accessed via numerical estimators that avoids the logarithmic query overhead of amplifying the confidence of estimates before the search. A coherent estimator that is $\varepsilon$-accurate with probability at least $2/3$ on each of $N$ labels suffices to find a $2\varepsilon$-optimal label using $O(\sqrt N)$ base-estimator queries at constant confidence. The query bound and the additive-error constant are separately worst-case optimal. More generally, suppose a preparation assigns probability mass at least a known $p$ to objective values at most $a$. Without knowing $a$ or the prepared distribution, our algorithm returns a candidate and an estimate $v$ such that, jointly with constant probability, $v$ is $\varepsilon$-accurate for the candidate and $v\le a+\varepsilon$.
items.author: Egil Bae

items.title: Fast, in-place, and ancilla-free quantum algorithms for integer multiplication and inversion
items.summary: Arithmetic operations are a fundamental building block in the design of quantum algorithms, with their implementation cost expected to have a significant impact on the viability of a wide variety of quantum applications. In this work, we present novel algorithms for a number of in-place quantum arithmetic operations that are highly efficient in terms of their space and gate count overheads compared to the current state-of-the-art. We show that in-place modular multiplication of integers, modulo a power of two, can be performed with either a classical or quantum odd multiplier using $O(n^{1+ε})$ gates and no ancilla qubits, for any $ε>0$.
items.author: David Halpenny, Adithya Sireesh, Petros Wallden

items.title: Scalable Simulation of Strongly Correlated Fermions with Neural Gaussian Tensor Networks
items.summary: Accurate simulations of strongly correlated electrons remain a central challenge in computational physics. We introduce neural-network Gaussian projected entangled-pair states (NN-GPEPS), which exploit the locally-entangled subspace of Gaussian states to give an architecture more compatible with modern neural networks and an exact contraction cost of $O(N^{3/2})$ on two-dimensional lattices. For the Hubbard model at $U/t=8$ and $1/8$ hole doping, we obtain state-of-the-art variational energies in large lattices of up to 1024 sites. These results demonstrate an accurate approach to strongly correlated fermions by connecting neural networks with Gaussian tensor networks.
items.author: Runze Chi, Ao Chen, Garnet Kin-Lic Chan

items.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
items.summary: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. To overcome this trade-off, we train a single, scalable network that processes both images and video and predicts depth maps at native resolution. Depth Pro 2 produces depth maps that are metrically accurate, sharp, and temporally consistent all at once, outperforming prior work in all of these dimensions. We release a family of models that define a new Pareto frontier in terms of metric accuracy, sharpness, temporal consistency, and runtime.
items.author: Peiyun Hu, Marko Mihajlovic, Lyndon Duong et al.

items.title: SoK: Assessing the Evolution of LLM Capability in Software Vulnerability Research
items.summary: LLM-based agents are becoming increasingly capable at discovering, validating and patching vulnerabilities in real software, and vendors and researchers report that this is already changing how vulnerabilities are found and fixed. These claims, however, are scattered across papers, vendor reports and disclosures and are rarely comparable. We introduce a framework that rates these capabilities on an autonomy scale modeled on the levels of driving automation, and qualifies each claim by its correctness, its availability and the strength of its evidence. We use this framework to systematize the published evidence on LLM capability in vulnerability research. We find that agents discovered, validated, and patched vulnerabilities in real-world software without human intervention before the restricted frontier models of 2026, and that open-weight models subsequently attained comparable autonomy for discovery and validation.
items.author: Amine Lbath, Manan Suri, Aurelien Delaitre et al.

items.title: A Tutorial on Complementarity-Based Contact Models for Robotics
items.summary: Simulating rigid-body dynamics with contact is fundamental to robotics, from motion synthesis and control to mechanism design. Many widely used simulators rely on cone complementarity formulations, whose physical assumptions and numerical solution require substantial background. While excellent surveys, monographs, and course notes exist, they mostly address computational mechanics or computer graphics or document a single simulator. To the best of our knowledge, a self-contained pedagogical treatment for robotics, bringing these formulations and their solvers together with complete derivations and a unified notation, does not yet exist. This tutorial addresses this gap by connecting rigid-body dynamics, conic optimization, and frictional contact.
items.author: Onur Beker, A. René Geist, Michael Posa et al.

items.title: Active Feature Acquisition by Distilling an Oracle Teacher
items.summary: Acquiring every feature of an instance is often costly: a measurement can carry a monetary price, a time delay, or a privacy cost. Active Feature Acquisition (AFA) addresses this by learning a policy that decides, per instance, which features to acquire under a budget. Existing AFA methods train this policy by optimizing a self-constructed utility target rather than distilling an explicit teacher. We construct this teacher explicitly. At training time the label and the unobserved feature values are available, and together they determine the teacher in closed form: an oracle that ranks every candidate by its effect on the downstream predictor's error.
items.author: Yang Meng, Zixin Ding, Robert L. Grossman et al.

items.title: Equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for congruence subgroups of level 2
items.summary: The modular properties of holomorphic Eisenstein series for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and its congruence subgroups do not carry over to their primitives. Instead, the transformation of iterated Eisenstein integrals under congruence subgroups of level $N$ introduces inhomogeneous terms comprising (among others) cyclotomic multiple zeta values of level $N$. We combine iterated Eisenstein integrals for the congruence subgroups of level $N=2$ of arbitrary iteration depth with their complex conjugates and (single-valued) level-2 cyclotomic multiple zeta values such that they define non-holomorphic modular forms. Our construction of these so-called equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for $Γ(2)$ and $Γ_0(2)$ proceeds at the level of generating series that take values in an infinite-dimensional (pro-unipotent) Lie group and closely follow Brown's analogous construction in the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ case.
items.author: Emiel Claasen, Mehregan Doroudiani, Claude Duhr et al.

items.title: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: Robotic vision-language-action (VLA) models can execute diverse individual manipulation skills, yet they still struggle with long-horizon loco-manipulation tasks, where temporal structure, skills, and precision are tightly coupled within a monolithic model. We propose Physically Grounded Execution (PGX), a framework that offloads temporal and precision control to two classical training-free components, allowing the VLA to focus on stage-specific skill dynamics. PGX decomposes long-horizon loco-manipulation into three layers: (i) a predicate-based state machine governs task progression, using physical predicates to gate phase transitions, trigger recovery, and coordinate navigation and waiting. Shared predicate semantics connect offline demonstration segmentation, online execution, and stage-wise evaluation; (ii) VLA skills operate within active manipulation phases, with flat or stage-trained models concentrating on task-relevant actions; and (iii) world-coordinate locking (WCL) maintains spatial consistency through base station keeping, object-relative positioning, and world-anchored contact targets.
items.author: Kai Lu, Chenyang Ma, Ioannis Havoutis

items.title: UV Bounds on Inflationary Parity Violation
items.summary: A question of fundamental interest is whether parity is violated on large scales in the Universe. This possibility has been motivated by recent analyses of the four-point matter correlation function. It has also been suggested that detectable parity violation could be generated during inflation by the dynamical Chern-Simons operator, a leading effective field theory correction to general relativity. In this work, we examine this possibility in realistic UV completions, including fermionic and string-theoretic examples. We show that existing bounds on the tensor-scalar-scalar (TSS) bispectrum strongly constrain the possibility of generating a detectable parity-odd trispectrum. For tensor-to-scalar ratios near current observational limits, detectability is incompatible with, or pushes against, the regime of validity of these UV completions.
items.author: Alexander Cassem, Mark P. Hertzberg

items.title: Star-forming disc galaxies align tangentially with the cosmic tidal field
items.summary: The alignments of galaxy shapes, with one another and with the large-scale structure of the Universe, have been a topic of considerable investigation within cosmology and extragalactic astrophysics for the last 60 years. Galaxy alignments are a major systematic for weak gravitational lensing and help us learn about the processes of galaxy formation. Red early-type galaxies are known to show strong radial alignments around other galaxies; however, blue star-forming galaxies have shown little evidence of alignment. We combine SPHEREx spectrophotometry with DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys to build a full-sky catalogue of 71 million galaxies with precise redshifts. With this catalogue we are able to measure alignment signals by splitting galaxies into colour and morphological samples.
items.author: Calum Murray, Roman Paviot, Martin Kilbinger et al.

items.title: Realized versus Population Reliability: Anytime-Valid Self-Consistency Certification under Correlated Reasoning
items.summary: Self-consistency certification treats repeated sampling from a language model as sequential evidence accumulation and stops when an anytime-valid e-process crosses a threshold, guaranteeing finite-sample Type I error control by Ville's inequality. Prior constructions assume sampled rollouts are conditionally independent. We show this assumption fails in practice: reasoning streams are positively correlated through shared reasoning prefixes or across-prompt heterogeneity, changing not merely certificate efficiency but the hypothesis certified. Modeling dependence via a per-unit latent state (the random-effects / intraclass-correlation structure) induces exchangeable, equi-correlated increments with correlation $ρ$. Correlation splits the single null into a realized null about the drawn belief and a population null about average model behavior, which coincide only when $ρ=0$.
items.author: Terence D. Agbeyegbe, Toneukarin G. Agbeyegbe

items.title: Which black hole modes ring freely? Horizon regularity, the forced ringdown transient, and GW250114
items.summary: The quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a black hole are defined by keeping only ingoing waves at the horizon. We ask what horizon regularity requires of the outgoing waves this condition discards. For a scalar-like perturbation, bounded first derivatives in a frame regular at the future horizon rule out outgoing waves that decay more slowly than the surface gravity $κ$, and smoothness singles out a ladder of frequencies, $ω=mΩ_{\rm H}-ijκ$ with $j=1,2,\dots$ and $Ω_{\rm H}$ the horizon angular velocity. We call these the horizon modes. For Schwarzschild black holes and the dominant $\ell=m=2$ Kerr modes, only the fundamental QNM decays more slowly than $κ$.
items.author: Jahed Abedi, Niayesh Afshordi

items.title: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual and textual information, but their outputs do not reveal internal concept representations. Global workspace theory (GWT) proposes that information is selected from parallel brain processes, integrated in a shared workspace, and made available to specialised processes. We introduce the Multimodal Concept Lens (MC-Lens), a multimodal Jacobian lens, to study these functions in VLM concept processing. Its vision encoder and language decoder lenses map intermediate states to a shared semantic space defined by the decoder's output vocabulary to compare concept accessibility across modalities. MC-Lens supports internal concept interventions to examine the role of accessed concepts in downstream computation.
items.author: Jiahao Huang, Jun Wang

items.title: Verify the Verifier: Specification-Grounded LLM Cross-Checking for Bugs That Escape UVM Scoreboards
items.summary: A passing UVM regression shows the design agrees with the reference model on what the scoreboard checks, not that it meets the specification. Bugs that pass every test yet violate the specification, termed scoreboard escapes, survive mature testbenches. We present Verify the Verifier, to our knowledge the first framework whose LLM-based Anomaly Cross-Checker examines a passing regression's traces against the specification. Of 564 bugs inserted into four OpenTitan IPs, 68 are candidate scoreboard escapes: non-equivalent, exercised by the tests, yet passing. The framework confirmed 41 as scoreboard escapes with assertions failing on the buggy design and proven on the original.
items.author: Ana E. Sanchez Villalobos, Michael D. Quinn, Aakash Tyagi et al.

items.title: High-Accuracy Neural-Network Quantum States via Randomized Real-Time Dynamics
items.summary: Neural-network quantum states (NQSs) exhibit a disparity in converging to the ground state during energy minimization: while the energy converges quadratically with the error in the variational wave function, other observables converge only linearly, which limits the accuracy of physical predictions. Here we show how to close this gap by introducing a new algorithm that improves the accuracy of NQSs. Our method, termed dynamical averaging, estimates expectation values by averaging over a state (or observable) evolved in real-time. Using insights from quantum information, we prove an up-to-quadratic suppression of error in arbitrary ground state observables, thus matching the fast convergence of the energy.
items.author: John M. Martyn, Rod Rofougaran, Samuel Stein et al.

items.title: Relativistic Kinetic Theory of Collisionless Particles with Variable Mass and Frame Transformations
items.summary: In this work, we present the relativistic kinetic theory of a gas of collisionless point particles with non-constant mass, which can also be understood as being subject to a scalar force. Our results hold in an arbitrary conformal frame, and we explicitly derive how they transform between frames. The mathematical construction relies on a tilted Sasaki metric, whose associated phase-space geometry is adapted to particles of variable mass, as well as on the one-particle distribution function, from which macroscopic observables are derived. Finally, we show that the one-particle distribution function can always be taken to be gauge- and frame-invariant, and the corresponding generalisation of the Liouville (or collisionless Boltzmann) equation is satisfied in each frame.
items.author: Adrián Casado-Turrión, Paulo B. Ferraz, Mindaugas Karčiauskas et al.

items.title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithm for Differential Equations: Application to Simulating a Biomolecular System
items.summary: Quantum algorithms for differential equations have the potential for substantial algorithmic speedups over classical methods. However, they rely on certain assumptions and abstract oracle specifications that leave their practical feasibility and computational advantages for realistic applications unclear. Here we formalize the concept of an end-to-end quantum algorithm for differential equations as one that accepts classical inputs and returns classical outputs, and provide implementations for algorithmic primitives in constructing such algorithms. We present a tailored end-to-end quantum algorithm for the linearized Poisson-Boltzmann (LPB) equation, a partial differential equation (PDE) with variable coefficients widely used in simulating a biomolecular system. We explicitly implement all aspects of the algorithm, from preparing an initial state to generating a quantum solution and estimating properties of the system.
items.author: Mohsen Bagherimehrab, Daniyaal Farooqi, Gavin K. Brennen et al.

items.title: Classically Trained Quantum Generative Models with Shared Training and Fine Tuning for Quantum Matter
items.summary: Ground-state measurement statistics characterize quantum matter. Selected correlations can guide the classical training of a quantum sampler even when sampling the full distribution is difficult. We ask whether training across related ground-state distributions helps the sampler reproduce their correlations more accurately. We train a hypernetwork to map Hamiltonian parameters to circuit angles, sharing information across the phase diagram before local fine-tuning with additional reference data for quantum deployment. For classical training, we derive an unbiased Monte Carlo estimator of Fourier coefficients for circuits built from general Pauli rotations, with a cost that depends on the circuit generators. We also introduce a CDF-KL loss for comparing selected marginals.
items.author: Mario Herrero-Gonzalez, Elham Kashefi, Mina Doosti

items.title: PhyDEX: A Benchmark for Physical Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models via Dynamic Extrinsic Dexterity
items.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have advanced rapidly in language-conditioned robotic manipulation, yet existing benchmarks mainly evaluate gripper--object contact and largely ignore how objects interact with the environment through gravity, friction, inertia, and mass distribution. As a result, it remains unclear whether current policies truly understand physics or merely interpolate from their training data. We address this gap through the lens of dynamic extrinsic dexterity and introduce PhyDEX, a throwing benchmark in which a robot must infer an object's mass, center of mass, and friction to send it to a destination beyond its kinematic workspace. PhyDEX contains 35K trajectories (143 hours) across nine tasks and 100 scenes, covering uniform, irregular, and dynamic-mass objects with static, multiple, and moving destinations.
items.author: Hao Vo, Taisei Hanyu, Yuki Ikebe et al.

items.title: Twisting Spinning Particles with Superghost Backgrounds
items.summary: We construct twists of spinning particles in the classical BV formalism by giving constant backgrounds to the bosonic ghosts of local worldline supersymmetry, in analogy with Costello and Li's twist of supergravity, which gives a nonzero background to the ghost of local spacetime supersymmetry. We represent the superghosts on polynomial states and gauge selected worldline R symmetries, imposing the shifted R constraints absolutely and the unshifted ones relatively. On flat targets, the N=2 particle, its N=4 extension on a complex target and an N=8 particle with two fermion flavors give the de Rham, Dolbeault and polynomial linear BCOV complexes. The last two are the linearized field content of the open and closed B-model target-space theories.
items.author: Erik Fink, Jingqian Gou, Niklas Holbach et al.

items.title: Refractive Neutrino Mass: Effects of Fluctuations of the Dark Matter Field
items.summary: Observed neutrino oscillations can be reproduced by a refractive neutrino mass-squared arising from interactions with ultralight scalar dark matter (ULDM). The wave behaviour of the scalar field gives rise to a fluctuating interference pattern, inducing spatial and temporal variations in the refractive mass that can distort neutrino oscillation probabilities. We simulate the interference patterns of the scalar field in the presence of self-interactions. Using results of these simulations, the oscillation probabilities for JUNO and T2K experiments are computed. We find that the refractive mass scenario remains viable for the complex scalar field without self-coupling for $m_φ\lesssim 10^{-16}~\mathrm{eV}$. For $m_φ\gtrsim10^{-16}~\mathrm{eV}$, repulsive self-interactions narrow the density distribution, reducing the deviation of the survival probability at the first minimum to $ΔP \approx 0.07$ for an appropriate self-interaction coupling.
items.author: Soham Sahasrabuddhe, Manibrata Sen, Alexei Y. Smirnov

items.title: Self-gravity depletes superradiant clouds
items.summary: Superradiant clouds of ultralight scalars around black holes are often modeled as free fields, whose levels grow independently and decay slowly through gravitational-wave emission. We show that this limit is never realized. The cloud's self-gravity redistributes particles between levels, just as in the case of axion self-interactions, and dominates over self-interactions for decay constants $f_a\gtrsim6\times10^{16}\,{\rm GeV}\,(α/0.1)$, with $α$ the gravitational fine-structure constant. Self-gravity depletes the cloud by orders of magnitude and feeds more extended levels, weakening all signals that rely on the existence of a large cloud mass. A binary companion, however, can partly offset the depletion. Any assessment of superradiant signals must therefore account for both self-gravity and the cloud's environment.
items.author: Mateja Bošković, Lucas Gathercole, Thomas F. M. Spieksma et al.

items.title: Emergent Fatigue Dynamics from Foundational Interatomic Potentials
items.summary: Foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials are trained on large, diverse DFT datasets, but their validation rests on equilibrium states, which does not guarantee correct emergent behavior in large-scale molecular dynamics. Where no direct experimental validation is available, comparisons to physically motivated potentials are valuable for drawing insight. We distinguish static properties, which are thermally accessible, from emergent properties, which require work from an external fatigue stress to drive rare events, and compare the potentials on both. An EAM potential and the NequIP foundational potential both agree closely with reference data for many near-equilibrium properties, but NequIP predicts an anomalously low intrinsic stacking fault energy ($\sim7$ times lower than EAM) and thus predicts far more plastic deformation under fatigue cycling of a nanoscale flaw modeled after the classical Griffith crack problem.
items.author: Jingye Tan, Benjamin A. Jasperson, Eric Rothchild et al.

items.title: From power to spectrum: an off-the-shelf photodiode turned into a spectrometer by its bias alone
items.summary: Computational spectrometers replace dispersive optics with detectors whose spectral response can be varied, but every reported single-detector device obtains this response through dedicated fabrication: two-dimensional heterostructures, graded epitaxial junctions, organic stacks, filters or photonic circuits. We demonstrate a generic, fabrication-free alternative in which a standard commercial photodiode becomes a spectrometer through its electrical drive alone, requiring no modification of the device, no optical filter and no modulation of the light. The mechanism is bias-modulated optoelectronic chromatic dispersion (OED): light of different wavelengths is absorbed at different depths, and a sinusoidal bias changes how carriers generated at each depth are collected, so that every spectrum is encoded in the shape of the photocurrent waveform over one bias period.
items.author: Roi Yozevitch, Shmuel Sternklar, Ziv Glasser

items.title: Full Kummer Beams: Skyrmionic textures in bichromatic light
items.summary: In this work, we introduce full Kummer beams, the bichromatic analog of full Poincaré beams. To this end, we define three parameters that characterize bichromatic states of polarization and span the Kummer shape, the bichromatic counterpart of the Poincaré sphere. We find that, under certain conditions, full Kummer beams can exhibit skyrmionic textures with a Skyrme number that depends not only on the topological charges but also on the frequencies. These beams can also exhibit emergent behavior upon propagation, including robust, higher-order-like structures and a propagation-invariant Skyrme number over a wide range of beam-waist selections.
items.author: Jefferson Delgado-Quesada, Miguel A. Alonso, Eileen Otte

items.title: Constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Finite Element Model Updating: Closed-Form Hyperelastic Strain Energies from Heterogeneous Experiments
items.summary: Calibrating a hyperelastic constitutive model for a soft material traditionally poses two problems: an expert must choose its functional form, and several homogeneous tests must determine its parameters. Neural constitutive models solve the first, but either remain black boxes or draw on a library of candidate terms fixed in advance. Full-field measurements, such as those from digital image correlation (DIC), promise to solve the second, replacing those tests by a single heterogeneous one. Two gaps remain: flexibility during training with interpretability afterwards, and a way to train such a model on one heterogeneous test. Here we close both. We embed a constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold network (CKAN) in finite element model updating (FEMU) and train it by minimizing the mismatch between the predicted and the measured kinematic fields and reaction forces.
items.author: Kian P. Abdolazizi, Kevin Linka, Christian J. Cyron

items.title: M 5.1 - 99 km WSW of Illapel, Chile
items.summary: A magnitude 5.1 earthquake was recorded 99 km WSW of Illapel, Chile. The event happened on 19 November 2026 at 18:09 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 10 km. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data. The agency event page has the map, updates and safety information.
items.author: USGS

items.title: Tropical Cyclone Akvan
items.summary: NASA's Earth Observatory Natural Event Tracker lists an open event in the category severe storms. The tracker collects reports from official agencies and updates them as an event develops. Open the source page for the latest details and maps.
items.author: NASA EONET

items.title: $Zγ$ production in gluon fusion at NLO+NLL
items.summary: We study the production of $Zγ$ in gluon fusion at hadron colliders at the next-to-leading-order (NLO) in QCD. At the $13.6$ TeV LHC, we find that these NLO corrections are found to enhance the leading-order (LO) cross section by about $83$\% and reduce the conventional seven-point scale uncertainty from $22.3$\% at LO to $15.2$\% at NLO. We further perform the threshold resummation at next-to-leading-logarithmic (NLL) accuracy and match to the fixed order NLO results. We have presented the production cross section for various center of mass energies at the LHC. We find that this NLL resummation enhances the NLO production cross section by about $23$\%.
items.author: Chinmoy Dey, Niraj Koirala, M. C. Kumar et al.

items.title: ACE-Brain-0.7: Learning Execution-Grounded Reasoning for Embodied Agents
items.summary: Reliable reasoning for long-horizon embodied tasks requires predictions grounded in the observed execution state. We present ACE-Brain-0.7, a 9B vision--language model that combines spatial grounding, task understanding, and progress estimation. To train the model, we curate 3.7 million question--answer pairs, drawing execution supervision from egocentric human videos, robot episodes, and simulation. These questions span different stages of an execution and connect task-level judgments with observed progress and outcomes. We then fine-tune Qwen3.5-9B on this collection together with additional task, spatial-grounding, and progress-estimation data. Across six public task-reasoning benchmarks, ACE-Brain-0.7 achieves an average score of 76.5, ahead of GPT-6 Astra at 72.7 and Claude Opus 5.5 at 73.5.
items.author: Yinhe Wang, Shijun Shi, Feng Pan et al.

items.title: JARVIS: An Agent That Designs, Builds, and Tests Circuit Boards on Its Own
items.summary: Power electronics is central to the energy transition, but developing new hardware still relies on human-led design, fabrication, testing, and iteration. We present JARVIS, an embodied AI agent that autonomously closes this loop for circuit boards. JARVIS maintains machine-specific capabilities and constraints, scans its workspace using a robot-mounted 3D scanner, and constructs an executable digital twin in which it rehearses robot motions, fabrication steps, and circuit behavior before consuming materials. A single text instruction initiates the physical experiment. Using unmodified desktop equipment, the agent coordinates a robot arm, a PCB printer that deposits conductive silver ink and solder paste, and a pick-and-place machine.
items.author: Shibo Zhou, Tianqi Hong, Zheng Yan et al.

items.title: Inhomogeneous Cutoff Regularization of Loops in Cosmological Correlators
items.summary: We revisit the use of cutoff regularization in computing loop corrections to cosmological correlators. We argue that a cutoff corresponding to a fixed physical scale must be defined with respect to the local background geometry. In the presence of superhorizon perturbations, this is naturally implemented within the separate universe picture, where different local patches are regulated at the same physical scale. Expanding this cutoff in the long-wavelength background generates a series of regulator-induced contributions to loop amplitudes, which admit a diagrammatic interpretation as long-mode insertions on the corresponding loop contractions. Our cutoff prescription preserves residual spatial dilatations and volume-preserving anisotropic rescalings.
items.author: Jacopo Fumagalli, Keisuke Inomata

items.title: An Open-Source ROS 2 Framework for Shared Control in Surgical Teleoperation: Integrating the Haply Inverse3 with the da Vinci Research Kit
items.summary: Surgical teleoperation deprives surgeons of touch, forcing visual inference of tissue forces; the commercial platforms now restoring force feedback remain closed, preventing open research on haptic shared control. This paper provides a system contribution: it presents an open-source, ROS 2-native framework that integrates the compact, three-degree-of-freedom (3-DOF) Haply Inverse3 haptic device with the da~Vinci Research Kit (dVRK). The framework includes a novel mapping strategy that combines 3-DOF translational device input with separately tracked VerseGrip orientation into 6-DOF patient-side manipulator commands. Two virtual-fixture-inspired guidance modes serve as reference implementations to evaluate the framework in a within-subjects user study on a teleoperated hot-wire benchmark task in simulation, and the architecture is further demonstrated on physical dVRK hardware.
items.author: Balint Varga, Sebastian Fritz, Gergely Kiss et al.

items.title: Two distinct notions of speed in antiferromagnets
items.summary: The terahertz resonance frequencies of antiferromagnets characterize their precessional dynamics but do not necessarily imply faster laser-induced quenching of magnetic order. Here, we investigate the distinct roles of magnetic compensation and electronic scattering phase space by comparing ultrafast demagnetization in the antiferromagnetic charge-transfer insulator NiO, the metallic antiferromagnet Mn2Au, and a ferromagnetic Ni reference. The extracted response in Mn2Au is approximately four times faster than in NiO and substantially faster than in Ni. These observations are consistent with exchange-mediated scattering between antiparallel sublattices enabling rapid loss of antiferromagnetic order without requiring net angular-momentum transfer to an external reservoir, provided sufficient electronic scattering phase space is available.
items.author: Paul Herrgen, Stephan Wust, Christin Schmitt et al.

items.title: Review of Pion and Nucleon Gluon Parton Distribution Functions from Lattice QCD
items.summary: Gluons play an essential role in the strong interaction that binds quarks into hadrons, as described by quantum chromodynamics (QCD). Understanding how the fundamental dynamics of QCD give rise to hadron structure remains one of the outstanding challenges in nuclear and particle physics. Parton distribution functions (PDFs) provide a successful framework for describing high-energy scattering processes involving hadrons. However, our knowledge of gluon PDFs remains comparatively limited because of the experimental challenges associated with directly constraining the gluon structure of hadrons. In recent years, a major breakthrough has enabled the calculation of the Bjorken-$x$ dependence of PDFs directly from lattice QCD.
items.author: William Good, Huey-Wen Lin

items.title: Future avenues for precision oscillation measurements with compact movable reactors
items.summary: No planned neutrino experiment is expected to surpass Daya Bay's precision on $\thone$. Doing so requires innovative strategies to reduce statistical and systematic uncertainties. In this study, we consider a futuristic program with a movable reactor antineutrino source placed within short distances ($L\lesssim 3\,\km$) from the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) detector. Due to the large fiducial mass of JUNO, even a relatively small reactor can produce a statistically significant number of events over a few years to probe the $\lesssim 8.7\% \,\nuebar$ disappearance set by $\thone$. We consider two possibilities: a $\mathcal{O}(20\mwth)$ microreactor in alcoves of the access tunnel to the underground laboratory, and a $\mathcal{O}(400 \mwth)$ unit on the surface.
items.author: Matheus Hostert, Stephan A. Meighen-Berger, Maxim Pospelov

items.title: Simulation-pretrained autoencoders versus PCA for compressing multimode fibre transmission matrices
items.summary: Multimode optical fibres can image through a thin, flexible probe once their transmission matrix (TM) has been measured, but a TM is large and must be re-measured whenever the fibre moves. A compact model of feasible TMs would make storing and re-estimating them cheaper, so we ask how compactly TMs can be represented, and from how few measured TMs. Here we benchmark a permutation-equivariant autoencoder, pretrained on simulated fibres and adapted to measured TMs, against principal component analysis (PCA). At 62x compression, adapting the pretrained autoencoder with just two measured TMs reconstructs the TM of a 50um fibre well enough to focus light at 98% of the ideal enhancement, and it stays accurate when the TMs are shifted by 25 pixels or zoomed by 10%, which quickly degrades a linear basis.
items.author: Callum J. Wilson, Terry Wright, Qing Yang et al.

items.title: A photon-number-conserving multimode framework for pulse propagation dynamics across zero nonlinearity: Kerr-Raman cooperation and competition
items.summary: Raman scattering in multimode fibers shifts pulse spectra to lower frequencies and transfers photons between spatial modes. When the nonlinear coefficient changes sign within the pulse spectrum, the ordinary generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE) can give unphysical predictions. Existing photon-number-conserving formulations either treat a single mode or exclude Raman scattering. We develop a time-domain multimode GNLSE that conserves photon number, includes the full Raman response and remains well defined at the zero-nonlinearity frequency. For narrowband pulses with a constant positive nonlinear coefficient, the framework reduces to the standard multimode GNLSE with instantaneous Kerr and delayed Raman terms. We then apply the framework to three coherently excited modes whose spectra shift across the zero-nonlinearity frequency.
items.author: Chao Mei, Weiye Huang, Junhong Yang et al.

items.title: High-Power Short-Wavelength Frequency Comb from Coherent Radiation of Uncompressed Electron Beams
items.summary: High-power frequency combs at short wavelengths would open new opportunities for precision measurements and high-resolution spectroscopy. Here, we propose a frequency comb based on coherent undulator radiation from uncompressed electron bunches. An optical frequency comb serves as the seed, establishing a common phase reference for microbunching in successive electron bunches and transferring its phase coherence to short-wavelength harmonic radiation. By exploiting interference between distinct laser-induced microbunching pathways, we reduce the sensitivity of the harmonic bunching phase to electron-beam energy fluctuations, a major challenge for maintaining interpulse coherence. Start-to-end simulations demonstrate frequency comb generation in the vacuum-ultraviolet (148 nm) and soft X-ray regimes, yielding average radiation powers of approximately 1 W and 100 mW, respectively, with approximately 6 $μ$W and 100 nW concentrated in individual comb teeth.
items.author: Chenzhi Xu, Bingyang Yan, Hanxiang Yang et al.

items.title: Perfumer: A Large Language Model-based Agentic Framework Accelerating Structural Relaxation and Electronic Band Prediction for First-Principle Calculation
items.summary: First-principles structural relaxation and band calculations require substantial computation and expertise. Here we present Perfumer, a large language model-based agentic framework that couples Quantum ESPRESSO with two predictive models. Across tested structures, pre-relaxation with Perfumer-relax model followed by QE refinement yielded a 2.75-fold overall speedup over QE alone. Perfumer-band model combines a periodic graph neural network with a latent Hermitian spectral head returns 12 band energies at any requested wavevector, preserving reciprocal lattice periodicity and time-reversal symmetry without constructing Hamiltonian. Trained on 125,153 self-curated band structures, Perfumer-band model reaches a median per-material mean absolute error of 0.157 eV on 2,607 test materials, including lanthanide, actinide and magnetic compounds, from held-out composition families spanning 85 elements, taking about 97 ms per material on two consumer CPU cores.
items.author: Zhiwei Li, Yuhao Zhou, Yikai Yang et al.

items.title: Hybrid Plasmon-Phonon Eigenmodes and Vortex States in a Graphene Ring on a Silica Substrate
items.summary: We investigate hybrid plasmon-phonon eigenmodes and localized electromagnetic vortex states in a graphene ring supported by a dispersive silica substrate. The interaction between graphene plasmons and infrared-active optical phonons of the substrate gives rise to distinct spectral branches of surface polaritons, whose dispersion characteristics are established analytically and validated by full-wave numerical simulations. Geometric confinement of these hybrid surface excitations produces spectrally separated families of localized multipolar eigenmodes with corresponding azimuthal symmetries. Particular attention is devoted to quadrupolar eigenstates, which exhibit nearly identical normalized spatial field distributions despite their substantial spectral separation and different attenuation characteristics. We demonstrate that coherent superposition of orthogonal quadrupolar field patterns gives rise to localized vortex states with opposite azimuthal phase winding.
items.author: Yanxu Guo, Oleh Demianyk, Vladimir R. Tuz

items.title: NASA Science Data Powers New Method to Discover Hard-to-Find Pulsars
items.summary: Open data from NASA’s Fermi mission helped an international team of scientists develop a method for finding pulsars about a million times faster than before.

items.title: Lake Pelku
items.summary: An astronaut on the International Space Station captured this photograph of Lake Pelku (near center) as the station orbited above Asia. The International Space Station serves as a unique platform for observing Earth with both hands-on and automated equipment. Station crew members have produced hundreds of thousands of images. These images record phenomena in real […]
items.author: HQ Web Team

items.title: Efficient calculation of the full Laguerre-Gaussian spectrum of entangled biphotons
items.summary: The spatial biphoton state generated by spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) enables applications in high-dimensional quantum information processing and is often described in Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) modes. However, calculating the full LG spectrum for arbitrary radial and orbital angular momentum (OAM) indices requires computationally demanding multidimensional integrations. We present a generating-function approach that analytically performs the four-dimensional transverse spatial integral without approximating the phase-matching function. The source geometry can be completely described by a few dimensionless parameters, which reduce to two parameters for wave-vector-degenerate photons with equal waists. Our derived expressions for the full LG spectrum allow for computationally efficient and numerically stable evaluation at high mode orders, addressing a crucial obstacle in previous works.
items.author: Jiabao Peng, Richard Bernecker, Stephan Fritzsche

items.title: Unusual increase in electrical and thermal conductivity of severely deformed CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy: Roles of disordering and nanostructuring in electron and phonon transport
items.summary: This work investigates how defect engineering and nanostructuring via severe plastic deformation influence electrical and thermal transport in the high-entropy alloy CrMnFeCoNi. High-pressure torsion (HPT) for up to N = 4 turns produces a hierarchical defect structure, including deformation twins at low strains, dislocations and Lomer-Cottrell locks at intermediate strains, and a high fraction of high-angle grain boundaries at large strains. While hardness naturally increases and saturates at ~520 Hv, both electrical and thermal conductivity exhibit an unusual increase upon HPT processing (from 0.953 MS m-1 and 10.3 W m-1 K-1 after homogenization to 1.003 +- 0.005 MS m-1 and 14.4 W m-1 K-1 after N = 4).
items.author: Jacqueline Hidalgo-Jiménez, Payam Edalati, Md Amirul Islam et al.

items.title: NASA Conducts Latest RS-25 Engine Test in Support of Future Artemis Missions
items.summary: NASA tested RS-25 engine No. 10001 on Nov. 18 on the Fred Haise Test Stand at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi. Test teams fired the developmental engine for the planned duration of three minutes and 20 seconds (200 seconds). While this developmental engine will not be used in flight, the hot […]
items.author: LaToya Dean

items.title: Reward misalignment as an opportunity for materials discovery
items.summary: Reward misalignment is usually regarded as a failure of artificial intelligence. In materials discovery with generative AI models, however, disagreement between predefined rewards and expert judgment may reveal materials that the rewards overlook. We investigate this possibility using electronic flat bands as a prime example. Experts mostly agree with a numerical bandwidth score, but their disagreements are systematic and cannot be explained by an estimated 5% rate of mistaken labels. We learn the experts' preferences from pairwise comparisons and use them to guide a crystal diffusion model. The learned preferences and numerical score agree on the flattest bands but diverge elsewhere.
items.author: Ryotaro Okabe, Shoki Kishida, Abhijatmedhi Chotrattanapituk et al.

items.title: DUV (257 nm) LIDT of Anti-Reflective Coatings
items.summary: Laser-induced damage threshold in the deep ultraviolet (DUV) was used to perform tests on AR coated windows intended for industrial processes. The 257 nm wavelength was generated from Yb:YAG fundamental (1030 nm) and the long-term LIDT stability (up to 100000 shots) was selected as representative for minimal industrial qualification. Selected setup for the fourth harmonics generation consists of two stages, generation of second harmonic and subsequently the fourth harmonic with 13,4% conversation efficiency. In both 1-on-1 and S-on-1 experiments, the optics coated with Al2O3/SiO2 by ion beam sputtering technique demonstrated the highest LIDT value of 0.73 and 0.5 J/cm2 respectively.
items.author: Martin Mydlar, Hana Turcicova, Priyadarshani Narayanasamy et al.

items.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 Makes History Reaching One Light-Day From Earth
items.summary: NASA’s Voyager 1 probe, humanity’s farthest-flying spacecraft, has reached one light-day from Earth, after more than 49 years of constant travel. A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours, equaling about 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). The spacecraft achieved the milestone at 2:16 a.m. PST (5:16 a.m. EST) Nov. 18. Voyager team […]
items.author: Jessica Taveau

items.title: Sliding-ferroelectric control of dipolar and quadrupolar excitons in R-stacked WSe$_2$
items.summary: A fundamental property of interlayer excitons is their dipolar character, enabling electrical tunability, enhanced exciton-exciton interactions and extended lifetime. It is important for studying collective phenomena and realizing novel optoelectronic devices. However, in homo- or heterostructures based on two-dimensional semiconductors, the magnitude and orientation of the dipole moment are commonly locked due to spatially confined charges and nature of the band transition. Here, we use gate-dependent photoluminescence of few-layer R-WSe2 to harness sliding ferroelectricity for controlling the exciton dipole configuration of emerging layer-hybridised excitons. The sliding-ferroelectric control enables a pronounced on/off switching of the diffusive transport of hybrid dipolar excitons, while further facilitating gradual and abrupt dipole reconfigurations with emerging quadrupolar excitons.
items.author: Asmund Ottesen, Shun Feng, Edoardo Lopriore et al.

items.title: GEI-17-mediated SUMOylation of GDP dissociation inhibitor GDI-1 regulates apoptotic cell clearance
items.summary: by Lei Yuan, Peiyao Li, Aiying Ma, Chao Li, Fuqiao Liu, Yunmin Xie, Qian Zheng, Hui Wang, Hui Xiao Apoptotic cell clearance represents the final stage of apoptosis and involves phagosome formation, maturation, and digestion. Here, we found that SUMO modifications participate in apoptotic cell clearance by influencing phagosomal degradation activity in C. elegans . The SUMO E3 ligase, GEI-17, SUMOylates GDP dissociation inhibitor (GDI-1) at K270 to trigger phagosomal degradation. Upon SUMOylation, GDI-1 facilitates release of GDP-bound RAB-1, which is subsequently converted to the GTP-bound form in a manner dependent on GDI displacement factor, PRAF-3. RAB-1 conversion enables binding and translocation of RAB-7 from the endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi to promote phagosome maturation and degradation activity.
items.author: Lei Yuan, Peiyao Li, Aiying Ma et al.

items.title: Altitude-induced hypoxia suppresses Varroa mite reproduction in Tibetan honey bees
items.summary: by Ruike Wei, Shangning Yang, Xinlan Chen, Yicheng Lu, Yao Liu, Fuliang Hu, Stephen J. Martin, Luo Zha, Huoqing Zheng Our reliance on honey bees ( Apis mellifera ) for pollination services and honey production continues to increase due to the global decline in other pollinators and rising demand for honey. The ectoparasitic mite ( Varroa destructor ) remains the biggest pest of honey bees forcing beekeepers into continual miticide use. Beekeepers on the Tibetan Plateau, however, report rarely seeing mites in their colonies, unlike all other areas of China. We conducted a series of translocation experiments to investigate this phenomenon.
items.author: Ruike Wei, Shangning Yang, Xinlan Chen et al.

items.title: Local feedback governs cell fate transition to drive self-organized phenotypic equilibrium in hierarchical tumors
items.summary: by Emma Legait, Charlotte Rulquin, Lauranne Bouteille, Raphaël Clément, Cédric Maurange How cell-state transitions are regulated along a tumor lineage to determine its overall cellular composition remains unclear. Using a simple hierarchical tumor model in Drosophila , we show that differentiation of cancer stem cells (CSCs) into transit amplifying progenitors (TAPs) depends on the fraction of TAPs among their immediate neighbors. This relationship is captured by a local feedback transition rule that quantitatively predicts CSC transition probability. Implementing this rule in 3D growth simulations spontaneously recapitulates CSC clustering and the emergence of a stable CSC fraction within tumors. Mechanistically, the local feedback is mediated by EGFR signaling from newly produced TAPs, propagating differentiation across CSC clusters.
items.author: Emma Legait, Charlotte Rulquin, Lauranne Bouteille et al.

items.title: AlphaInterp: Revealing how AlphaFold 3 processes structure, confidence, and evolutionary information
items.summary: by Jonathan Feldman, Jeffrey Skolnick How does evolutionary information become structural knowledge? AlphaFold 3 predicts protein structures and biomolecular assemblies with remarkable accuracy, yet how it transforms comparative sequence information into three-dimensional structure remains poorly understood. Here, we use mechanistic interpretability to follow this transformation through AlphaFold 3 and identify a computational principle underlying its structural inference. By extracting single- and pair-representations across the model’s forward pass and combining representational-geometry analysis, linear probing, activation patching, and perturbation of the multiple-sequence alignment (MSA) and its phylogenetic diversity, we show that AlphaFold 3 does not simply infer structure from raw sequence nor from MSA depth.
items.author: Jonathan Feldman, Jeffrey Skolnick

items.title: Gray bats heighten their response to social cues when navigating group flight in environments with obstacles
items.summary: by Eighdi Aung, Nicole Abaid Bats are fast fliers with great maneuverability. Many species sense and communicate through echolocation, relying on acoustic signals in the environment. Bats also form large colonies, which necessitates that they fly in groups. When group size increases or obstacles are in their flight paths, the acoustic space can become cluttered, posing a non-trivial challenge for navigation. How do they interact with their environment and conspecifics, and how do they balance social and environmental cues? Recent research has uncovered individual adaptations to calling and flight patterns when flying in the groups or avoiding obstacles. Studies also suggest coordination when foraging, as well as strategies used by the group to mitigate acoustic clutter.
items.author: Eighdi Aung, Nicole Abaid

items.title: Müllerian duct maintenance is promoted by GATA2: Evidence from genetic mouse studies and two human cases of Müllerian duct agenesis
items.summary: by Shuai Jia, Margaret Woodward, Allyssa Fogarty, Jessica King, Janine R. Daub, Mary L. Fairbanks, Audrey M. Neale, Wenyan Bai, Emery H. Bresnick, Steven M. Holland, Veronica Gomez-Lobo, Fei Zhao The paradigm of sexual differentiation holds that female embryos retain the Müllerian ducts, the precursor of the female reproductive tract, by default in the absence of anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH). However, whether Müllerian duct maintenance requires active signaling remains unknown. Here, using mouse genetic models, we discover that deletion of mesenchymal Gata2 causes selective regression of the cranial Müllerian duct, the precursor of the oviduct. This regression is not driven by ectopic AMH signaling but may instead result from the loss of region-specific NRG1 signaling.
items.author: Shuai Jia, Margaret Woodward, Allyssa Fogarty et al.

items.title: GPCR-Gαq signaling drives adaptive resistance to MEK inhibition in BRAF-mutant melanoma
items.summary: by Jingyi Ke, Zi Wang, Zhengyang Guo, Guangshuo Ou, Wei Li Oncogenic BRAFV600E mutations drive constitutive MAPK signaling across various cancers; however, resistance to MEK inhibitors such as trametinib undermines clinical benefits, and the mechanisms sustaining MAPK activity under treatment remain unclear. We developed a lin-45(V627E) Caenorhabditis elegans model to mimic oncogenic BRAF signaling and found that these animals exhibited high-dose trametinib resistance, as assessed by brood size. Transcriptomic analysis revealed increased egl-30 expression in worms resistant to high-dose trametinib. Genetic and pharmacological analyses implicated EGL-30/Gαq-PLC-PKC signaling in this high-dose resistance phenotype. In trametinib-resistant A375 melanoma cells, F2RL1 , which encodes the Gαq-coupled GPCR PAR2, was upregulated compared with parental cells.
items.author: Jingyi Ke, Zi Wang, Zhengyang Guo et al.

items.title: Genotype-phenotype investigation of evolving mutations associated with antimalarial resistance among Senegalese Plasmodium falciparum malaria parasites
items.summary: by Katelyn Vendrely Brenneman, Wesley Wong, Yaye Die Ndiaye, Jonathan T. Smith, Stephen Schaffner, Bassirou Ngom, Karina L. Bellavia, Imran Ullah, Amy Gaye, Djiby Sow, Mame Fama Ndiaye, Mariama Toure, Nogaye Gadiaga, Aita Sene, Awa Bineta Deme, Baba Dieye, Mamadou Samb Yade, Khadim Diongue, Younouss Diedhiou, Jules François Gomis, Mouhamadou Ndiaye, Mamadou Alpha Diallo, Ibrahima Mbaye Ndiaye, Bronwyn MacInnis, Dyann F. Wirth, Daouda Ndiaye, Sarah K. Volkman Drug resistance in Plasmodium falciparum threatens malaria control and elimination efforts, particularly where sustained chemoprevention and treatment have driven parasite evolution. Senegal has implemented antimalarial strategies for two decades, including sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) for intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy and SP plus amodiaquine for seasonal malaria chemoprevention in children.
items.author: Katelyn Vendrely Brenneman, Wesley Wong, Yaye Die Ndiaye et al.

items.title: A single amino acid switch in PilO controls planktonic-sessile lifestyle in Helicobacter pylori
items.summary: by Xiaolin Liu, Jiunn C. N. Fong, Eric H. L. Huang, Karen M. Ottemann Helicobacter pylori and related Campylobacterota assemble high torque motors with many additional proteins compared to model bacteria. Despite these structural enhancements, some wild-type H. pylori strains have been previously reported to have delayed migration in the semisolid agar motility assay. The basis for this delay was characterized by identifying genetic suppressors that allowed H. pylori G27 wild type to migrate immediately. This analysis identified loss of function mutations in four genes ( pilO , fliL , hcpX , and alpA ) that restored migration. Targeted loss of any one of these genes resulted in strains that both migrated immediately in semisolid agar and displayed low early biofilm formation.
items.author: Xiaolin Liu, Jiunn C. N. Fong, Eric H. L. Huang et al.

items.title: Correction: African swine fever virus pB318L suppresses inflammatory response by inhibiting NF-κB activation and NLRP3 inflammasome formation
items.summary: by Xiaohong Liu, Guangqiang Ye, Yi Zeng, Hanyu Wu, Siqi Dong, Xiaoping He, Qiongqiong Zhou, Hongyang Liu, Zhaoxia Zhang, Jiangnan Li, Changjiang Weng, Li Huang
items.author: Xiaohong Liu, Guangqiang Ye, Yi Zeng et al.

items.title: Deltacoronavirus modulates circRNA circC3 biogenesis to accelerate MBNL1 mRNA decay
items.summary: by Liuyang Du, Liping Wang, Lei Zhao, Juan Li, Yan Yan, Xiran Peng, Weiren Dong, Wei Wu, Jiyong Zhou, Jinyan Gu Circular RNAs (circRNAs) with diverse biological functions are frequently dysregulated upon viral infection, yet the mechanisms governing their differential expression and functional relevance during infection remain poorly defined. Here, we identify a previously uncharacterized circRNA, circC3 , that is robustly upregulated following virus infection. Host RNA binding protein muscleblind-like 1 (MBNL1) was markedly induced by deltacoronavirus (δ-CoV) infection, which recognizes YGCY motifs within intron 19 and intron 21 of the C3 gene and promotes skipping of exons 20 and 21 for C3 gene, thereby enhancing circC3 biogenesis.
items.author: Liuyang Du, Liping Wang, Lei Zhao et al.

items.title: N6-methyladenosine dependent glycolysis enhances viral infection by histone lactylation in an arthropod
items.summary: by Xumei Sun, Fan Xin, Siyuan Zhang The glycolysis is crucial for the material and energy source of virus infection. However, the role of post-transcriptional modification, particularly N6-methyladenosine (m6A), in regulating virus-induced glycolysis in invertebrate remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that METTL3-mediated m6A modification of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) mRNA increased in shrimp upon white spot syndrome virus (WSSV) infection to promote glycolysis. An m6A site in the LDH mRNA is recognized by the m6A reader YTH domain family protein 3 (YTHDF3), which recruits translation initiation factor core subunit eIF4A to enhance LDH translation elongation and mRNA stability. LDH-derived lactate acts as a key metabolite responsible for lactylation of histone lysine residues that stimulates methyltransferase-like 3 ( mettl3 ) gene transcription from chromatin directly.
items.author: Xumei Sun, Fan Xin, Siyuan Zhang

items.title: Low HLA-A expression linked to NK cell phenotype and functionality is associated with low total HIV-1 DNA and cure/remission in very early art-treated children
items.summary: by Nicholas G. Herbert, Gabriela Cromhout, Nomonde Bengu, Giuseppe Rubens Pascucci, Rowena Fillis, Samantha Kannie, Jeroen van Lobenstein, Kogielambal Chinniah, Roopesh Bhoola, Malini Krishna, Noxolo Mchunu, Maria C. Puertas, Maria C. Garcia-Guerrero, Dimitra Peppa, Wilfredo Garcia-Beltran, Andreas Groll, Nicola Cotugno, Donato Amodio, Paolo Palma, Mary Carrington, Thumbi Ndung’u, Javier Martinez-Picado, Veron Ramsuran, Philip J. R. Goulder Natural killer (NK) cells play a central role in immune control of HIV-1 in ART-naïve children and also in post-treatment control in adults living with HIV-1. To evaluate the role of NK cell activity in post-treatment control in very early-ART-treated children, we here studied a cohort of 274 children from KwaZulu-Natal followed from birth after vertical transmission.
items.author: Nicholas G. Herbert, Gabriela Cromhout, Nomonde Bengu et al.

items.title: Handheld Raman spectroscopy for ex vivo molecular assessment of cervical lesions: A methodological feasibility study
items.summary: by Yixuan Zhang, Huan Wang, Ying He, Siyuan Zhang, Pengyu Wang, Yimin Han Current diagnostic workflows for cervical lesions remain constrained by processing time, sampling representativeness, and limited molecular-level tissue assessment. Handheld Raman spectroscopy may provide label-free molecular profiling of ex vivo tissue specimens. In this methodological feasibility study, we evaluated a defined ex vivo acquisition workflow using a handheld 785-nm Raman spectrometer. We systematically evaluated laser power, integration time, and tissue thickness, and 128 mW laser power, 4000 ms integration time, and approximately 1-mm-thick tissue sections were selected as the working acquisition conditions for subsequent cervical measurements. The cervical cohort comprised 74 patients contributing 212 Raman spectra and was evaluated for two predefined primary binary classification tasks: invasive cervical cancer versus noncancer lesions (B1) and high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (HSIL) versus benign lesions plus low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (LSIL) (B2).
items.author: Yixuan Zhang, Huan Wang, Ying He et al.

items.title: IntiCom-DB v2.0: An expanded manually curated resource for inter-tissue/organ communications
items.summary: by Qiong Zhou, Changxian Xiong, Linshu Wang, Huai Pang, Rucong Liu, Jingkun Yi, Yu Han, Yuan Zhou Inter-tissue/organ communication (ITC) is essential for coordinating metabolism, immunity, development and disease progression. However, experimentally supported ITC events are dispersed across individual studies, hindering a systematic retrieval of their molecular mediators, source-to-target tissue routes and supporting evidence. Here, we present IntiCom-DB v2.0, an updated literature-derived database of experimentally supported ITC events. Compared with the previous version, IntiCom-DB v2.0 expands the curated collection to 1,862 entries from 1,485 publications, covering 651 unique ITC molecules across proteins, RNAs and metabolites. The updated database identifies 398 distinct communication routes between 51 source tissues and 53 target tissues, with protein-mediated events representing the largest category.
items.author: Qiong Zhou, Changxian Xiong, Linshu Wang et al.

items.title: Regulatory effects of Maillard reaction precursors on humification during co-composting of spent mushroom substrate and pig manure at extreme mixing ratios
items.summary: by Ming Sun, Yanyan Liu, Baoyi Lu, Mingshuo Wang, Pingxin Liu Spent mushroom substrate (SMS) and pig manure (PM) represent two dominant types of agricultural organic waste. Co-composting of these two substrates at extreme mixing ratios—common in regions with a surplus of a single waste type—frequently suffers from C/N imbalance, suppressed humification, and substantial nutrient loss. Maillard reaction precursors (MRPs) are well-documented key regulators of humus (HS) formation, yet their regulatory mechanisms and efficacy in SMS–PM co-composting at extreme mixing ratios remain poorly understood. In this study, we performed a 120-day aerobic solid-state incubation experiment using two extreme SMS: PM mass ratios (9:1 for the high-SMS system, 1:9 for the high-PM system), with catechol (Cat), glucose (Glu), and glycine (Gly) applied as exogenous MRPs.
items.author: Ming Sun, Yanyan Liu, Baoyi Lu et al.

items.title: Assessment of aspirin response in patients undergoing neuroendovascular treatments: A comparison of five platelet function tests across two platforms
items.summary: by Tasuku Sakayori, Kenji Shoda, Ryosuke Nakanishi, Yoshihiko Ueno, Ayumu Kanbe, Aki Oka, Daisuke Mizutani, Miyu Kitagami, Keisuke Kitano, Ryosuke Kikuchi, Yukiko Enomoto Aspirin is widely used for periprocedural antiplatelet therapy in neuroendovascular procedures; however, variability in patient response poses clinical challenges. This study aimed to assess five platelet function tests on two different platforms: light transmission aggregometry (LTA) using the CN-6000 device and the VerifyNow system, which were utilized to assess patients undergoing neuroendovascular procedures. A total of 124 patients who underwent elective neuroendovascular procedures and received perioperative aspirin-based antiplatelet therapy between September 2020 and December 2023 were retrospectively reviewed.
items.author: Tasuku Sakayori, Kenji Shoda, Ryosuke Nakanishi et al.

items.title: Structural reorganization of elite men’s water polo: A quasi-experimental multivariate analysis of the 2025 rule changes
items.summary: by Seung-Hun Lee The 2025 World Aquatics rule revisions for water polo aimed to accelerate offensive tempo and alter tactical decision-making by reducing the field length, shot clock duration, and possession reset times. This study used the 2024 and 2025 Men’s Water Polo World Championships as consecutive editions of the same elite international competition to provide an initial quasi-experimental assessment of performance changes associated with these revisions. Performance indicators across four domains (offensive performance, goalkeeping, exclusions, and game management) were analyzed using a multivariate analysis of variance. Notably, significant multivariate differences were observed between tournaments across all performance domains. Subsequent univariate analyses showed that these differences were primarily reflected in the frequency and distribution of match events.
items.author: Seung-Hun Lee

items.title: Clinicopathological factors associated with biochemical recurrence after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: A systematic review and meta-analysis
items.summary: by Ting Li, Danhua Wu, Lujie Ye Background This study aimed to systematically review and quantify the associations between clinicopathological factors and biochemical recurrence (BCR) following robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP). Methods This study systematically searched PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science for observational studies on predictors of BCR following RARP. The search was conducted up to March 20, 2026. Included studies were required to report results of multivariate analyses and provide odds ratios (OR) with their 95% confidence intervals (CI). Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale (NOS) criteria, and data analysis was performed using Stata 15.
items.author: Ting Li, Danhua Wu, Lujie Ye
