items.title: Multicellular signaling in reverse cardiac remodeling revealed by integrated bulk and single-nucleus transcriptomics
items.summary: Heart failure results from maladaptive multicellular remodeling triggered by sustained biomechanical stress. Although mechanical unloading can promote reverse remodeling, recovery is frequently incomplete and its mechanistic basis remains unclear. Using a reversible murine pressure-overload model combined with bulk and single-nucleus transcriptomics, we demonstrate that reverse remodeling represents an actively maintained yet constrained multicellular state. Unloading improved cardiac function and partially restored extracellular matrix and metabolic programs, whereas inflammatory and mitochondrial dysfunction signatures persisted. Cardiomyocytes and endothelial cells largely re-established homeostatic transcriptional states, while fibroblasts retained activated programs that dominated residual pathology. Multicellular factor analysis delineated a reversible metabolic stress program and a persistent inflammatory-mitochondrial program coordinated across cardiac cell types.
items.author: Steier, M., Rivero-Garcia, I., Flores, R. O. R. et al.

items.title: Network modeling identifies vitamin B2 control of AIFM2 deficit-driven hepatocyte death in MASLD
items.summary: Drug discovery for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remains difficult due to network effects. We developed MetaLiver, a public resource to identify druggable nodes within complex interactomes. It incorporates a MASLD-specific knowledge graph that improves bioactive compound contextualization while reducing computing time 18.8-fold. Layering progression-resolved bulk and hepatocyte-specific single-cell MASLD data onto this graph identified the vitamin B2-dependent flavoproteome (FlavProt) as an injury-sensitive network. Induced pluripotent stem cell-derived and primary human hepatocytes validated that flavin-cofactor replenishment mitigates FlavProt-dependent dysregulation, augmenting metabolic functions under cellular stress. Saturating flavin-cofactor availability blunted human immune cell activation. Clinically, a FlavProt expression score significantly correlated with poor outcomes in retrospectively stratified MASLD patients.
items.author: Weihs, J., Baldo, F., Cardinali, A. et al.

items.title: A dynamic displacement mechanism drives protein import into mitochondria
items.summary: Most mitochondrial proteins are produced in the cytosol and imported through the translocase of the outer mitochondrial membrane (TOM) to reach their final destination. Although this protein entry gate has been structurally characterized, it remains unclear how precursor proteins are handed off from the cytosolic receptor domains to the translocation pore. Here we show that the cytosolic domain of Tom22 - traditionally viewed as the central TOM receptor - acts not as a structured scaffold but as a largely disordered, flexible segment that plays an active role in precursor transfer. Atomic-level structural techniques and in vivo experiments identified a conserved short linear motif that forms a transient -helical element within this disordered domain.
items.author: Sucec, I., Guillerm, U., Schneider, J. et al.

items.title: From Network Topology to Parameterization: An Optimized Model of Endothelial Mechanobiology
items.summary: Endothelial cells integrate biomechanical and biochemical cues to regulate vascular function, which can be modeled using signaling networks. Yet, the extent to which their signaling behavior is determined by network topology versus reaction-specific parameterization remains unclear. We developed a continuous logic-based ordinary differential equation model of endothelial signaling containing 70 species and 123 regulatory reactions assembled from the literature. Model predictions were evaluated against 79 literature-defined responses to imposed wall stress, wall shear stress, hypoxia, or TNF. We first tested whether a single global parameter triplet (describing reaction weight, Hill coefficient, and half-maximal activation) could reproduce these observations. Investigator-selected global parameters reproduced 62/79 responses (78.48%).
items.author: Gueldner, P. H., Irons, L., Warren, J. L. et al.

items.title: Dynamic Hierarchical Interleaved Bloom Filter: An Updatable Index for Large-Scale Fast Sequence Search
items.summary: Motivation: A continued decrease in sequencing costs has facilitated the exponential increase in available sequencing data, with public databases like the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) and Sequence Read Archive (SRA) reaching well in the order of petabases. This has been the incentive to develop more scalable tools for common bioinformatics tasks. One such task is the approximate searching of short sequence patterns like genes or reads in reference data sets. In recent years, a variety of indexing data structures have been proposed for searching large sequencing databases. The state-of-the-art index, the Hierarchical Interleaved Bloom Filter (HIBF), was first-in-class to index one million samples.
items.author: Seiler, E., Willemsen, M., Piro, V. C. et al.

items.title: Ribonucleotide Reductase Inhibition Overcomes FLT3 Inhibitor Resistance in Acute Myeloid Leukemia
items.summary: Internal tandem duplication mutations in FLT3 (FLT3ITD) occur in approximately 30% of patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and are among the most common genetic alterations in this disease. FLT3ITD is a major driver of AML and associated with poor clinical outcomes. Although FLT3 inhibitors (FLT3is) have significantly improved outcomes for patients with FLT3ITD+ AML, acquired resistance remains a major barrier to durable clinical benefit. Reactivation of RAS/MAPK signaling, often driven by activating NRAS mutations, is a major mechanism of FLT3i resistance in AML; however, effective strategies to overcome this resistance remain lacking. Here, we identify ribonucleotide reductase (RNR) as a critical therapeutic vulnerability in NRAS-driven FLT3i-resistant FLT3ITD+ AML.
items.author: Tian, Z., Zhang, H., Chatla, S. et al.

items.title: Interpersonal alignment in infra-slow EEG rhythms and bodily signals anticipates mutual recognition
items.summary: Across multiple timescales, neural rhythms coordinate cognitive and physiological processes. Slower rhythms are increasingly recognised as the scale at which autonomic and interoceptive processes are folded into ongoing cognition, a brain&body view of allostatic regulation that is particularly relevant to social interaction. Examining these slow components of the electroencephalogram (EEG) during real-time interaction remains challenging. Here, we recorded infra-slow EEG alongside respiratory, cardiac and skin conductance signals during the perceptual crossing experiment, a social interaction and EEG hyperscanning paradigm. We assessed interpersonal alignment by contrasting trials in which dyads achieved mutual recognition with trials in which they did not, which separates genuine social alignment or recognition from a shared anticipatory context.
items.author: Gravel, N., Guendelman, S., Vidaurre, D.

items.title: Spatiospectral signatures of stomach-brain synchrony
items.summary: While cognitive neuroscience has increasingly recognized the brain-body connection, the temporal dynamics of how the stomach's intrinsic rhythm (~0.05 Hz) modulates human neural activity remain poorly understood. Leveraging high-resolution magneto- encephalography (MEG) and novel high-density electrogastrography (EGG), we provide the first comprehensive spatiotemporal mapping of human gastric-brain coupling at rest. Our circular-linear correlation approach revealed widespread, broadband phase-amplitude coupling between the gastric rhythm and spontaneous cortical oscillations across delta, theta, alpha, and beta bands. Using nonnegative matrix factorization, we identified distinct spatiospectral fingerprints that significantly overlap with the known fMRI-based gastric resting-state network. Functional connectivity analyses based on multivariate Granger causality further showed that these modulation patterns extend to a gastric influence on frequency-specific, directed communication between network components.
items.author: Berther, T., Saltafossi, M., Fehring, J. et al.

items.title: Spreading depolarization, not seizure activity, drives immediate early gene expression in mouse cortex after electroconvulsive stimulation
items.summary: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is a highly effective treatment for several psychiatric disorders, though its biological mechanisms remain unclear. ECT's therapeutic action has traditionally been attributed to the generalized seizure it induces. However, this view is challenged by the recent finding that electroconvulsive stimulation (ECS) can trigger a spreading depolarization (SD) in cortex. Because SD drives massive molecular changes, including expression of the plasticity-related immediate early gene Fos, we hypothesized that SD could be a key mediator of ECT's plasticity-inducing effects. We recorded the neuronal response to ECS in mouse dorsal cortex and observed similar activity to that of patients undergoing ECT.
items.author: Ladret, H. J., Lupori, L., Sieni, L. et al.

items.title: Decoding Articulatory and Phonetic Features: Somatotopic and Sensorimotor Representations in Native and Non-native Consonant Perception
items.summary: Speech perception relies on the integration of auditory and articulatory information, yet the precise role of motor regions remains debated. We combined fMRI with multivariate pattern analyses (MVPA) and behavioral measures to investigate cortical representations of native French and non-native Mandarin consonant perception under clear and noisy conditions. Cross-modal classification analysis showed that articulator-specific features of perceived degraded native bilabial and dental consonants are mapped somatotopically in right lip and tongue motor areas, which are also engaged in consonant production. These representations may support consonant categorization by compensating for degraded auditory input. Representational similarity analysis further revealed that a network encompassing bilateral temporal auditory and frontal motor regions encodes phonetic features, including place and manner of articulation, for both native and non-native consonants.
items.author: Tseng, T., Thibault, S., Krzonowski, J. et al.

items.title: Peripheral detection of viruses shapes brain immunity and behavior in zebrafish
items.summary: Olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs) are constantly exposed to pathogens, including viruses. However, serious brain infection via the olfactory route rarely occurs. When OSNs detect a virus, they coordinate local antiviral immune responses to stop virus progression to the brain. Despite effective immune control in the olfactory periphery, pathogen-triggered neuronal signals reach the CNS via the olfactory bulb (OB). We hypothesized that neuronal detection of a virus by OSNs initiates neuroimmune responses in the OB that prevent pathogen invasion. Using zebrafish (Danio rerio) as a model, we demonstrate viral-specific neuronal activation of OSNs projecting into the OB, indicating that OSNs are electrically activated by viruses.
items.author: Kraus, A., Garcia, B., Ma, J. et al.

items.title: The bile acid receptor TGR5 is a modulator of the bone marrow microenvironment
items.summary: The gut is an emerging regulator of bone marrow (BM) hematopoiesis, with several molecules involved in this communication. Among them, bile acids (BAs) act as a relay between the microbiota and the rest of the body by activating specific receptors, including Takeda G protein-coupled receptor 5 (TGR5). Although TGR5 has potent regulatory effects in immune cells, its role in the BM remains unclear. Here, we show that TGR5 is expressed across hematopoietic populations, including hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells. While TGR5 deficiency did not affect steady-state hematopoiesis, it mildly impaired cell-autonomous short-term hematopoietic reconstitution. In contrast, TGR5 deletion altered the BM microenvironment.
items.author: Alonso-Calleja, A., Perino, A., Schyrr, F. et al.

items.title: Identification of a somatic H3K23me3 methyltransferase SET-19 in C. elegans
items.summary: Histone methylation plays essential roles in modulating chromatin organization and gene expression. H3K23 methylation is a conserved histone modification, yet its biological roles and the enzymes responsible for its deposition remain poorly understood. Here, we show that the loss of set-19 leads to a pronounced reduction in H3K23 methylation in C. elegans, as revealed by quantitative mass spectrometry, western blotting, and immunofluorescence staining. In vitro biochemical assays show that recombinant SET-19 proteins purified from E. coli directly catalyze H3K23 methylation. Genome-wide chromatin immunoprecipitation assays reveal that H3K23me3 is enriched at heterochromatic regions and that loss of set-19 alters H3K23me3 levels, accompanied by derepression of a subset of genes.
items.author: Xu, M., Fan, Z., Yan, C. et al.

items.title: Can Folding Models Tell Binders from Bluffers? Evidence from POISK: The Patent-Derived Antibody Dataset
items.summary: Structure prediction models are increasingly deployed as zero-shot digital screens in antibody design, operating under the assumption that high folding confidence implies true binding. However, rigorous validation of this premise has been limited by small test sets, narrow target diversity, and the risk of data leakage from training-adjacent structures. Here we introduce POISK: Patent-extracted Organization of Immunoglobulin Sequence Knowledge, a large-scale dataset derived from the US patent literature, comprising 89074 antibody-antigen records extracted from 10110 patents using an LLM-based pipeline. From this resource, we curate a balanced benchmark set of 22494 complexes: 11247 patent-validated binders without a known resolved structure paired with putative non-binders constructed from sequence-similar human repertoire antibodies.
items.author: Tupikina, D., Roncoli, A., Bujotzek, A. et al.

items.title: CellChat Hotspot: A Targeted Approach to Cell Cell Communication Analysis With Spatial transcriptomics Validation.
items.summary: Abstract. In recent years, single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA seq) has enabled the investigation of intercellular communication through Cell Cell Communication (CCC) tools such as CellChat. Despite their potential, these approaches remain challenging to interpret, particularly when global analyses generate complex interaction networks that may include biologically irrelevant signals. To address this limitation, we developed a framework termed CellChat Hotspot, designed to improve the biological interpretability of inferred communication networks. This approach integrates gene set enrichment analysis with a context driven filtering strategy, selecting both genes and cells based on their functional relevance prior to communication inference. Applied to stage II colon cancer data, CellChat Hotspot enabled the identification of condition-specific interaction patterns associated with recurrence.
items.author: Monaco, D., Dioguardi, M., Dipalma, M. et al.

items.title: Combined EZH1/2 and DNMT inhibition overcomes transcriptional barriers imposed by drug-induced epigenetic plasticity in colorectal cancer cells
items.summary: Abnormal DNA methylation patterning is a defining epigenetic hallmark of human cancers and is therapeutically targetable with DNA methyltransferase inhibitors (DNMTi's). However, epigenetic plasticity involving Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2)-dependent H3K27 methylation can constrain transcriptional responses to DNMTi's and may contribute to their limited activity in solid tumors. Here, we compare pharmacologic strategies targeting EZH1 and EZH2 in combination with DNMT inhibition in colorectal cancer (CRC) cells and define the molecular features that distinguish EZH2-selective from dual EZH1/2 inhibition. We find that dual EZH1/2 inhibition produces more robust transcriptional activation when combined with DNMT inhibition and more extensive depletion of H3K27 methylation states than EZH2-selective inhibition.
items.author: Chomiak, A. A., Wiseman, A. K., Hrit, J. A. et al.

items.title: Activation of perivascular thermogenic fat improves aortic stenosis
items.summary: Aim: Aortic stenosis (AS) is a common condition with exponential increases in incidence in aging populations. Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) forms the outer layer of the aortic wall and has - especially in the thoracic area - characteristics of thermogenic adipose tissue, which dissipates energy and releases endocrine factors. Here, we set out to investigate the role of thermogenic PVAT in AS. Methods and results: We studied the role of (PVAT) in the development of AS in a murine model of AS. To specifically delineate the role of PVAT activity in AS, we used a pharmacological {beta}3-adrenergic agonist as well as cold exposure in combination with a genetic mouse model with deficient PVAT development.
items.author: Hildebrand, S., Wunderling, K., Siwik-Rog, Z. et al.

items.title: Mathematical Modeling of the Canonical Aryl Hydrocarbon Receptor Pathway in murine bone-marrow-derived macrophages
items.summary: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) is a ligand-activated transcription factor involved in xenobiotic sensing, as well as development, immunity, and tissue homeostasis. AhR signaling proceeds through a canonical and a non-canonical branch. It remains unclear which biochemical steps of the canonical pathway are responsible for distinct ligand specific transcriptional responses. Here, we developed a mechanistic ordinary differential equation model of the canonical AhR pathway in murine bone-marrow-derived macrophages. We calibrated it to time-resolved qPCR measurements of Cyp1a1 and Ahrr mRNA in mouse bone-marrow-derived macrophages exposed to three structurally diverse, environmentally relevant ligands with known immunomodulatory activity: 3-methylcholanthrene, indolo[3,2-]carbazole and bisphenol A.
items.author: Wieland, V., Blum, T., Iriady, I. et al.

items.title: Acute FMR1 reduction alters cellular and circuit properties in human cortex
items.summary: Transcriptional silencing of FMR1 results in Fragile X syndrome (FXS), the leading inherited cause of intellectual disability (ID) and autism. Although the impact of FMR1 reduction on cortical function has been studied using the Fmr1-/y mouse model, mechanistic insights from the human brain are lacking. Here we show that acute FMR1 reduction in ex vivo human cortical slices induces transcriptomic changes that are concordant with those observed in FXS patient cortex, identifying many targets not altered in the Fmr1-/y mouse model. Consistent with changes in ion channel expression specifically in human tissue, FMR1 reduction drives increased intrinsic excitability of deep-layer pyramidal neurons and network-level population bursts observed with two-photon calcium imaging.
items.author: Singh, A., Abbaspoor, S., Chung, L. et al.

items.title: Distinct contemplative traditions share a common EEG complexity signature
items.summary: Meditation encompasses diverse practices that train attention inward, unlike externally oriented task states. Which brain-activity features are shared across contemplative practices, which accompany long-term training, and which are tradition-specific remains unclear. We leveraged electroencephalography data from 226 participants: advanced meditators of four contemplative traditions and non-meditating controls. We developed a neurodynamic profiling approach spanning 21 features across four feature families: oscillatory, aperiodic, complexity and timescale. Using extensive machine learning, we found that meditation and task states were reliably separable, driven by a large, uniform drop in complexity during meditation. Meditators differed from controls primarily in timescale dynamics. Traditions exhibited distinct signatures in all feature families except complexity, and meditators neurodynamic profiles identified the contemplative tradition they practiced.
items.author: Shrimali, P., Sasidharan, A., Malipeddi, S. et al.

items.title: Loss of riboflavin biosynthesis leads to accumulation of select aromatic amino acids and loss of infectivity in Mycobacterium tuberculosis
items.summary: Riboflavin biosynthesis is required for in vitro survival of the human pathogen Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb). However, despite the lack of a known transporter, growth can be rescued by exogenous riboflavin. The riboflavin biosynthesis pathway is also predicted essential in vivo, but whether riboflavin levels available in the host can support survival has not been directly tested. Here we constructed a set of inducible CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) knockdown and targeted gene deletion strains for known riboflavin biosynthesis genes (ribA2, ribG, ribH, ribC) as tools to characterize riboflavin requirements, uptake, and metabolite changes and to assess in vivo essentiality. We found that riboflavin, but not flavin adenine dinucleotide or flavin mononucleotide, rescued auxotrophy for all strains tested.
items.author: Jaisinghani, N., Arasappan, A., Pradhan, A. et al.

items.title: Measuring satellite arrays of the human Y chromosome from sequencing reads
items.summary: Human Y chromosome satellites vary widely but remain difficult to measure in large cohorts. We developed Yruler, which uses pangenome assemblies to measure satellite lengths, composition and Y dosage from sequencing reads without alignment. Across cohorts, we find lineage-associated differences in centromere and non-centromeric array length, and show that heterochromatin components vary unequally within lineages. Yruler enables population-scale studies of how Y satellite variation relates to health and disease.
items.author: Ortigas-Vasquez, A., Guarracino, A.

items.title: CNVSIM: an interpretable cross-study copy-number reference atlas for cancer subtyping
items.summary: Genome-wide copy-number variation (CNV) profiles provide a representation of structural changes in cancer genomes, but interpreting new profiles with respect to their underlying biology remains challenging. We developed CNVSIM, which organizes CNV profiles into root-specific reference spaces and defines subtypes with chromosome-scale and gene-level signatures. Applied to the Progenetix dataset, CNVSIM established 112 CNV-defined subtypes across 19 cancer roots, supported by 155,881 neoplastic analyses from diverse studies and assay platforms. In the context of diagnostic concepts, these subtypes distinguish genomic architectures and reveal associated differences in somatic mutation patterns, with selected associations supported across cohorts. In practice, CNVSIM enables new profiles to be projected onto the established reference and linked to corresponding reference analyses.
items.author: YU, J., Bardet-Trouilloud, J., Jaeger, S. et al.

items.title: pH-driven dynamics and mechanisms of LNP-mediated siRNA delivery
items.summary: We present a comprehensive analysis of a clinically relevant DLin-MC3-DMA (MC3)-based lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulation that exhibits strong short interfering RNA (siRNA, ~21 nt) delivery and potent inhibition of targeted RNAs. Using a combination of coarse-grained and atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we characterize the pH-dependent structure of both unloaded and siRNA-loaded LNPs, elucidate the mechanism of siRNA encapsulation, and use these models to propose a plausible mechanism of endosomal escape. Consistent with prior experimental and computational studies, our simulations reproduce an inverted-hexagonal-type morphology in a ~70 nm siRNA-loaded LNPs. For the smaller LNPs mimetics, with only one siRNA sequence, we observe a similar hydrated core as observed in the larger 70 nm LNP model.
items.author: Hossain, K. A., Valerio, M., Medina, P. et al.

items.title: A general method for bootstrapping dense 3D segmentations from sparse 2D annotations
items.summary: Volumetric electron microscopy (vEM) provides unparalleled insight into cellular architecture, transforming our understanding of fundamental biological processes. Precise quantification of volumetric bioimaging data requires 3D instance segmentation, but the time and cost of manual ground-truth annotation present a major bottleneck for training accurate machine learning models. Our lightweight two-stage method generates complete 3D instance segmentations from sparse 2D annotations. A 2D network predicts dense boundaries on every section from minimal 2D labels. A 3D network pre- trained on synthetic data infers connectivity between sections. Across the imaging modalities and biological structures tested, our method generates base segmentations with minutes of human effort per volume.
items.author: Thiyagarajan, V. V., Sheridan, A., Harris, K. M. et al.

items.title: Synaptic pruning, myelination and the emergence of psychiatric disorders in late adolescence
items.summary: Adolescence is an important developmental period during which there are diverse changes in the brain and behavior. Goal-directed behaviors, including working memory, response inhibition, and reinforcement learning, improve during adolescence. At the same time there is substantial pruning of excitatory connections in prefrontal cortex and ongoing myelination of axons, which likely underlie these improvements in behavior. However, psychiatric disorders also become increasingly prevalent in late adolescence. In this study, we develop computational models that suggest a hypothesis for how ongoing changes in the brain can give rise to the increased prevalence of psychiatric disorders including depression, obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), schizophrenia and substance use disorders (SUDs).
items.author: Averbeck, B. B., Brunel, N.

items.title: Assessing multi-eGO Predictions of PDZ2-Peptide Binding across Mutations
items.summary: Accurately predicting how mutations alter protein-peptide binding remains challenging for molecular simulations because both conformational sampling and binding kinetics are computationally demanding. Here, we investigate whether multi-eGO, a hybrid transferable/structure-based atomistic-resolution model previously developed and validated for protein-small molecule interactions, can be transferred to protein-peptide binding. Using the PDZ2 domain of protein tyrosine phosphatase basophil-like in complex with the peptide EQVTAV as a benchmark, we show that multi-eGO, calibrated on explicit-solvent simulations of the complex, predicts the equilibrium dissociation constant of the complex within the expected uncertainty, although binding and unbinding are both accelerated by several orders of magnitude. We then introduce conservative mutations in PDZ2 and in the peptide without additional training for each mutant.
items.author: Ardizzone, C., Stegani, B., Bacic Toplek, F. et al.

items.title: Network modularity reveals context and state-dependent reorganization of time-varying functional connectivity in single-cell resolved neural activity recordings
items.summary: An important goal of neuroscience is to understand how biological neural networks organize activity at multiple scales to enable complex information processing and behavioral output. To address this challenge, large-scale neural activity datasets with increased resolution and wider coverage have become more prevalent across many model systems. However, bridging the gap in scale between changes in pairwise functional connectivity between neurons and changes in brain-wide organization of activity remains a key challenge. In this work, we demonstrate application of modularity-based community detection and network modularity to single-cell resolved recordings, for the first time, as a method to summarize complex changes in time-varying functional connectivity, facilitating comparisons across multiple time windows, recordings, and conditions.
items.author: Moon, S., Liang, J., Lee, H. J. et al.

items.title: Reactive and predictive processes during unpredictable driving collisions in virtual reality: an exploratory immersive study with multimodal neurophysiological monitoring
items.summary: Anticipatory neurophysiological activity before unpredictable emotional events has been reported for decades, but the effects are small, difficult to replicate, and obtained almost exclusively in stripped-down laboratory paradigms. Whether they reflect genuine predictive processes or methodological artifacts remains debated; one rarely tested possibility is that such settings mute it. We examined anticipation in an immersive virtual reality (VR) driving simulation whose collision outcomes were assigned by a quantum random number generator, while EEG, photoplethysmography (PPG), EMG, EOG and inertial (IMU) signals were recorded from a single wireless dry-electrode headset built into the VR display. Sixteen participants passively observed 120 driving sequences ending in a collision or no collision.
items.author: Cannard, C., Yesilbas, D.

items.title: Immersive display systems for simulating natural vision
items.summary: Vision is traditionally studied using simplified stimuli presented briefly near the center of a flat display while subjects maintain visual fixation. This paradigm contrasts sharply with real-world vision, which is immersive, dynamic and strongly influenced by self-initiated actions. Traditional approaches have allowed researchers to systematically study the neural encoding of visual features and the influence of cognitive operations such as attention. However, other methods are needed to study more holistic and first-person perspectives on vision, such as those related to physical space, continuous time, and self-movement. To enable the study of these and other aspects of real-world vision, we developed hemispherical ("dome") display systems for macaque visual neuroscience.
items.author: Katti, H., Murphy, A. P., Helde, M. et al.

items.title: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion
items.summary: Monitoring maritime activities is important for safety and security, particularly for detecting illegal activities, but remains challenging due to the size and complexity of the maritime domain. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) is commonly used for this purpose, despite its known vulnerabilities. In contrast, space-based radio frequency (RF) observations provide an independent source of vessel activity but lack ship identification and therefore cannot identify vessels on their own. Following the CRISP-DM process, this study applies a Pair Hidden Markov Model (PHMM) to align individual RF detections with AIS trajectories, using temporal and spatial information while modeling noise and timing discrepancies.
items.author: Daniel Grimm, Kyra Jongman, Renato Cordeiro Ferreira et al.

items.title: FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices
items.summary: Recent advances in speech neuroprostheses have enabled new communication avenues for people who have lost the ability to speak due to neurological illness or injury. These systems can decode neural activity during attempted speech into text by relying on language priors to achieve high decoding accuracy. This performance currently comes at the cost of using a compute-intensive language modeling stack, presenting a major bottleneck for real-world use. Further, current language models incur highly variable and disruptive inference latencies, limiting communication throughput and preventing users from reliably participating in natural conversation. We introduce FETTUCCINE, an end-to-end brain-to-text framework that leverages the speed and portability of automatic speech recognition (ASR) models to address the aforementioned practical challenges, while achieving usable (<10%) word error rates (WER), efficient adaptation to neural non-stationarities, and reliable performance on mobile devices.
items.author: Jonathan D. McCart, Pranav I. Deevi, Mehdi Azabou et al.

items.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
items.summary: Robot-use agents (RUAs) have emerged as a promising approach to general-purpose robot control. However, strong performance has so far been achieved only by frontier proprietary models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, whereas open-weight models remain substantially less capable. We show that an open-weight 27B reasoning model can be trained to use real robots natively through reinforcement learning, entirely in simulation and without demonstrations. Like a computer-use agent (CUA), the model observes the environment, reasons in a chain of thought, and generates the next end-effector pose, without any harness. We build a Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics (PEAR) and use it to train the model on simulated robot tasks at scale with robot-use reinforcement learning (RURL), mirroring how frontier models acquire computer use.
items.author: Jiaming Tang, Zhuoyang Zhang, Junxian Guo et al.

items.title: BAL: Bidirectional Autoregression in Latent Space for Learning Human Movement Representations
items.summary: Learning semantically meaningful human movement representations from 3D pose sequences is essential for human behavior modeling. Existing self-supervised methods derive supervision from artificial assumptions, e.g., invariance to augmentation within a certain range or recoverability of masked regions at a certain temporal scale, introducing heuristic hyperparameters that make the learned semantics sensitive to their settings. We propose BAL, a self-supervised framework that instead exploits supervision intrinsic to human movement: the natural ordering structure of everyday behavior. BAL autoregressively predicts in a semantically abstract latent space, analogous to how humans anticipate others' actions rather than their precise joint configurations. Bidirectional autoregressive prediction, both forward and backward in time, fully leverages these ordering constraints while enabling representation extraction using both past and future context at inference.
items.author: Genki Kinoshita, Ko Nishino

items.title: Reconstruction of Dynamical Dark Energy and Gravity from latest cosmological data
items.summary: Recent cosmological observations have renewed interest in non-standard late-time evolution. We investigate whether departures from the standard expansion history are accompanied by modifications of gravitational dynamics through a joint, non-parametric reconstruction of the effective dark energy density, $Ω_{\rm X}(a)$, and the gravitational response functions $μ(a)$ and $Σ(a)$. Combining CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon+, and large scale structure observations, including DES Year 3 $6\times2$pt data, we perform reconstructions with and without a theory motivated correlation prior derived from stable Horndeski models. We find a persistent maximum in $Ω_{\rm X}$ at $z\simeq0.5$--$0.7$, corresponding to a crossing of the effective phantom divide. This feature is already present in the CMB+BAO combination and remains robust when modifications to clustering and lensing are allowed.
items.author: Maria Luisa Gallavotti, Alessandra Silvestri

items.title: Does Dark Energy Evolve $\textit{and}$ Cluster?
items.summary: Recent cosmological observations have renewed interest in dynamical dark energy, and naturally raise the question of whether departures from the standard expansion history are accompanied by modifications of gravitational dynamics. We address this question through a joint, non-parametric reconstruction of the effective dark-energy contribution to the expansion and the gravitational responses governing clustering and lensing, complemented by a combined covariance-mode analysis, without imposing model-specific relations between the sectors. Combining CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, and Pantheon+ supernova observations, and subsequently adding large scale structure observations including DES Year 3 $6\times2$pt data and other surveys, we recover a broad maximum in the effective dark-energy density near $z\simeq0.6$--$0.7$.
items.author: Maria Luisa Gallavotti, Alessandra Silvestri

items.title: From pure spinor modules to superspace superfields
items.summary: We relate the pure spinor formalism to the superspace description of constrained superfields and gauge multiplets, mainly for abelian two-dimensional N=(2,2) supersymmetry, with three- and four-dimensional N=1 examples for comparison. For each multiplet we give an explicit module over the supertranslation Chevalley-Eilenberg algebra and match its reconstruction with the known superfields. First-order constraints come from modules supported on linear subspaces of the nilpotence variety, and higher-order ones, such as the complex-linear constraint, from Yoneda products of their Ext classes. Requiring a connection to act on given matter and its conjugate restricts its curvature, which yields the ordinary, twisted and semichiral vector multiplets with their field strengths.
items.author: Ondrej Hulik, Raphael Senghaas

items.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
items.summary: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. They can read what a network was trained to do, fix a network that fails, and write working networks from scratch, all without gradient descent. This capability has been termed Weight-Space Programming (WSP). Exploring this new paradigm systematically requires a robust benchmark. We introduce WEIGHTBENCH, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs of increasing capability on 42 WSP tasks across five tracks: reading, fixing and writing weights, recognizing edits that are impossible, and data-free compression. The networks whose weights the LLMs read and edit range from 2K-parameter control policies to 7B-parameter language models.
items.author: Aayush Marasini, Barsat Khadka, Nick Rahimi

items.title: Real-time simulation of scattering in $φ^4$ theory: localized excitation, scalable wave packet preparation, and peak-generating artifacts
items.summary: Probing real-time dynamics is essential for understanding non-perturbative scattering and interactions in quantum field theory. A common challenge in real-time simulation is preparing accurate asymptotic incoming states. Through efficiently solvable eigenvalue problems, we jointly optimize a superposition of single particle momentum eigenstates and a single site interpolating operator to maximize preparation fidelity from the interacting vacuum. This leads to a localized excitation in the interacting theory analogous to a position eigenstate. Weighted sums of the resulting interpolating operator over lattice sites prepare wave packets of arbitrary spatial extent. To ensure that this construction produces the correct continuum limit, relative phases among single particle momentum eigenstates in this superposition are calibrated using a relation derived from Lorentz symmetry.
items.author: Boyu Gao, Natalie Klco

items.title: Modeling the Frictional Contact of Continuum Robots with Environments through Linear Complementarity Problem
items.summary: Accurate friction modeling in continuum robots is essential for precise motion control and path planning. However, current approaches make predictions only for the mechanism's internal friction that is limited by the boundary forces of the Coulomb friction cone, which fail to characterize the static friction and motion hysteresis. In this paper, we propose a novel friction model based on complementarity constraints under the Coulomb friction assumption. This model predicts various friction effects caused by environmental interactions, including both static and sliding frictions and hysteresis behavior, as well as the corresponding robot deformation induced by these interactions, which are crucial for the practical motion planning and control of continuum robots.
items.author: Jia Shen, Junhyoung Ha, Yue Chen

items.title: Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Demonstrations are an effective way to accelerate single-agent reinforcement learning (RL), but extending this idea to multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is non-trivial as it is difficult and often impossible for a single person to teleoperate multiple agents simultaneously. Round-Robin Behavior Cloning (R2BC) addresses this by letting a single demonstrator control one agent at a time while the others execute their current policies. However, the resulting imitation policies are limited by the quality of the demonstrations. We propose Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (IBMARL), a framework that extends Imitation Bootstrapped Reinforcement Learning (IBRL) to cooperative teams and uses R2BC to train the imitation policies.
items.author: Tony H. Zhang, Connor Mattson, Daniel S. Brown

items.title: Elliptic Sampling: Optimal Interpolant Schedules for Gaussians and Beyond
items.summary: Generative modeling based on stochastic interpolants requires specifying two key choices: an interpolant schedule bridging the initial and target distributions, and an efficient discretization of the resulting probability-flow ODE. In this work, we introduce a new framework for joint schedule/discretization design based on the analyticity properties of the (complexified) ODE trajectories, which in turn ensure good numerical behavior. Our formulation can be solved exactly via conformal mapping, yielding a natural family of variance-preserving elliptic schedules, parametrized by Jacobi elliptic functions. Pairing an elliptic schedule with a tailored discretization, we obtain Zoloflow, a new sampling algorithm closely connected to Zolotarev's optimal rational function approximants.
items.author: Cole Becker, Taylan Kargin, Kimia Hassibi et al.

items.title: Geometric Quantization of the Giant Graviton Master Moduli Space
items.summary: We describe a remarkable reorganization of the space of gauge invariant operators of free or twisted $U(N)$ gauge theories as combinations of single-trace and determinant operators modulo certain "open loop equations". The reorganization has a transparent holographic interpretation, describing how states at finite $N$ can be reproduced by imposing certain $N$-independent gauge constraints on the combination of the closed strings Fock space and a geometric quantization of the moduli space of Giant Graviton D-branes, with quantization parameter $N^{-1}$. The moduli space of Giant Graviton D-branes is reproduced from tachyon condensation of auxiliary D-brane/anti-D-brane pairs which are "Koszul dual" to the D-brane system which supports the original gauge theory.
items.author: Kasia Budzik, Davide Gaiotto

items.title: Why Finite Intelligence Works in an Infinite World: A Mathematical Theory
items.summary: An information system often has to learn before it knows what it will be asked. A finite representation can succeed without recording an infinite environment in full when those asks share collective structure, rather than demand unrelated facts scattered arbitrarily across it. We formalize this phenomenon through future-task information, the minimum retained information needed to preserve decision value relative to the available evidence. A joint decision-regret state records posterior comparisons among actions for every permitted task. Under compactness assumptions, every retained representation admits a calibrated replacement based on this state, preserving all task regrets without increasing information; the resulting information-regret curve equals an operational coding rate.
items.author: Mojtaba Soltanalian

items.title: ModHarness-RL: Recasting Harnesses as Learnable and Evolving Programs for Agentic RL
items.summary: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) increasingly relies on a harness, the scaffold around the model that decides what it sees of its own interaction and what guidance it receives. Most existing approaches train under a hand-written harness that stays fixed throughout. However, an effective harness depends on the domain, the data and the model, and keeps changing as the model trains. We introduce ModHarness-RL, which recasts the harness as programs that are learned from data and evolve as the model trains with RL. ModHarness-RL records the interaction as structured State, a set of typed blocks, and two core components of the harness are programs over these blocks, a Compression program that assembles the accumulated history into the model's context and a Steering program that supplies guidance when behavior deviates.
items.author: Zelin He, Siyu Zhu, Jacob Helwig et al.

items.title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are expected to complete tasks while following rules of conduct, but these objectives can conflict. We study how evolutionary selection shapes an agent's choices between them, and whether experience can make those choices reflect human judgments and withstand subsequent pressures. In our model, copies of an agent face a common uncertain reward state, and only those taking the rewarded action reproduce. We show that long-run growth is maximized when each action is taken as often as the environment rewards it. We compare three policies. A task-only policy thrives in a sandbox rewarding completion alone but fails when conduct matters.
items.author: Thomas Brennan, Andrew W. Lo, Chaoyi Zhao

items.title: Three-dimensional parton structure in QCD with CP-violation
items.summary: The Energy-Momentum tensor encodes the mechanical properties of a system such as the internal distributions energy, momentum, forces, and particle fluxes. The QCD energy momentum tensor respects CP symmetry even when QCD is modified with a CP-violating $θ$-term. In this theory, there are 5 unique generalized form factors in the Lorentz decomposition of the total Energy Momentum tensor and 3 more which only vanish when summing over all flavors. We introduce two new lightcone GPDs whose Mellin moments give the electromagnetic and gravitational form factors. These generalize the observables for QCD-based CP violation such as the neutron electric dipole moment to three dimensional light cone structure.
items.author: Alexandru-Mihail Sturzu, Joe Karpie

items.title: Pressure and Magnetic Field Control of Topology in Antiferromagnetic Bilayers
items.summary: Controlling band topology in magnetic semiconductors requires strategies that couple electronic structure to experimentally accessible degrees of freedom. Here we propose a cooperative approach based on pressure and magnetic reorientation in A-type antiferromagnetic bilayers. Antiparallel layer magnetizations suppress hybridization between exchange-polarized band-edge states, limiting their response to interlayer compression. A magnetic field that aligns the layer moments removes this spin mismatch, enabling pressure-enhanced hybridization to drive a band inversion. The magnetization direction then controls the symmetries of the inverted bands and whether spin--orbit coupling produces a Chern-insulating gap or symmetry-protected nodal crossings. First-principles calculations for bilayer CrSBr illustrate this mechanism within a compressed orthorhombic structural model.
items.author: Narsimha Rao Elaprolu, Marco Gibertini

items.title: The Spectral Anatomy of Complex-Time Singularities
items.summary: The properties of the bulk spacetime in a holographic theory may be probed by the analytic structure of the boundary correlator $G(t,x)$. In this letter, we analyse the singularities of $G(t,x)$ by deriving them from Fourier space. We show that the quasinormal modes are characterised by two distinct momentum scaling regimes. The first regime is defined by a finite $k/ω^γ$ for some characteristic exponent $γ$ which is extracted from the singularity, and probes $G(t,0)$, reproducing the bouncing geodesic analysis. The second regime is defined by a finite $k/ω$, and probes the complexified bulk away from the singularity, which allows us to study the singularities of $G(t,x\neq 0)$.
items.author: Samuel Valach, Mile Vrbica

items.title: Parity conservation of the isotropic galaxy 4PCF in redshift space
items.summary: Recent observational investigation of cosmological Parity Violation (PV) through the galaxy Four-point Correlation Function (4PCF) has motivated a careful theoretical examination of potential systematic contributions. In this work, we demonstrate that parity-odd contributions to the isotropic 4PCF estimator induced by Redshift Space Distortion (RSD), up to the leading order $\mathcal{H}/k$ of general relativistic corrections, vanish upon averaging over all the Line-of-Sight (LOS). We analyse the perturbative relativistic galaxy number density, combining the biased tracer expansion and the dark matter gravitational dynamics within the framework of Standard Eulerian Perturbation Theory (EPT) to third order in the density perturbation.
items.author: Chanasorn Kongprachaya, Nicola Bartolo, Daniele Bertacca et al.

items.title: Can Mechanistic Interpretability Help Explain LLM Agent Failures? A Case Study on Web Element Hallucination
items.summary: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) has made significant progress in explaining the internal computations of Large Language Models (LLMs); however, these advances have yet to demonstrate comparable success in explaining the decision-making processes of LLM-based agents. This paper examines the challenges MI tools face when applied to realistic agentic failures. We focus on one such failure: web agents hallucinating actions that are not available on a website. We apply a series of mechanistic analyzes to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as it interacts with live websites. We find that a linear probe trained on the last prompt token can predict hallucinations before generation begins (0.80 AUC) and steering along a probe direction corrects 85\% of hallucinations, but disrupts 7\% of valid actions.
items.author: Mohamed Aghzal, Mor Geva, Gregory J. Stein et al.

items.title: MeReader: An Offline, Privacy-Preserving, Progress-Aware AI Assistant for Narrative eBook Reading
items.summary: This paper introduces MeReader, a privacy-preserving, offline and progress-aware AI assistant designed to function as a contextual companion for narrative reading on consumer hardware. Unlike conventional Large Language Model (LLM)-based systems that process documents/books online in an all-texts-at-once type of way, thereby risking narrative spoilers, MeReader confines both retrieval and generation to the reader's distinct position in the text. The system integrates a hybrid retrieval architecture, combining vector similarity, BM25, and summary embeddings, to ensure high fidelity to the reader's current context. We evaluate the system across classical English books using both quantitative comprehension metrics and qualitative LLM-based independent judging.
items.author: Mohammed Efaz, Udo Bub, Itilekha Podder

items.title: Probing baryonic feedback using fast radio bursts and galaxy surveys
items.summary: The dispersion measure (DM) of fast radio bursts (FRB) provides a noisy measure of the free-electron column density to the burst. With next-generation FRB surveys the number of bursts will drastically increase and measurements of the baryon distribution will be possible on the Mpc scales most relevant to Stage IV weak lensing surveys. Comparing the DM auto-spectrum, DM-shear cross-spectrum and the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect, we argue that the cross-correlation of FRB catalogs with galaxy surveys offers many advantages. Hybrid Effective Field Theory (HEFT), often used in large-scale structure cosmology, is capable of modeling the clustering of electrons jointly with galaxies and matter to small scales.
items.author: Haruki Ebina, Martin White

items.title: Complex fluid flow dynamics by bright scattershot boson sampling
items.summary: Boson sampling machines have become a fruitful tool for establishing new concepts, which connect fundamental physics with computer science applications. Here, we exploit the intrinsically high-dimensional correlations generated by the measurement outcomes of a multiphoton boson sampling machine and demonstrate how a reconfigurable architecture can be programmed to autonomously model the time evolution of nonlinear dynamical systems that describe complex fluid flows. By extending on the original scattershot boson sampling (SBS) scheme to include higher photon number components -- a scheme which we label bright scattershot boson sampling (BSBS) --- this scheme overcomes scaling issues inherent to SBS-based schemes by utilizing all randomly generated input photon number distributions.
items.author: Robert Schade, Shailendra K. Rathor, Tim J. Bartley et al.

items.title: Disturbance-Aware Informative Planning in Spatiotemporal Environments
items.summary: Autonomous robots are widely used for persistent monitoring of spatiotemporal environments, where quantities of interest (QoI) change across space and time and require repeated measurements. In practice, robot motion can be affected by external disturbances that vary across the environment. When such external disturbances are not considered in trajectory optimization, it can lead to inaccurate predictions of robot motion and, consequently, the information acquired about the QoI during execution. However, estimating disturbances throughout the environment can be inefficient, as disturbances in regions with little overlap with monitoring trajectories have limited impact on monitoring performance. We therefore propose a two-stage informative planning framework for unknown, spatially varying but time-invariant disturbances, combining informed disturbance sampling with disturbance-aware trajectory optimization.
items.author: Kaleb Ben Naveed, Haejoon Lee, Anouck Girard et al.

items.title: Agentic AI for Discovering Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
items.summary: Scaling quantum computing toward practical quantum advantage is currently limited by the efficiency of circuits that operate on information encoded by quantum error-correcting codes. The full stack of quantum computing encompasses several tasks: preparation of logical code states, implementation of logical gates, logical routines on encoded qubits, etc. Yet, these circuits are largely designed by hand for individual cases, with some recent works incorporating machine learning for certain aspects. We formulate this problem as agentic evolutionary program synthesis, wherein a large language model, leveraging its pretraining knowledge and tool-use proficiency, and guided by a circuit verifier, evolves a program that defines a Clifford circuit for a wide range of curated tasks such as logical state preparation, logical gate design, and logical routines such as code-switching, code growth, etc.
items.author: Aritra Lahiri, Florian Marquardt

items.title: Solution of the Qubit Marginal Problem from Fermionic Representability
items.summary: Whether local reduced states are compatible with a global quantum state---the quantum marginal problem---is central to quantum information and simulation. Here we present a solution to the ensemble marginal problem for qubits based on the representability theory of fermions. Encoding each qubit as one fermion in two orbitals, we prove that the representable qubit marginals form an exposed face of the set of $N$-representable fermionic reduced density matrices, selected by the vanishing of every site-occupation variance. Complete hierarchies of fermionic representability conditions therefore transfer exactly to qubits. Applications to frustrated Heisenberg and transverse-field Ising rings show that the $(2,3)$-positivity conditions are exact at the Majumdar--Ghosh point and accurate to about 0.5% at criticality.
items.author: David A. Mazziotti

items.title: In Situ Monitoring and Predictive Modeling of Harmful Algal Blooms with Autonomous Surface Vehicles
items.summary: Harmful Algal Blooms (HABs) pose significant environmental, economic, and public-health challenges in coastal and inland water bodies, creating a need for scalable methods to collect spatially distributed water-quality data. This paper presents an autonomous surface vessel-based sensing system for in-situ water-quality monitoring related to harmful algal bloom detection. The system integrates a BlueBoat Autonomous Surface Vessel (ASV), a motorized winch for depth-controlled sonde deployment, a multiparameter water-quality sonde, side-scan sonar, and an event-camera payload. Autonomous waypoint missions were used to collect measurements across selected sampling regions and multiple depths, enabling both horizontal and vertical characterization of environmental conditions. Field deployments were conducted in Lake Pontchartrain, Louisiana, with additional measurements collected in False River, Louisiana to increase dataset diversity.
items.author: Nenyi Kweku Nkensen Dadson, Jean Paul Gonzalez, Daniel P. Arabie et al.

items.title: Toward Resilient Self-Driving Laboratories through Telerobotic Interventions
items.summary: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) accelerate scientific research by integrating robotics, automated experimentation, and machine learning to execute experiments autonomously. Biology and chemistry have adopted these systems. However, increasing SDL complexity heightens susceptibility to unexpected faults in automated workflows, highlighting the need for efficient recovery mechanisms. In this study, we investigate telerobotic interventions to enhance SDL resilience against unexpected failures. We developed a teleoperation interface enabling human operators to resolve disruptions during automated tasks. The interface enables precise control of a six-degree-of-freedom (DOF) robotic arm (UR3e) using a 3D mouse (3Dconnexion SpaceMouse Pro). Two velocity-based controller strategies were evaluated: (i) a coupled mode mapping all six DOFs to the 3D mouse's central knob and (ii) a decoupled mode separating translational and rotational motions.
items.author: Ziheng Wu, Adrian Vecina Tercero, Andre A. Fatehi et al.

items.title: Blind in-memory arithmetic with confined skyrmions: doubling and successor functions on a skyrmion byte
items.summary: We present a skyrmionic-based computation platform, able to perform fully in-memory computing by collectively manipulating the skyrmions that serve as bits of the binary memory. The computation protocols are implemented through driving currents and adequately located anisotropy defects that modify the dynamics of the skyrmions along a magnetic track. Simulations demonstrating the feasibility of such an in-memory computing system are shown for several basic and simple mathematical operations with natural numbers, such as doubling and adding one (the successor function). We also discuss how further optimization of the geometry, barrier profiles, current amplitudes, and timing parameters could improve both the robustness and the overall practical feasibility of the system.
items.author: Joan Reverté, Nuria Del-Valle, Jaume Cunill-Subiranas et al.

items.title: When Will You Hand It Over? A Hidden Start Delay Makes Self-Play Handover Robust to Unfamiliar Partners
items.summary: Cooperative self-play can teach a humanoid to receive an object without any human data, but the partner it meets after training is never the one it trained with; we show that a fluent self-play handover policy breaks with unfamiliar partners, identify the main cause, and repair it. In a physics-based parcel handover between a Unitree G1 and a learned giver, both trained by alternating PPO self-play, the receiver completes 95% and 90% of handovers with its own partner (two training seeds) but only 31% with scripted partners it has never met. Paired interventions isolate the cause: under a shared reward the learned giver always starts its offer at once, so the receiver learns a single rendezvous, and delaying its own partner by one second cuts success from 95% to 6% (87% to 34% in the second seed).
items.author: Mohammad Khoshnazar, Mike Degany, Deyuan Qu et al.

items.title: Fine-tuned atomistic foundation model for accurate sodium-carbon chemistry in Na-ion batteries
items.summary: Atomistic foundation models have emerged as a promising route to DFT-level accuracy for materials simulation with complex chemical environments. However, their reliability across competing bonding regimes and, more importantly, how complex bonding affects predictions of material properties remain unclear. Among materials with competing bonding regimes, sodium storage in hard carbon poses a substantial challenge. Hard carbon features diverse local structural motifs, including defective and curved graphitic regions, amorphous regions, and closed/open pores. Motivated by its importance for Na-ion batteries, we systematically evaluate existing pretrained foundation models based on the MACE architecture across different local Na/C motifs. We find that the pretrained models fail to accurately capture Na-Na and Na-C interactions for metallic Na clusters on graphene.
items.author: Andres Felipe Usuga, Ihor Radchenko, Yuxin Tang et al.

items.title: Dissipation as a Resource for Entanglement via High-Spin Mediator Purification
items.summary: We study entanglement generation between two spin qubits mediated by a single, thermally mixed, high-spin ($S=5/2$) magnetic impurity, using the Lindblad master equation to compare coherent and dissipative control of the mediator. We show that no coherent drive, however strong or resonant, can purify the mediator beyond its thermal value --- a direct consequence of unitary evolution exactly preserving state purity --- while a dissipative channel purifies it up to the limit set by the optical pumping cycle itself, $\mathrm{Tr}[ρ_M^2]\approx0.8$. Modeling this channel with rates fixed by the measured optical pumping of a single Mn spin, we find that the entanglement it enables is not monotonic in the pump strength: it peaks at a finite rate and then decreases, since the same channel leaks decoherence to the qubits through the coupling that mediates their entanglement.
items.author: Ellen Martins Fernandes, Fabricio Macedo de Souza

items.title: A charge-dependent electron emission yield from electron irradiated dielectrics
items.summary: The total electron emission yield (TEEY) of dielectric surfaces may vary during electron irradiation owing to charge accumulation within the material. In the present work, the generation, transport, and escape formulation of Dionne is extended by introducing an additional attenuation of secondary electrons that depends on trapped positive charge. The resulting emission law is coupled to a charge-balance equation, allowing the TEEY to be calculated as a function of incident energy and injected charge. The model is examined using measurements on polycrystalline Al2O3, from which effective cross sections describing interactions between trapped charge and secondary electrons are determined. Their mean value is then used to predict the evolution of the TEEY curves without further adjustment.
items.author: M. Belhaj, A. M. Cavalca de Almeida, N. Fil

items.title: From AI-Enabled Remote Patient Monitoring Toward Agentic Robotics: Embodiment, Governance, and Care Integration
items.summary: AI-enabled remote patient monitoring is evolving beyond passive data collection toward agentic AI systems that interpret patient states, coordinate care, and initiate action across domestic and clinical settings. This structured scoping review finds that mature agentic care has not yet emerged: Most systems remain human led, while stronger decision-action coupling and embodied AI remain largely confined to prototypes and pilots. Healthcare robotics makes the transition from monitoring to action especially visible by translating AI-generated recommendations and decisions into speech, movement, prompting, physical assistance, escalation, and care coordination, making embodiment, clinical integration, human oversight, and governance fundamental design requirements. Further progress requires safe and interoperable care architectures in which intelligent components operate through clinically validated and accountable workflows.
items.author: Ivana Ragusa, Lorenzo Guiducci, Filippo Cavallo

items.title: Beyond Blossom: Accelerating MWPM Decoding for Surface Codes With Local Predecoding and Architecture-Aware Optimizations
items.summary: Minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) is widely used to decode surface codes, but its computational cost increases with code distance. We present Beyond Blossom, a state-of-the-art CPU-based MWPM decoder for surface codes. It combines algorithmic optimization through local predecoding, architecture-aware optimization, and pipeline-wide parallelism to reduce matching workload and execution overhead while preserving MWPM optimality. Across rotated surface codes with distances 9-33 and circuit-level physical error rates of 0.05%-0.3%, on a single CPU core, Beyond Blossom achieves a 4.23$\times$ geometric-mean speedup and up to 5.58$\times$ speedup over Sparse Blossom in PyMatching. At distance 33 and a physical error rate of 0.1%, with 8 CPU cores, decoding a block of 33 measurement rounds takes 21.40 $μ$s on average, equivalent to 0.65 $μ$s per round.
items.author: Jiayu Fu, Zirong Shen, Lin Gan et al.

items.title: Machine learning of strength surfaces enables high regularization length phase-field fracture
items.summary: Classical phase-field models of brittle fracture capture toughness-controlled crack growth but not the material's strength surface, which governs crack nucleation. The theory of Kumar et al. (2020) incorporates the strength surface through a nucleation driving force, and Chockalingam (2025) derived this driving force for arbitrary strength surfaces described by $n$ material parameters, with which the phase-field strength surface (PFSS) converges to the material strength surface as the regularization length $\varepsilon \to 0$ and matches it exactly at $n$ chosen states for any $\varepsilon$. In practice, however, the strength surface must be supplied as an analytic form chosen and calibrated case by case, and for the widely used analytic surfaces ($n=2$) accurate strength reproduction requires $\varepsilon$ commensurate with the Irwin characteristic length $l_{ch}$, imposing prohibitive mesh requirements for large structures.
items.author: S Chockalingam, Aditya Kumar, Adrian Buganza Tepole

items.title: Exploring M-theory on AdS$_7\times$S$^4$: Mellin amplitudes with composite operators
items.summary: We bootstrap mixed correlators in M-theory on AdS$_7\times$S$^4$, focusing on tree-level correlation functions involving one double-particle operator and three single-particle operators. Combining inputs from AdS/CFT, the chiral algebra, and the OPE at large central charge, we uniquely determine the Mellin amplitude for $\langle [{\cal O}_{2}{\cal O}_{q}]{\cal O}_{2}{\cal O}_{p}{\cal O}_{p+q-2}\rangle$ for generic $p$ and $q$. While our main focus is the $\mathcal{N}=(2,0)$ SCFT in six dimensions, we also derive the analogous result in AdS$_5\times$S$^5$, applying the same bootstrap approach to $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM. Despite their different dynamics, the resulting Mellin amplitudes exhibit a strikingly similar structure, with non-trivial OPE predictions for low-twist protected operators providing a key input.
items.author: Francesco Aprile, Hector Puerta-Ramisa, Mitchell Woolley

items.title: Symmetry-Controlled Quantum State Transfer in Poly-bi-[8]-annulenylene: From Heisenberg to Hubbard Dynamics
items.summary: We investigate quantum state transfer in the poly-bi-[8]-annulenylene lattice using isotropic Heisenberg and Hubbard models. For a 16-site lattice, reflection symmetry separates the single-excitation Hamiltonian into independent triplet and singlet sectors, allowing analytical determination of the energy spectra. Although perfect state transfer is forbidden for positive couplings, appropriately chosen coupling ratios enable pretty-good transfer with arbitrarily high fidelity. Remarkably, the triplet transfer probability is independent of the interchain rung coupling, while singlet transfer can be selectively enhanced or suppressed, enabling symmetry-selective quantum transport without time-dependent control. Extending the analysis to the Hubbard model, we show that the Heisenberg transfer dynamics emerge in the strong-interaction limit, while finite interactions delay all high-fidelity transfer peaks of a symmetry sector by the same fraction of their transfer time, set by the spectrum, and reduce the peak fidelity, even at the corrected time, by an amount that grows with the transfer time.
items.author: Adnan Jaljuli, Pablo Serra, Ammar Ali et al.

items.title: Topological phase diagram of an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with negative coupling
items.summary: Recently, an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with three atoms per unit cell has been experimentally realized in perovskite exciton-polariton micropillars. A distinctive feature of this system is that the second and third bands undergo a topological transition through a band crossing at the wave vector $k=0$, associated with a negative coupling. In this work, we analytically determine the phase diagram of the model as a function of the on-site energy splitting and the ratio of intercell to intracell hopping amplitudes. We identify seven regions in this lane, with four distinct topological phases, characterized by different Zak phases of the three bands.
items.author: P. A. Grizzi, P. Roura-Bas, A. A. Aligia

items.title: Learning observable propagation with sparse local moments
items.summary: We propose a unified framework for predicting local moment dynamics in high-dimensional many-body systems from short-time trajectories. Thanks to the locality of the dynamics, we construct the transition moment matrices by projecting the Markov operator onto low-order connected-cluster basis functions supported near the target observable. Exploiting the spatial decay of time-lagged correlations, {these matrices} can be approximated in sparse-plus-low-rank form using trajectory samples, with computational cost scaling linearly in the system dimension and the number of trajectories. The learning error can be further reduced by correcting the memory effect induced by the Galerkin projection. We numerically demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework in extrapolating the dynamics of various many-body systems, including Langevin and Glauber dynamics for classical systems as well as Lindblad dynamics for open quantum systems.
items.author: Yuehaw Khoo, Bowen Li, Yuguan Wang et al.

items.title: High Entropy Oxides as Room Temperature Anderson Insulators with Colossal Soft Gaps
items.summary: The Anderson effect, arising from destructive quantum interference of electron wave packets in disordered potentials, is usually observed at cryogenic temperatures and typically arises from extrinsic defects in conventional materials such as phosphorus dopants in silicon or oxygen vacancies in transition metal oxides. Here we demonstrate that a multication lattice of transition metals in a high-entropy oxide (HEO) natively establishes an interacting Anderson insulator that extends up to $500\,\mathrm{K}$. By controlling the population of transition metal cations in $\mathrm{La}_{0.7}\mathrm{Sr}_{0.3}\mathrm{Mn}_{1-x}(\mathrm{Cr},\mathrm{Fe},\mathrm{Co},\mathrm{Ni})_{x/4}\mathrm{O}_3$ (LS5B), we tune the system from the prototypical correlated metal $\mathrm{La}_{0.7}\mathrm{Sr}_{0.3}\mathrm{Mn}\mathrm{O}_3$ at $x=0.00$ to a localized insulator at $x=0.80$, where the disorder length contracts to near the unit cell (3.85 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$) and drives the electron mean free path to the Ioffe-Regel limit.
items.author: Elena Salagre, Heather Hare, Eli Rotenberg et al.

items.title: Validating Graph Neural Network Feature Attribution Through Local Perturbations: A Study on CoMoFeNiCu Decomposition Enthalpy
items.summary: Graph neural networks (GNNs) show promise for predicting materials properties, but interpretability remains a challenge, particularly understanding whether attributed feature importance reflects physical reality or statistical artifacts. Here, we present a methods validation study that deliberately overfits a physics-aware GNN ensemble to probe the robustness of feature-ranking approaches. Using the CoMoFeNiCu high-entropy alloy system with three stoichiometries, we train GNNs to predict decomposition enthalpies from DFT-calculated structures while explicitly constraining output weights to encode feature importance. By design, our dataset is limited (approximately 900 binary and 4,500 ternary decomposition pathways) to control compositional complexity and enable precise interrogation of local chemistry effects.
items.author: Miguel Tenorio, James Chapman

items.title: Tunable Hybridization of Whispering Gallery Modes in High-Index Photonic Molecules
items.summary: Photonic molecules formed by coupled dielectric microresonators provide a platform for controlling collective optical modes, yet the interplay between molecular topology, resonator detuning, and dielectric environment in determining their spectral response remains insufficiently quantified. Here, we systematically quantify the evolution of Whispering Gallery Mode (WGM) hybridization in high-index TiO$_2$ and perovskite coated TiO$_2$ microresonators with molecular topology, and establish the corresponding effective inter-cavity coupling using a combined numerical and analytical analysis. We further show that perovskite-shell incorporation provides a diameter and thickness-dependent modification of the effective coupling, producing a non-monotonic response rather than a uniform suppression of coupling. Despite the resulting closely spaced hybridized resonances in the high-index perovskite environment, the supermodes remain spectrally resolvable, with $Q$-factor of order \(10^3\) for representative modes.
items.author: Ayusmin Panda, Birabar Ranjit Kumar Nanda

items.title: The State Is Not the Bottleneck: A Paged-State Gated-DeltaNet Tile on a Tri-Mode Multicast Mesh, Bit-Exact from RTL to Silicon
items.summary: Linear-attention language models replace a growing key-value cache with a recurrent state of fixed size. On an edge FPGA, this state can exceed the on-chip memory and must be paged to external memory. This paper asks whether such paging dominates the cost of decoding (generating tokens). We built a hardware tile that computes one complete layer of a custom 369-million-parameter hybrid Gated DeltaNet model on an Agilex 5 FPGA and pages its recurrent state. The model state needs 6.2 MiB, whereas the device has 0.87 MiB of block memory. Paging adds 26.0 MB of memory traffic per decoded token, at most 11.2 percent of the calculated total.
items.author: Cong Xu, Ravi Sankar

items.title: Graph diffusion transformer for interpretable generation and inverse design of disordered atomic structures
items.summary: Atomic disorder offers a potent degree of freedom to tailor material properties, yet the resulting vast configuration space obscures structure-property relations and hinders rational inverse design. Here we introduce Graph Amorphous Diffusion Transformer (GaDiT), a generative model that combines dynamic periodic graphs, masked conditioning and an interval-weighted training-noise distribution. GaDiT generates high-quality disordered structures while accelerating sampling by two orders of magnitude compared with existing corrector-based approaches, as demonstrated across two-dimensional amorphous carbon and three-dimensional amorphous silicon and silica. Moreover, GaDiT supports conditional generation under single or combined structural features, physical properties and preparation conditions in a unified model, and enables inverse design that expands accessible structure-property ranges beyond the training distribution.
items.author: Jiani Hu, Chenyan Wang, Yongkun Yang et al.

items.title: Gravitational Corrections to OPE Coefficients
items.summary: The short-distance singular behavior of correlation functions of quantum field theories in curved spacetime is a universal property shared by all well-behaved states (known as Hadamard states). For two-point functions this takes the form of the Hadamard tail of free scalars and its generalizations to spinning fields and interacting theories. In this work, we compute similar universal curvature corrections to curved-space OPE coefficients in a short-distance expansion for interacting quantum field theories in general dimensions. We work at leading order in the curvature but for arbitrary backgrounds. Examples include weakly coupled scalar field theories with cubic and quartic interactions as well as strongly coupled conformal field theories.
items.author: Ameya Chavda, Alessandro Podo, John Staunton

items.title: Number fluctuations and particle loss in Dicke superradiance
items.summary: Dicke superradiance, the collective spontaneous emission of identical quantum emitters into a common reservoir, produces a burst with a characteristic delay $t_{\mathrm{SR}}$ and a peak intensity that scales quadratically with the emitter number $N$. This strong dependence makes the burst sensitive to how many emitters actually participate. In experiments, however, this number is rarely fixed: it fluctuates between preparations and decreases during emission through atom loss. Here we extend the analytical treatment of superradiance to variable emitter numbers using the Schwinger-boson mapping of the collective spin onto two bosonic modes. In this formulation, collective decay annihilates an atom in the excited-state mode and creates one in the ground-state mode.
items.author: Christian Niehof, Nico S. Bassler, Claudiu Genes

items.title: Uniaxial strain induces $d$-wave phonon chirality in ferroelectric BaTiO$_3$
items.summary: Circularly dichroic resonant inelastic x-ray scattering has revealed electrically switchable $g$-wave phonon chirality in freestanding BaTiO$_3$ membranes. Here, we show from first principles that uniaxial strain changes the angular class of this texture. Lowering $C_{4v}$ to $C_{2v}$ adds a $d$-wave helicity that is bilinear in the orthorhombic strain $η$ and the polarization, with nodal lines along the stress axis. For the 38~meV branches at $η=1\%$, we find that (i) along the diagonal, where the helicity vanishes by symmetry without strain, it reaches about 60\% of the unstrained maximum, and (ii) at the measured wave vectors off the mirror it is reduced by more than half.
