items.title: Integrated optical isolators enabled by 2D semiconductors via spin-momentum locking
items.summary: Integrated optical isolators based on spin-momentum locking hold great potential for protecting photonic integrated circuits from unwanted reflections. Currently, the most common implementations are magneto-optical isolators that require an externally applied magnetic field. Nevertheless, a wide range of nonreciprocal effects remains to be exploited in alternative material platforms. Although the majority of these effects induce changes to the propagation of light as a function of its polarization, they can be directly connected to the propagation direction through spin-momentum locking. We employ a computational approach to investigate various designs of integrated isolators based on nonreciprocal 2D semiconductors, studying the influence of their geometry and optical properties on the device performance.
items.author: Fernando Martín-Romero, Víctor J. Gómez, Alberto G. Curto

items.title: Still the one: Transcriptional control across leukopoiesis by SPI1/PU.1.
items.summary: The transcription factor (TF) SPI1 (historically called PU.1) is a critical pioneer TF and regulator of hematopoiesis. It exerts exquisitely dose-dependent and stage-specific control over lymphoid, myeloid, and central nervous system-resident lineages. Structurally characterized by an intrinsically disordered N-terminal transactivation region and a highly conserved C-terminal DNA-binding E26 transformation-specific domain, SPI1 can operate alone as a monomer, via homodimerization, through epigenetic interactions, and in context-dependent transcriptional partnerships. While early animal models established its essentiality for leukopoiesis, modern human genomics has unveiled direct links between altered SPI1 function and disease. Heterozygous loss-of-function germline variants cause PU.1-mediated agammaglobulinemia, whereas somatic mutations and/or regulatory alterations can drive hematologic malignancies.
items.author: Mackie J, Sim S, Cominsky LY, Nigrovic PA, Romberg N.

items.title: Severe dengue: Are type I interferon autoantibodies involved?
items.summary: Dengue virus (DENV) is the most rapidly disseminating arbovirus worldwide. A new study by Yang et al. (https://doi.org/10.70962/jhi.20260072) shows that autoantibodies neutralizing type I IFNs (AAN-I-IFN) may underlie severe dengue in ∼14% (7/49) of cases in a cohort of Chinese patients. Further studies of children and adults of different ancestries with silent, benign, and severe DENV infection are warranted.
items.author: Tran VL, Borghesi A, Casanova JL, Zhang SY.

items.title: Heterogeneous patterning behavior emerges from human stem cell-based embryo model.
items.summary: Undergoing complex self-organization, two-dimensional gastruloids derived from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) are a scalable model system to study developmental processes. However, gastruloid heterogeneity has been obscured by technological limitations. A microraft-based assay was developed to screen, sort, and sequence individual living gastruloids expressing germ layer reporters to quantify the emergence of gastruloid variability. In this proof-of-concept study, distinct patterning trajectories were identified from latent representations using time-series imaging combined with self-supervised deep learning. End point gene expression of isolated single gastruloids was measured to further evaluate heterogeneity and link phenotype to gene expression. The computational analysis captured nuanced technical and biological differences among individual gastruloids across and within batches.
items.author: Jan I, Evarts JI, Cain JY, Chiu PH, Yang M, Bagheri N, Allbritton NL.

items.title: Age modifies recurrence risk across the 2025 American Thyroid Association risk stratification in papillary thyroid carcinoma.
items.summary: Context The 2025 American Thyroid Association (ATA) guidelines updated recurrence risk stratification for papillary thyroid cancer (PTC). Whether age modifies the absolute structural recurrence risk represented by these strata is unclear. Objective To determine whether age modifies 5-year structural recurrence risk across ATA 2025 stratification in PTC and improves risk prediction. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 14 397 patients with PTC who underwent initial surgery at a tertiary cancer center in China from 2000 to 2018. The primary outcome was 5-year structural recurrence-free survival. Cox models with restricted cubic splines evaluated age effects and ATA2025-by-age interaction. ATA-based and age-interaction models were compared by temporal validation and decision-curve analysis.
items.author: Qin L, Liu Y, Zhang X, Yan D, Liu J, Liu W, Ni S, Huang H, Liu S.

items.title: Cardiovascular Implications of QTc Prolongation in Dialysis.
items.summary: Cardiovascular Implications of QTc Prolongation in Dialysis. QT prolongation is associated with increased mortality in both dialysis patients and the general population, although its comparative prognostic significance remains uncertain. Serial QTc assessment, consideration of dialysis-related electrolyte changes, and structural cardiac evaluation may improve cardiovascular risk stratification in patients undergoing dialysis.
items.author: Mısgınova S, Görenek B.

items.title: Evaluating a large language model-powered system for semi-structured interview in health research.
items.summary: Objectives Conducting qualitative health research with marginalized populations presents persistent challenges related to trust, disclosure, and resource constraints. Traditional in-person interviews can be costly and difficult to scale, while participants may hesitate to share sensitive experiences openly. This study assessed the feasibility and acceptability of a large language model (LLM)-powered conversational interview system as an alternative to semi-structured qualitative interviews with marginalized populations in a community-engaged health research context. Materials and methods We developed a web-based, LLM-powered interview system informed by a community-based participatory research framework. The system was tested with 28 caregivers of children with asthma living in subsidized housing.
items.author: Currie J, Liu M, Chung JE, He L, Li J, Panthi A, Rai R, Sedhain B, Riche C, Kasule O.

items.title: GOntact: using chromatin contacts to infer target genes and Gene Ontology enrichments for cis- regulatory elements.
items.summary: Cis -regulatory elements (CREs) can be efficiently predicted genome-wide, but identifying their target genes remains challenging. Regulatory interactions between genes and CREs can take place over long genomic distances, often bypassing genes. Inferring CRE targets based on genomic proximity, as traditionally done in genomic studies, can thus be misleading. Thanks to chromosome conformation capture techniques, chromatin contacts between CREs and gene promoters can be assayed at the genome-wide scale, thus permitting more accurate predictions of CRE target genes. Here, we present a standalone computational tool and webserver named GOntact, which infers CRE target genes using chromosome conformation capture data. GOntact can be used to derive Gene Ontology (GO) enrichments for CRE sets, thus providing a basis for functional interpretation.
items.author: Laverré A, Tannier E, Veber P, Necsulea A.

items.title: Equipoise for Laminoplasty Versus Fusion for Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy: Is a Randomized Trial Feasible?
items.summary: Background and objectives There is global variation and uncertainty regarding the utilization of laminoplasty in the treatment of patients with degenerative cervical spondylotic myelopathy. We asked whether clinical equipoise can be established among cervical spine surgeon experts for a possible trial comparing laminoplasty with fusion. Methods Fifty randomly selected cases from a cervical spondylotic myelopathy trial [NCT-02076113] were presented to 26 cervical spine experts to determine the suitability of randomization to laminoplasty vs fusion surgery. A brief clinical vignette, sagittal T2-weighted MRI, and appropriate axial images were reviewed by the experts. Each expert assessed the randomizability of each case and then stated the choice of approach: laminoplasty, fusion (anterior or posterior), arthroplasty, or no surgery.
items.author: Ghogawala Z, Rizvi TZ, Liesching ME, Adkins RD, Wang MY, Mummaneni PV, Resnick DK, Harrop JS, Michael FG, Riew KD, Albert TJ, Whitmore RG, Tumialan LM, Hoh DJ, Falavigna A, Patel AA, Arnold PM, Traynelis VC, Ray WZ, Steinmetz MP, Magge SN, Chou D, Ludwig SC, Bydon M, Rajshekhar V, Rhee JM, Combalia A, Vleggeert-Lankamp C, Wang MC, Kanter AS, Holly LT, Lawrence BD, Wang LX, Mroz T, Shaffrey CI, Heller JG.

items.title: Single Center, Single-Group Trial to Evaluate the Safety and Feasibility of 50 Hz Stimulation to Enhance Stroke Recovery of Upper Limb Function: The Motor Recovery Through Plasticity-Inducing Cortical Stimulation Open-Loop Protocol.
items.summary: Background and objectives A previous study (the Everest trial) of epidural cortical stimulation showed improved rehabilitation outcomes in a subset of those with poststroke related disability as long as (1) the individual had a degree of surviving corticospinal tracts and (2) an electrode that when delivering stimulation could evoke a motor response. The goal of this study is to examine the safety and feasibility of new sense-and-stim capable implantable devices with configurable electrode arrays, using subdural stimulation, to improve stroke rehabilitation and associated motor functional outcomes. Methods We will implant 4 patients who have chronic upper limb impairment after stroke to (1) demonstrate the safe usage of a cortical sensing-enabled stimulation system in a stroke rehabilitation protocol and (2) evaluate the system's capability to deliver activity-triggered stimulation for future clinical studies using neuroplasticity-inducing stimulation to enhance stroke rehabilitation outcomes.
items.author: Herron JA, Cho H, Robert-Gonzalez A, Bahadori-Nejad M, Wohns N, Friedman GN, Fu J, Bi P, D'Souza S, Anderson A, Wright DR, Bunnell AE, Mazwi N, Perlmutter SI, Creutzfeldt CJ, Tirschwell DL, Klein E, Weaver KE, Grannan BL, Ko AL, Moritz CT, Cramer SC, Ojemann JG.

items.title: Preoperative Stereotactic Radiotherapy for Spinal Metastases: Study Protocol for a Prospective Exploratory Interventional Trial.
items.summary: Background and objectives Spinal metastases frequently require surgical stabilization and/or decompression followed by postoperative radiotherapy (RT). Preoperative stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) may reduce postoperative complications and improve local tumor control. The primary objective of this exploratory trial is to evaluate safety and preliminary efficacy of preoperative SBRT in patients with spinal metastases. Methods The Preoperative Stereotactic Radiotherapy for Spinal Metastases study is a single-center, prospective, exploratory, interventional trial that will enroll 20 patients scheduled for surgical treatment of spinal metastases at University Medical Center Göttingen. Patients will receive SBRT (1-3 fractions) performed 1 to 3 days before surgery. The primary endpoint is local tumor control at 3 months after surgery.
items.author: Zwerenz CM, Asendorf T, Younes B, Huckhagel T, Weiser L, Lehmann W, Rieken S, Oelmann JT, Hille A, Dröge LH, Bendrich S, Guhlich M, Donath S, Fischer LA, Schmitt D, Rohde V, El Shafie R, Abboud T.

items.title: Breast Morphology, Volume, and Ptosis Patterns in Pakistani Women: An Anthropometric Study.
items.summary: Background Anthropometric breast data are crucial for planning aesthetic and reconstructive breast surgery. The purpose of this study is to evaluate baseline breast anthropometric measurements, breast volume, and assess patterns of breast ptosis in Pakistani women. Methods From October 2023 to February 2024, a multicenter cross-sectional study was carried out with 198 women 16-60 years of age having a body mass index of 25-32 kg/m 2 . Volume was calculated using Qiao's anthropometric formula, and ptosis was graded using Regnault classification. Statistical analysis involved Spearman rho (ρ), Mann-Whitney U tests, and multiple linear regression with significance set at P Results Median breast volume was 628 cm 3 .
items.author: Khan S, Kamran H, Naeem MAB, Zain M, Raza M, Mehmood H, Umair M, Asif M, Mustansir M, Rani S, Amjad N, Aminpoor H, Aimen UE, Suhail A.

items.title: Recurrent Multi-territory Thromboembolism As the Initial Presentation of Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma and Suspected Nonbacterial Thrombotic Endocarditis.
items.summary: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE), also known as Marantic endocarditis, is an uncommon complication of malignancy that may cause systemic embolization. We report a 74-year-old woman who developed a right gastrocnemius deep vein thrombosis followed by recurrent right middle cerebral artery occlusions requiring two mechanical thrombectomies. Her subsequent course was complicated by further deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and acute limb ischemia. Repeat echocardiography demonstrated mitral valve vegetations, initially raising concern for infective endocarditis. However, repeated blood cultures and cultures of retrieved thrombotic material were negative. Imaging revealed widespread metastatic disease, and biopsy of a left supraclavicular lymph node confirmed metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
items.author: Alsammak R, Ferry P.

items.title: Outcomes and Trends in Pediatric Orthognathic Surgery.
items.summary: Background This study compares risk factors, complication rates, and perioperative outcomes among pediatric patients undergoing Le Fort I osteotomy (LF1), mandibular osteotomy (MO), bimaxillary osteotomy (BMO), or Le Fort I with distraction osteogenesis (LF1+DO). Methods We conducted a retrospective review of the National Surgical Quality Improvement Program Pediatrics database from 2018 to 2023, including patients aged 5-18 years who underwent an orthognathic procedure. The primary outcome was unplanned readmission or reoperation. Secondary outcomes included total hospital length of stay, operative time, and blood loss. Results A total of 1203 patients met inclusion criteria: LF1 (n = 651), BMO (n = 294), MO (n = 190), and LF1+DO (n = 68).
items.author: Ahdoot AI, Massenburg BB, Kanack MD.

items.title: Controlled Tensioning Medial Patellofemoral Ligament Augmentation Using Double-Tape Suture and Arthroscopic Lateral Soft-Tissue Release for Patellar Instability.
items.summary: Overtensioning the medial patellofemoral ligament during reconstruction is a key cause of patellofemoral overload, anterior knee pain, and limited flexion. We present a reproducible, tension-calibrated augmentation technique using a single 4.75-mm SwiveLock anchor preloaded with double FiberTape and sutures-eliminating graft harvest. This technique is intended as an augmentation rather than a full ligament substitution. The staged fixation strategy, combined with arthroscopic evaluation and selective lateral release, serves to minimize the risk of medial overconstraint. The anchor is placed at the Schöttle point, and sutures are passed subcapsularly to the medial patella, exiting through two 2.5-mm transverse bone tunnels. Initial lateral knot fixation is performed, followed by stepwise lateral release and vastus lateralis detachment to relieve residual lateral tension.
items.author: Tan HY, Luo YF, Zeng JH, Huang P, Jin S, Deng XH, Zhang ZZ, Lin NH, Zhou AY, Chen Z.

items.title: Scalpel Versus Geometric Electron Modulation Electrocautery in Thyroid and Parathyroid Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.summary: Background Postoperative scarring is an important concern following thyroid and parathyroid surgery. Geometric electron modulation (GEM) electrocautery is designed to reduce tissue injury while providing effective hemostasis. However, evidence regarding its long-term cosmetic outcomes remains limited. This study compares long-term scar quality following cervical incisions created using GEM electrocautery versus a conventional scalpel. Methods In this prospective, randomized, self-controlled trial, 24 patients undergoing thyroidectomy or parathyroidectomy were enrolled. Each half of the cervical incision was randomly assigned to GEM electrocautery or conventional scalpel. Intraoperative blood loss, incision time, and surgical field clarity were recorded. Scar quality was assessed at 2 weeks and at 1, 3, and 12 months using the Thai linear version of the Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale.
items.author: Pojkhamkam T, Supanakorn V, Rawangban W, Tangjaturonrasme N, Samuckkeethum W.

items.title: Development of isourea-based covalent GPX4 inhibitors and structure-activity relationship analysis in ferroptosis induction.
items.summary: Ferroptosis holds significant promise for cancer therapeutics. While inhibition of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), a central intrinsic defense against ferroptosis, is sufficient to induce this process in cancer cells, the scarcity of bioavailable GPX4 inhibitors has hindered both mechanistic studies in vivo and therapeutic exploration. Furthermore, the absence of a well-defined ligand-binding pocket and the high intrinsic reactivity of traditional covalent chemotypes complicate inhibitor optimization. Inspired by the SN 2 -like geometry of the oxidative step in GPX4 catalysis, we developed a heterobenzylic isourea as a tunable leaving group for covalent GPX4 inhibitor design. Systematic variation of the isourea substituent, heteroaromatic scaffold, conformational rigidity, distal side chain, and stereochemistry established comprehensive structure-activity relationships.
items.author: Lu Y, Pan Z, Bai L, Xiao S, Gu X, Li J, Shi W, Zhang X, Liu S, Lu C, Zhou Z, Ma R, Xu Y, Tan Q, Qu H, Hu D, Liu B, Fan L, Yao H, Chen Z, Fan W, Qian Q, Cao J, Hou W, Li Q, Wei C, Zeng W, Naowarojna N, Yu J, Wang Y, Zou Y.

items.title: Posterior Tibial Slope Is Not Associated With Failure After Medial Meniscus Posterior Root Tear Repair at a Minimum 2-Year Follow-Up.
items.summary: Purpose To examine the relation between posterior tibial slope (PTS) and failure after medial meniscus posterior root tear (MMPRT) repair. Methods Patients who underwent isolated primary arthroscopic transtibial pullout MMPRT repair between 2012 and 2022 at a single institution and with a minimum 2-year follow-up were retrospectively identified. Patients were grouped into high (PTS ≥ 12°), intermediate (PTS 8°-11°), and low (PTS ≤ 7°) categories. Failure was defined as repeat ipsilateral knee arthroscopy or conversion to knee arthroplasty. A Kaplan-Meier curve and log-rank test were employed to analyze the relation between PTS and MMPRT repair failure. Results A total of 74 patients (77% women) with a mean age of 52.3 ± 9.3 years (range 23.5-73.3 years) with a minimum 2-year follow-up were identified.
items.author: Rock C, Myers RJ, Agner KE, Al Janabi H, Abdelshahid M, Nowell J, Barker T, Kaeding CC, Magnussen RA, Flanigan DC, Apseloff NA.

items.title: Long-Term Real-World Effectiveness and Safety of Recombinant ADAMTS13 in Congenital Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura: A Multicenter Retrospective Follow-Up Study in Poland.
items.summary: Background Congenital thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (cTTP) is an ultrarare, inherited thrombotic microangiopathy caused by severe ADAMTS13 deficiency. Recombinant ADAMTS13 (rADAMTS13) provides targeted enzyme replacement, offering an alternative to plasma-based prophylaxis. Although clinical trials have demonstrated encouraging outcomes, evidence regarding long-term effectiveness and safety in routine clinical practice remains limited. This study evaluated extended hematological outcomes, acute thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) events, treatment continuity, and safety during rADAMTS13 prophylaxis. Methods This multicenter retrospective observational study included 10 patients with cTTP treated at 5 specialist centers in Poland. Nine patients belonged to a previously published cohort, and one additional patient was included.
items.author: Laguna A, Szczepanska M, Pietrys D, Wojdalska M, Trembecka-Dubel E, Jazdon M, Balwierz W, Laguna P.

items.title: Hydrothermally synthesised Nd 2 Te 4 O 11 nanosheets for broadband visible light photodetection and optical switching application.
items.summary: Wide-bandgap semiconducting materials are essential for improving electronic devices and energy storage applications. As rare-earth tellurium oxides belong to the wide-bandgap group, they will be impactful for optoelectronic applications. Neodymium oxotellurate (IV) (NTO) samples were synthesized via the hydrothermal method, with varying concentrations of Nd and Te. We varied the concentration ratios of Nd and Te in 1 : 1, 1 : 2, and 1 : 3 proportions, and the corresponding samples were NTO-1, NTO-2, and NTO-3, respectively. The Nd 2 Te 4 O 11 structure in the monoclinic system was obtained from XRD analysis for all samples. Morphological analysis revealed nanorod and nanosheet structures, and the presence of the constituent elements was confirmed by EDX.
items.author: Sahoo M, Kumar PC, Alagarasan D, Naik R.

items.title: Exploring the open-aperture nonlinear optical and organic luminescent properties of a novel triazolium glutarate (TAG) single crystal.
items.summary: Centrosymmetric nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals were effectively grown at room temperature using the slow-evaporation solution technique. The crystal structure and lattice parameters of the grown crystal were determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SXRD), and the TAG crystal was found to be monoclinic with the space group P 2 1 / c . The active functional groups were investigated by FTIR spectroscopic analysis. The optical properties were observed at 3.3 eV with a cutoff wavelength of 413 nm, and thermal studies revealed that the grown crystal is stable up to 192 °C. Dielectric studies of the TAG crystal were conducted at room temperature in a frequency range of 100 Hz to 6 MHz.
items.author: Velayudham D, Kannan MR, Sabari Girisun TC, Vijaya Kumar T, Gunasekaran B.

items.title: Target-triggered DNAzyme hydrogels with boron-doped atomically dispersed Fe nanozymes for one-step bacterial colorimetric sensing.
items.summary: Nanozyme-based bacterial detection faces two long-standing challenges: (1) dependence on multi-step enzymatic cascades that complicate assay workflows, and (2) insufficient sensitivity originating from the intrinsic low catalytic activity of nanozymes and the lack of target pre-amplification for bacterial biomarkers. To address these bottlenecks, we construct a target-triggered DNAzyme hydrogel platform integrated with boron-doped nanozymes (HCFe-B). This platform synergistically couples stimuli-responsive hydrogel-mediated controlled-release and heteroatom-doped nanozyme engineering, enabling one-step ultrasensitive bacterial detection. Upon recognition of bacterial biomarkers, the rationally designed DNAzyme hydrogel triggers one-step nanozyme release, which fully obviates the requirement for multi-step enzymatic cascades. DFT calculations verify that boron doping lowers the energy barrier of the rate-determining O-O cleavage step for atomically dispersed Fe nanozymes, greatly boosting their peroxidase-like activity.
items.author: Ji T, Li Y, Zhang R, Zhai X, Liu R, Xu S, Luo X.

items.title: Visible-light degradation of ciprofloxacin by hierarchical Ag 3 PO 4 /CuInS 2 heterostructures: interfacial charge transfer, transformation pathways, and ecological risk context.
items.summary: Ciprofloxacin persists in aquatic environments and may contribute to antimicrobial resistance, creating demand for efficient, low-energy treatment technologies. In this study, a hierarchical flower-like Ag 3 PO 4 /CuInS 2 heterostructure was synthesized through a combined solvothermal-hydrothermal route and evaluated for visible-light-driven ciprofloxacin degradation. XRD, FTIR, Raman, XPS and elemental mapping confirmed the coexistence and interfacial coupling of cubic Ag 3 PO 4 and chalcopyrite CuInS 2 . The heterostructure consisted of faceted Ag 3 PO 4 particles integrated with flower-like CuInS 2 aggregates and exhibited a surface area of 39.22 m 2 g -1 , average pore diameter of 47.70 nm and band gap of 1.92 eV.
items.author: Oluwole AO, Mahlangu NC, Ngwenya P, Tichapondwa SM, Daramola MO, Iwarere SA.

items.title: The efficacy of upgrading rural drinking water treatment in karst areas of Chongqing: simultaneous removal of conventional pollutants and microplastics.
items.summary: Rural drinking water safety is a critical issue in China's public health sector. This study focused on typical small-scale rural water treatment plants in the karst region of southeastern Chongqing, Southwest China, and systematically compared the treatment performance of the conventional simplified coagulation-natural sedimentation-sand filtration process with that of the upgraded combined grid-flocculation-inclined tube sedimentation-submerged ultrafiltration (GF-TS-SUF) process. The removal efficiency of the processes was quantitatively assessed based on conventional parameters such as turbidity, color, iron, manganese, permanganate index, nitrate (NO 3 - ), as well as microplastics (abundance, morphology, size, polymer type), and correlations among parameters were explored. The results showed that the GF-TS-SUF process achieved substantially higher purification efficiency in this case study, with an effluent turbidity of 0.28 ± 0.02 NTU, a color of 3 ± 1 PCU, iron and manganese levels below detection limits, and a permanganate index of 1.58 ± 0.09 mg L -1 .
items.author: Li W, Xu W, Li J, Ran L, Xiang Q, Tian Y, Shao T.

items.title: Safety of Garcinia mangostana L. (mangosteen) peel extract as a novel food pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2015/2283.
items.summary: Following a request from the European Commission, the EFSA Panel on Nutrition, Novel Foods and Food Allergens (NDA) was asked to deliver an opinion on Garcinia mangostana L. (mangosteen) peel extract as a novel food (NF) pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2015/2283. The NF is a dried, hydro-alcoholic extract obtained from the peel (pericarp and skin) of the fruit of the mangosteen tree, G. mangostana L. The applicant intends to market the NF for use in food supplements, at a maximum dose of 200 mg per day. The target population proposed by the applicant is the general adult population. The NF is intended to be marketed as standardised to 44%-52% total xanthones, which includes 26%-34% α-mangostin and 2%-6% γ-mangostin.
items.author: EFSA Panel on Nutrition, Novel Foods and Food Allergens (NDA), Turck D, Bohn T, Cámara M, Castenmiller J, De Henauw S, Jos Á, Maciuk A, Mangelsdorf I, McNulty B, Naska A, Pentieva K, Siani A, Thies F, Bermano G, Dogliotti E, Heinonen M, Kukula-Koch W, Pilegaard K, Hirsch-Ernst KI, Azzollini D, Ackerl R.

items.title: Disulfide-poly(β-amino ester) nanoparticles for glutathione-responsive drug delivery.
items.summary: Stimuli-responsive polymeric nanocarriers have emerged as promising platforms for controlled drug delivery, enabling cargo release in response to specific biological signals. Among triggers, the high intracellular concentration of glutathione (GSH) offers a unique opportunity to activate redox-responsive systems through cleavage of disulfide bonds. In this work, a disulfide-containing poly(β-amino ester) (PBAE) was synthesized and conjugated with PEG to obtain block copolymers capable of spontaneous self-assembly into polymeric nanoparticles. While PBAEs have been previously established for nucleic acid delivery, their application as redox-responsive drug carriers for the physical encapsulation of small-molecule therapeutics remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that a disulfide-containing PEG-PBAE copolymer can efficiently encapsulate punicalagin (a model drug) through self-assembly, forming nanoparticles with hydrodynamic diameters below 200 nm and a near-neutral ζ -potential.
items.author: Colli C, Mullahi S, Moscatelli D, Mauri E.

items.title: Painless Takotsubo Syndrome Triggered by Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD): A Retrospective Observational Study of Seven Cases.
items.summary: Takotsubo syndrome (TS) as a manifestation of acute chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation is uncommonly reported. Emotional and adrenergic stress, hypoxemia, negative intrathoracic pressure, and the use of beta-agonists are frequently implicated in triggering myocardial dysfunction in this setting. We present a retrospective study of seven cases of TS in patients with COPD exacerbation in which none reported typical chest pain, representing a diagnostic challenge in patients with an apparent clinical justification for their dyspnea. All patients had electrocardiographic changes and elevated cardiac biomarkers, underwent echocardiography and coronary angiography or coronary computed tomography angiography, and received a confirmed diagnosis of TS.
items.author: Kirchenchtejn C, Besborodco A, Wolff Fridman M, Millner LH.

items.title: Recurrent Hypertensive Carcinoid Crisis Despite Somatostatin Analog Therapy.
items.summary: Carcinoid crisis is a rare, life-threatening complication of neuroendocrine tumors characterized by hemodynamic instability. Although hypotension is more commonly described, severe hypertension can also occur. An 84-year-old woman who had undergone resection of a grade 1 terminal ileal neuroendocrine tumor and two hepatic metastases presented with worsening flushing, severe headaches, mild wheeze, palpitations, and chest tightness. She was receiving maintenance long-acting lanreotide and had used the maximum prescribed dose of rescue subcutaneous octreotide for two weeks without sustained benefit. Her blood pressure was highly labile, with a peak systolic reading of 198 mmHg, and her heart rate reached 110 beats/min.
items.author: Ghannoum A, Young AC, Rao R.

items.title: Effectiveness of Compartmentalized Expanded Polytetrafluoroethylene 3-wire Neural Conduit for Sciatic Nerve-directed Bundle Regeneration.
items.summary: Background Peripheral nerve defects pose major reconstructive challenges when tension-free end-to-end repair is not feasible. Although autologous nerve grafting remains an ideal strategy for bridging nerve gaps, donor-site morbidity and limitations regarding graft availability stimulated the development of tissue-engineered nerve conduits. Attempting to improve fascicular guidance, compartmentalized conduit designs were proposed, promoting more organized axonal regeneration. The present study evaluates the reparative efficacy of a compartmentalized expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (e-PTFE) 3-wire neural conduit compared with established reconstructive approaches using a rat sciatic nerve injury model. Methods Seventy-one (n = 71) adult rats were allocated into 5 experimental groups. Group A received end-to-end repair following sciatic nerve transection.
items.author: Dalianoudis IG, Papastefanaki F, Tzanos IA, Apostolidou K, Vekris MD, Batistatou A, Matsas R, Lykoudis EG.

items.title: Scoping Review of Intraoperative Vasopressor Use in Free Flap-based Breast Reconstruction.
items.summary: Background Breast reconstruction by free tissue transfer has become the gold standard with excellent surgical outcomes. However, due to early research regarding intraoperative use of vasopressors in free flap surgery, microsurgeons have historically avoided vasopressor use and opted for intravenous fluids to maintain tissue perfusion during long microvascular anastomosis procedures. The purpose of this study is to comprehensively review the effect of vasopressor use on outcomes in free flap-based breast reconstruction. Methods A scoping review in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines was conducted to filter articles relevant to studies examining vasopressor agents in free flap-based breast reconstruction.
items.author: D'Elia A, Dhanoa A, Shamoun V, Hadzimustafic N, Haykal S.

items.title: Extensive Placental Abruption With Fetal Demise and Couvelaire Uterus in an Adolescent in a Low-Resource Setting: A Case Report.
items.summary: Placental abruption is a life-threatening obstetric emergency with disproportionate impact on adolescent populations, who carry elevated biological risk for hypertensive complications and poor perinatal outcomes. This case report describes a 17-year-old primigravida from the Dominican Republic who presented at 34 weeks of gestation with severe abdominal pain, decreased fetal movements, and absent fetal heart tones on auscultation. Admission ultrasonography was reported to show fetal demise and placental findings described as infarction. Emergency cesarean delivery revealed approximately 90% placental separation and hemorrhagic infiltration described as involving approximately 20% of the posterior uterine surface, consistent with Couvelaire uterus. Estimated blood loss was approximately 1300 mL, although the period covered by this estimate was not documented in the available records.
items.author: Choi MS, Laidler CR, Gonzalez Valladares KH, Sosa S, Gonzalez KA.

items.title: Presumed Cross-midline Migration of a Barbed Polydioxanone Thread to the Contralateral Upper Lip After Midface Thread Lifting.
items.summary: Thread migration is a recognized complication of facial thread lifting, but presumed cross-midline migration to the contralateral upper lip requiring surgical removal is rarely described. A 47-year-old woman underwent midface lifting with 4 Fiora barbed polydioxanone threads and lower-face lifting with 4 Tesslift polydioxanone threads. The early postoperative course was uneventful. Around 1 week later, she intermittently noticed cheek catching and a loosening sensation. On postoperative day 14, localized ecchymosis appeared at the right alar base and left lateral philtral region. On day 19, upper lip swelling, pain, and right upper lip ecchymosis developed, and a thread tip was palpable in the right upper labial mucosa.
items.author: Tachibana K, Matsui C, Maeda T, Yoshida Y, Wang S, Tie S.

items.title: Neuroevolution potentials uncover concentration-dependent Li + transport mechanisms in PEO-LiTFSI electrolytes.
items.summary: Ion transport in solid polymer electrolytes depends on local coordination, polymer segmental relaxation and collective ionic motion. Modelling ion transport across salt concentrations remains challenging because the local coordination must be accurately described while slow polymer relaxation and ionic motion are adequately sampled. Here, we combine uncertainty-guided active learning with neuroevolution potential (NEP) simulations to investigate poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO)-LiTFSI electrolytes over a broad range of salt concentrations. Trained on density functional theory reference data, the NEP reproduces local coordination, density and glass-transition-temperature trends. On the test set, the NEP achieves energy and force root mean square errors of 3.91 meV atom -1 and 132.5 meV Å -1 , respectively.
items.author: Pu X, Xu J, Hou P, Li Z, Dong H, Liu Z, Liu X, Zhu Y.

items.title: Opioid-sparing Pain Management for Pediatric Alveolar Bone Grafting: Efficacy of the Bupivacaine-soaked Absorbable Sponge.
items.summary: Background The iliac crest is the gold-standard donor site for alveolar bone grafting, yet donor-site pain often leads to increased opioid use and prolonged hospital stays. This study evaluates whether the adjunctive use of bupivacaine-soaked absorbable sponge in addition to subcutaneous local anesthesia infiltration provides improved postoperative pain management compared with local anesthetic alone. Methods Medical records of consecutive patients who underwent alveolar bone grafting between January 2023 and September 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were grouped based on whether they received bupivacaine-soaked absorbable sponge with local anesthetic (sponge group, N = 28) or subcutaneous local anesthetic alone (no-sponge group, N = 38).
items.author: Tang EA, Ravamehr-Lake D, Nezerwa Y, Munshey F, Joachim K, Fisher DM, Phillips JH, Podolsky DJ, Riesel JN, Wong Riff KWY.

items.title: Delayed Extensor Apparatus Reconstruction for Post-Burn Digital Extension Loss in a Pediatric Patient.
items.summary: Late sequelae of pediatric hand burns may include occult damage to the digital extensor apparatus beneath healed scar tissue. The digital extensor apparatus is a complex anatomical system composed of interconnected components that function together to produce coordinated finger extension at interphalangeal joints. Injury to this system may remain clinically unrecognized during acute burn management and present later as isolated extension loss despite preserved joint suppleness. We report the case of a 10-year-old girl who presented 2 years after a flame burn involving the dorsum of the left hand with inability to actively extend the index and middle fingers. Clinical examination demonstrated absent active extension at the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints, whereas passive motion, sensation, and vascularity were preserved.
items.author: Bhatnagar A, Bhatnagar A.

items.title: Open Surgical Management of Permanent Synthetic Fillers of the Buttocks: Principles, Outcomes, and Reconstructive Considerations.
items.summary: Background Permanent synthetic fillers provide immediate aesthetic results but may cause substantial local, systemic, immunologic, and reconstructive complications. We describe standardized surgical principles for their management and removal in the gluteal region. Permanent synthetic fillers included liquid silicone, biopolymer mixtures, methacrylate-derived compounds, industrial oils, and other nonbiocompatible injectable materials identified clinically, radiologically, or histopathologically. Methods A retrospective longitudinal cohort study evaluated patients undergoing open gluteal permanent synthetic filler removal from 2017 to 2024. The meticulous approach safer and keeper technique has been used since 2014 and the butterfly wing technique since 2004. Clinical, hematologic, immunologic, metabolic, and radiologic variables were assessed preoperatively and through 1 year postoperatively.
items.author: Pachón Suárez JE, Santos Gutiérrez IA, Rizo Tello VZ, Salazar MC, Rosales Solano DE.

items.title: AI-guided prioritization of potential FAM171A2 ligands through pharmacophore-aware and receptor-based screening.
items.summary: FAM171A2 has recently emerged as a potential therapeutic target in Parkinson's disease because it selectively recognizes α-synuclein fibrils and promotes their neuronal uptake. However, ligand prioritization for this receptor remains challenging because of scarce known binders, the absence of an experimentally resolved ligand-bound structure and the requirement for blood-brain barrier permeability. Here, we established an AI-guided computational screening framework that integrates pharmacophore-aware retrieval, hierarchical receptor-based screening, blood-brain barrier permeability prediction and molecular dynamics-based assessment to prioritize potential FAM171A2 ligands. Starting from 1.41 million compounds, the workflow progressively narrowed the search space to two structurally representative candidates, E634-1386 and F707-2364. Both candidates showed more favorable in silico profiles than the reference blocker Bemcentinib across complementary computational assessments: E634-1386 achieved higher KarmaDock and CarsiDock scores, whereas F707-2364 yielded the most favorable AutoDock Vina score and MM/GBSA estimate.
items.author: Yan B, Lu Y, Tong Y, Lin S, Li W.

items.title: Severe gastric distension in a teenage boy.
items.summary: A 16-year-old male presented with acute abdominal pain, nausea, and distension and was found to have severe gastric dilation on imaging. Antroduodenal manometry showed erythromycin-induced phase 3 migrating motor complex beginning in the antrum but post-prandial antral hypoactivity. Mitochondrial DNA sequencing was normal. Exome analysis revealed a rare variant of uncertain significance in the smooth muscle myosin heavy chain 11 ( MYH11 ) gene (NM_002474.3: c.4123G>A, p.Asp1375Asn), which is necessary for smooth muscle contraction. Pathogenic MYH11 alterations cause multiple disorders, including autosomal dominant (AD) familial thoracic aortic aneurysm, AD visceral myopathy, and autosomal recessive megacystis-microcolon-intestinal-hypoperistalsis syndrome. Amino acid p.Asp1375 is within the rod region of the MYH11 protein that self-assembles to form thick filaments; thus, pathogenic variants in this region may affect filament formation and impair interactions with thin filaments.
items.author: Chang E, Wolfson S, Heuckeroth RO, Medne L, Nomakuchi TT, Murrell J, Reichert SL, Weckselblatt B, Webster J.

items.title: Vanishing act: A case report of atovaquone-proguanil-induced vanishing bile duct syndrome in a pediatric patient.
items.summary: Drug-induced vanishing bile duct syndrome (VBDS) is a rare complication of severe cholestatic hepatitis characterized by progressive ductopenia despite withdrawal of the offending agent. Prognosis ranges from gradual recovery to liver failure requiring transplantation. We report the first known pediatric case of biopsy-confirmed VBDS following atovaquone-proguanil exposure. An 11-year-old girl developed severe cholestatic hepatitis approximately 2 months after a 21-day course of malaria prophylaxis. Liver biopsy demonstrated marked ductopenia, with bile ducts identified in only 2 of 22 portal tracts. Despite a severe presentation, she achieved complete biochemical and clinical recovery within 6 months. This case expands the spectrum of drug-induced VBDS in children and highlights the potential for favorable outcomes despite significant duct loss.
items.author: Kaihlanen K, Pottorff A, Goyal A, Rakheja D, Scheuerle AE, Rojas I.

items.title: Beyond clinical training: Addressing financial literacy gaps in pediatric gastroenterology fellowship.
items.author: Ekezie C, Lee R, Chugh A.

items.title: Synthesis route-dependent structural and electrochemical properties of La 0.63 Ga 0.37 Mo 0.74 Fe 0.26 O 3-δ symmetrical electrodes for intermediate-temperature SOFCs.
items.summary: This study carefully explores the impact of synthesis route on the structural, optical and electrochemical properties of La 0.63 Ga 0.37 Mo 0.74 Fe 0.26 O 3-δ (LGMF) as a symmetrical electrode for intermediate temperature solid oxide fuel cells (IT-SOFCs). The LGMF material was synthesized via four distinct routes such as sol-gel, hydrothermal, co-precipitation and solid-state methods. The detailed characterization of the prepared materials revealed strong dependence of phase formation route, crystallinity and band gap. X-ray diffraction (XRD) and Raman spectra confirmed the formation of crystalline perovskite-related phases, with the co-precipitation and sol gel routes exhibiting improved crystallinity and structural homogeneity.
items.author: Gulzar H, Ghauri MW, Shareef MS, Javed S, Ahmad MA, Khan MA, Shakir I, Almohammedi A, Raza R, Abbas G.

items.title: Carbon quantum dot-based nanoplatforms for cancer therapy and photodynamic therapy: emerging strategies for targeting cancer and cancer stem cells.
items.summary: With cancer's rising incidence and mortality rates expected to increase sharply by 2030, cancer continues to be a major worldwide health concern. Drug resistance, non-specific toxicity, and the persistence of cancer stem cells (CSCs), which cause tumor recurrence, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance, frequently limit conventional therapies. Although photodynamic therapy (PDT) provides a less intrusive option, tumor hypoxia, low photosensitizer (PS) selectivity, and restricted light penetration limit its therapeutic usefulness. Because of their remarkable optical characteristics, biocompatibility, adjustable surface chemistry, and inherent photosensitizing powers, carbon quantum dots (CQDs) have become a viable nanoplatform for cancer treatment. This review offers a comprehensive synthesis of current developments in CQD-based PDT for CSC and cancer cell targeting.
items.author: Kah G, Abrahamse H.

items.title: Extraction of critical metals from chrysotile asbestos tailings via an ammonium sulfate roasting-water leaching process.
items.summary: Chrysotile asbestos tailings (CATs) are hazardous industrial wastes that contain substantial amounts of valuable critical metals, including Mg, Fe, and Ni. This study investigates the co-extraction of these metals from CATs using an ammonium sulfate ((NH 4 ) 2 SO 4 ) roasting-water leaching process. Key process parameters, including (NH 4 ) 2 SO 4 dosage, roasting temperature, and roasting time, were systematically optimized to maximize the leaching efficiencies of Mg, Fe, and Ni. The phase transformations and microstructural evolution during roasting were characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and thermogravimetric analysis (TG). Under the optimal conditions, the leaching efficiencies of Mg, Fe, and Ni all exceeded 93%.
items.author: Gan H, Zhou X, Su F.

items.title: A highly dynamic active state for transducin-bound phosphodiesterase-6 in vertebrate phototransduction.
items.summary: In vertebrate phototransduction, the G protein-coupled receptor rhodopsin activates the α-subunit of transducin (Gα T ), which, upon binding the γ-subunits of phosphodiesterase-6 (PDE6), stimulates cGMP hydrolysis. We reported a cryoEM structure for a complex containing two constitutively active Gα T (Gα T *) subunits coupled by a bivalent antibody bound to PDE6 that demonstrated a striking displacement of both PDEγ subunits from the PDEα/PDEβ catalytic sites and suggested an alternating-site mechanism for PDE6 activation. Here, we use site-directed spin labeling and double electron-electron resonance spectroscopy (DEER) to probe PDE6 conformational changes upon Gα T * binding. PDEγ spin labeled on Cys68 and Ile64Cys demonstrate that PDEγ have highly flexible C-termini that transiently bind to the PDEα/PDEβ heterodimer.
items.author: Holechek JN, Shang JY, Assafa TE, Crane BR, Cerione RA.

items.title: A dual-barrier sustained-release hydrogel based on Cu-exchanged Y zeolite and sodium alginate for infected wound healing.
items.summary: Bacterial wound infection and the growing crisis of antibiotic resistance urgently demand non-antibiotic wound dressings that integrate long-term antibacterial activity and high biosafety. Herein, we designed a dual-barrier sustained-release antibacterial hydrogel (CuY@SA) by embedding Cu 2+ -exchanged Y zeolite (CuY) into a calcium-crosslinked sodium alginate (SA) matrix. The ordered microporous zeolite acts as the first-stage reservoir to enable intrinsic Cu 2+ sustained release via ion exchange, while the alginate network serves as a second physical diffusion barrier to suppress burst release and prolong delivery. The resulting CuY@SA hydrogel eliminated the initial burst and achieved nearly-linear Cu 2+ release over 48 h, with an equilibrium swelling ratio of approximately 28 g g -1 in pH 7.4 PBS.
items.author: Rao Y, Yu X, Xu K, Zheng L, Pu S, Wen N, Wang P, Lin W.

items.title: A dual-function Cu-MOF-polyaniline nanorod composite for efficient water splitting and enhanced capacitive energy storage.
items.summary: In the present study, we synthesized a composite material comprising a copper-based metal-organic framework (Cu-MOF) (BDC) integrated with polyaniline (Pani) nanorods for dual applications in water splitting and capacitive energy storage. The material was characterized using a range of techniques, including X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), ultraviolet-visible (UV-vis) spectroscopy, thermal analysis, scanning electron microscopy-energy dispersive X-ray analysis (SEM-EDAX), and surface mapping. The electrochemical performance for water splitting was evaluated for both the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER). The Cu-Pani-NR composite exhibited an overpotential at a current density of 10 mA cm -2 ( η 10 ) of 196 mV for HER and 160 mV for OER.
items.author: Al-Qahtani SD, Hefnawy MA, Al-Senani GM, Al-Fawzan FF, Ahmed HA, Alkhalaf NI, Medany SS.

items.title: Nanocomposite engineering of aggregation-induced electrochemiluminescence for biosensing and bioanalytical applications.
items.summary: Aggregation-induced electrochemiluminescence (AIECL) is a technique that integrates aggregation-induced emission (AIE) with electrochemiluminescence (ECL). By circumventing the aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) effect inherent in conventional emitters, this approach delivers high emission efficiency and strong luminescence, which render it attractive for diagnostic and single-cell imaging applications. However, its broader adoption is constrained by several factors, including limited emission efficiency, complex synthetic routes, poor biocompatibility, a shortage of cathodic luminophores, and substantial reliance on co-reactants. Nanomaterials offer a promising means to alleviate these drawbacks. They promote controlled aggregation of AIE luminogens, amplify weak signals via multiple mechanisms such as energy/electron transfer and electromagnetic field effects, regulate energy-transfer pathways, and enable the integration of recognition and detection functionalities onto a single nanoscale entity.
items.author: Jia Y, Min X, Liu X, Zhou M, Yi X, Zeng W, Shen J, An C, Wang X.

items.title: A Rare Case of Cutaneous Metastases From Lung Cancer.
items.summary: We present an uncommon case of cutaneous metastasis from non-small cell lung cancer in an 88-year-old woman without systemic symptoms. The initial presentation of an ulceronodular lesion on the right arm led to the diagnosis of a metastatic lung primary, which was confirmed by histopathology and immunohistochemistry. This case illustrates the diagnostic importance of considering related internal malignancies when evaluating atypical skin lesions in elderly patients, even without systemic symptoms.
items.author: Vinjamuri S, Parisa ZT, Sarkar MAA, Alam FMT.

items.title: Synthesis, cholinesterase inhibition, antiproliferative activity, and in silico evaluation of novel hydantoin conjugates.
items.summary: A new series of novel hydantoin conjugates 3a-q was synthesized using a facile route and obtained in excellent yields. The newly synthesized conjugates were characterized using FTIR, 1 H-NMR, 13 C-NMR, and HRMS analyses, and their cholinesterase [acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE)] inhibitory and antiproliferative properties were subsequently evaluated. Among the tested compounds, 3d and 3p were identified as potent BChE inhibitors (IC 50 = 10 ± 1.43 and 18 ± 2.65 µM). To explore antiproliferative activity, all the compounds were screened against MCF7, A549, and PC3 cancer cell lines. Compound 3j displayed the most potent antiproliferative effect (IC 50 = 13.95, 16.53, and 34.62 µM, respectively) against MCF7, A549, and PC3 cancer cell lines, while 3d, 3h, 3k, and 3q also exhibited considerable cytotoxicity.
items.author: Abdullah AH, Al-Sha'er MA, Habashneh AY, Chandrasekaran B, Bardaweel SK, Hourani W, Alelaimat MA.

items.title: RETRACTION: Seasonal Coat Colour Moult and Mismatch in Ezo Mountain Hares ( Lepus timidus ainu ): Phenotypic Plasticity and Snow Cover Effects in Hokkaido, Japan.
items.summary: [This retracts the article DOI: 10.1002/ece3.74052.].

items.title: Resolving Electron-Transfer Heterogeneity in Electrochemical Aptamer-Based Sensors by Distribution of Capacitive Times.
items.summary: Distribution of timescales methods have become powerful tools for extracting hidden kinetic processes from electrochemical impedance spectra. Their physical interpretation, however, depends critically on matching the assumed mathematical model to the underlying physical electrochemical system. Here, we show that the Distribution of Capacitive Times (DCT) model is well-matched to the physics of surface-immobilized redox systems, enabling electron-transfer rate heterogeneity to be resolved. This makes electrochemical aptamer-based (EAB) sensors a natural system for DCT analysis, as their surface-tethered redox reporters can occupy distinct molecular states with different electron-transfer kinetics. Applying DCT to a vancomycin EAB biosensor reveals two distinct electron-transfer populations whose respective rates remain nearly constant as a function of vancomycin concentration.
items.author: Lansdorp BM, Gibson JM, Sepunaru L, Plaxco KW.

items.title: The Role of Light in Mediating Physiological Stress in Small Corals Exposed to Elevated Temperature.
items.summary: Marine heat waves (MHW) are important stressors on coral reefs, and evaluating their implications for the population dynamics of young corals has become a key research need. However, projecting the effects of MHW on the demographics of young corals is made difficult by an incomplete understanding of how their response to high temperature is modulated by light. Here we tested for the interactive effects of temperature and light on genetically identified colonies of the Pacific coral, Pocillopora spp. from 3-m depth in the back reef of Moorea, French Polynesia. The ecological implications of the responses to manipulated temperature and light were strengthened through context provided by long-term in situ records of temperature and light.
items.author: Edmunds PJ, Scafidi KC, Cohn F, Layagala K, Sims JA, Correa AMS, Burgess SC.

items.title: Phytoplankton seasonal succession in response to environmental drivers in the eastern English Channel: a revised Margalef Mandala for a highly turbulent region.
items.summary: Classical conceptual models or Mandalas may explain phytoplankton dynamics in ecosystems where succession from diatoms to dinoflagellates is commonly observed. In highly turbulent, diatom- Phaeocystis dominated waters of the eastern English Channel, however, these models may not be fully applicable. This study identifies environmental states and key drivers of phytoplankton seasonal succession in the eastern English Channel by integrating high-frequency hydrological and physicochemical data with low-frequency phytoplankton observations. Multilevel Spectral Clustering (M-SC) was applied to a high-frequency dataset to identify environmental states, which were then linked to a phytoplankton abundance dataset. Eight environmental states were identified, including recurrent, rare, and extreme events, revealing a succession from winter conditions dominated by tychopelagic and other diatoms (e.g.
items.author: Halawi Ghosn R, Grassi K, Poisson-Caillault E, Lefebvre A.

items.title: Engineering organic-inorganic-polymer hybrid electrolytes for transition bimetallic sulfides@MXene nanocomposites toward advanced energy storage and electrochemical sensing.
items.summary: Next-generation wearable and self-powered diagnostic systems have attracted great interest in the development of multifunctional electrode materials that can be used simultaneously for energy storage and electrochemical sensing applications. This paper reports the synthesis and physicochemical evaluation of a MXene-doped vanadium-niobium sulfide (VNbS@MXene) composite, along with a systematic evaluation of its electrochemical behavior in four different electrolyte systems, and the demonstration of dual functionality for energy storage and glucose sensing applications. The synergistic combination of high-conductivity nanosheets provides plenty of redox-active sites and high electron transport pathways, which allow the improvement of electrochemical kinetics. Electrochemical characteristics of the electrode were tested in four types of electrolyte systems, and the hybrid electrolyte design demonstrated the most desirable electrochemical characteristics, as it showed better ionic conductivity and stronger ion-electrode interactions.
items.author: Khalil S, Al-Saeedi SI, Afzal AM, Mumtaz S, El-Sabban HA.

items.title: Defect-engineered erbium iron garnet via high-pressure torsion for enhanced magnetic hyperthermia.
items.summary: High-Pressure Torsion (HPT) is a promising severe plastic deformation technique for tailoring the functional properties of magnetic materials. In this study, we investigated the impact of HPT on the magnetic and hyperthermia properties of erbium iron garnet (Er 3 Fe 5 O 12 ) particles synthesized via a sol-gel auto-combustion method. HPT processing induced significant grain refinement, reducing particles from micron-scale (∼2.3 µm) to the submicron/nanoscale (∼170-550 nm mean size), with ultra-fine fractions as small as 40 nm. While the saturation magnetization (M S ) decreased due to surface disorder, the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) improved from 2.8 W g -1 (as-synthesized) to 4.396 W g -1 (processed at 240 MPa).
items.author: Polozhentsev O, Arthur DE, Li Z, Abdulvakhidov K, Shukla N, Soldatov AV.

items.title: Researcher Analysis Toolkit for integrated and traceable evaluation of electrochemical, photoelectrochemical, and spectroscopic data.
items.summary: Electrochemical and photoelectrochemical data are often processed using several stand-alone programs, making it difficult to maintain a consistent workflow from raw data to reported results. Here, we introduce the Researcher Analysis Toolkit, a modular desktop application that brings together voltammetry, Tafel analysis, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), semiconductor and photoelectrochemical calculations, time-resolved photoluminescence fitting, optical band-gap estimation, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analysis. For EIS, the toolkit supports both user-defined circuit fitting and hierarchical screening of candidate circuits. The fitting workflow includes Lin-KK consistency testing, residual analysis, parameter-bound warnings, and approximate uncertainty and parameter-correlation diagnostics. Users retain control over fitting ranges and analysis settings, whereas calculations and data export follow a common workflow across modules.
items.author: Behroozi M, Sadighi S, Luque R, Doustkhah E.

items.title: Optimisation of the microwave-assisted extraction process and comparative phytochemical, nutritional and antimicrobial profiling of Allium stracheyi (Baker) across an altitudinal gradient.
items.summary: Allium stracheyi is an important ethnomedicinal plant species in the genus Allium , commonly used as a vegetable and spice in the Himalayan region. This study optimised microwave-assisted extraction (MAE) of A. stracheyi leaves using a Box-Behnken Design (BBD) based on Response Surface Methodology (RSM). The extraction conditions were optimised for aqueous and ethanolic solvents to maximise yield, Total Phenolic Content (TPC), and Total Flavonoid Content (TFC). A comparative analysis of phytochemical activities, antimicrobial activities, and nutritional profiling (elements, amino acids, and phenolic acids) was conducted on optimised A. stracheyi samples (collected from four different altitudes). We conducted elemental analysis using AAS, tentatively profiled bioactive compounds by GC-MS, and identified amino acids and phenolic compounds using U-HPLC.
items.author: Singh P, Semwal P, Gururani P, Bhatnagar P, Jameel Pasha SB, Thapliyal A.

items.title: One-step antimicrobial peptide immobilization technique: universal compatibility with clinical bone cements.
items.summary: Nisin-based antimicrobial peptide (AMP) immobilization represents a promising strategy for antibacterial bone cements. This one-step approach fits standard surgical workflows and addresses drawbacks of antibiotic-loaded cements, such as burst drug release, short-term antibacterial activity and compromised mechanical properties. Nevertheless, its compatibility with clinical cements for translation has not been verified. Here, we covalently anchored nisin onto three clinical cements during in situ polymerization and assessed pre-clinical performances. The modified cements maintained ISO-compliant compressive strength and MMA release profiles remained largely unaltered. They yielded 94-100% contact-killing efficacy against Staphylococcus aureus without peptide leaching. Moreover, the treated cements maintained desirable handling properties and biocompatibility.
items.author: Wang C, Lin H, Lu B, Wang X, Li Y, Li Z, Chu J, Xu Y, He F.

items.title: Corrosion behavior of polar marine steel FH40 in simulated marine environments.
items.summary: With the increasing strategic value of the Arctic Passage, corrosion behavior of polar marine steel in harsh environments has become a key issue for ship life-cycle reliability. This work systematically compares the corrosion behavior of FH40 polar marine low-temperature steel under three conditions: 20 °C immersion, 20 °C salt spray, and -60 °C immersion. Combined with EBSD characterization, the effects of environmental factors on the corrosion mechanism, product evolution, grain boundary characteristics, and dislocation density are elucidated. Results show that the corrosion mechanism is synergistically controlled by environment and temperature. Immersion at 20 °C is dominated by uniform dissolution with local pitting, while -60 °C immersion presents typical local pitting.
items.author: Hu L, Wang D, Zhao J, Wang Y, Gong X, Ding P, Chang X.

items.title: Japonindolates A-C: new indole diterpenoids from the endophytic fungus Aspergillus japonicus 334 and their anti-inflammatory activities.
items.summary: Chemical investigations on the endophytic fungus Aspergillus japonicus 334 yielded six structurally diverse indole diterpenoids (1-6) including three new compounds, namely japonindolates A-C (1-3). Their structures were elucidated by comprehensive spectroscopic analyses, including NMR, HRESIMS, electronic circular dichroism calculations, and quantum-chemical NMR calculations. The anti-inflammatory activities of compounds 1-6 were evaluated in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages and an LPS-induced inflammation model using Tg(mpx:EGFP) transgenic zebrafish larvae. In RAW264.7 macrophages, compounds 1-6 significantly reduced LPS-induced TNF-α secretion, compounds 2-4 and 6 decreased IL-1β secretion, and compounds 3-6 reduced NO production. In zebrafish larvae, compounds 2-4 and 6 significantly inhibited LPS-induced neutrophil recruitment, whereas compounds 1 and 5 showed no significant effects.
items.author: Huo LN, Hu LJ, Wang LN, Gu G, Yang Q, Sun ZQ.

items.title: Frontiers in Biophotonics.
items.summary: Biophotonics is poised to play a central role in the transition toward personalized, data-driven healthcare by enabling increasingly sensitive, quantitative, and minimally invasive measurements of biological systems. This editorial examines interconnected frontiers shaping the field, and highlights how advances across these areas can collectively accelerate clinical translation. Its perspective emphasizes education, interdisciplinary collaboration, and the development of future researchers as the foundation for converting technological progress into meaningful healthcare impact.
items.author: Komolibus K, Untracht GR, Andersson-Engels S, Andersen PE.

items.title: Text Psychometrics: Assessing psychological constructs in text using natural language processing.
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have revolutionized natural language processing (NLP). Yet when used to assess psychological constructs in text, they are generally not evaluated for the types of validity, reliability, and standardization typically expected from traditional questionnaires with rating scales. This study bridges that gap by proposing a framework for evaluating the psychometric properties of NLP-based psychological assessments (including LLMs-based ones), an area of research we refer to as Text Psychometrics. We first review different NLP methods, compare their ability to address key challenges in psychological research such as explainability, and outline ways of evaluating them on many desirable psychometric properties.
items.author: Low DM, Mair P, Nock MK, Ghosh SS.

items.title: Synthetic torpor in the rat protects the heart from ischaemia-reperfusion injury.
items.summary: During times of environmental stress, many animals enter torpor: a reversible protective physiological state typically characterised by reductions in core temperature, heart rate, and oxygen consumption. Species that naturally enter this hypothermic and hypometabolic state are tolerant of ischaemia-reperfusion injury. Consequently, there is a growing interest in utilising aspects of torpor for clinical applications such as protection from stroke or myocardial infarction. It is currently unknown, however, whether a torpor-like state is protective in animals that do not naturally enter torpor. Using viral vector-mediated chemogenetic activation of the medial preoptic area of the hypothalamus, we induced synthetic torpor in the rat, a species that does not naturally enter torpor.
items.author: Elley M, Taddei L, Ali Khan M, Wilcox UR, Hitrec T, Lewis M, Pickering AE, Ambler M.

items.title: Reply to Marciano and Rossiter: Balancing muscle oxygen consumption sampling and slope quality in NIRS-derived assessment of muscle oxidative capacity.
items.author: Costalat G, Sautillet B, Millet GP, Unal C, Abaïdia AE, Hassar A, Cozette M.

items.title: The impact of functional sagittal pelvic tilt on CT-based hip dysplasia diagnostics in adults: a cross-sectional 3D simulation study.
items.summary: Background and purpose Accurate acetabular coverage assessment is essential for diagnosing adult hip dysplasia. Computed tomography (CT) best evaluates 3-dimensional acetabular morphology but is typically acquired supine, while symptoms arise during weightbearing. This study evaluates how sagittal pelvic tilt affects CT-based acetabular parameters in adults with hip dysplasia and whether pelvic tilt causes clinically relevant measurement changes. Methods 3D-models from supine CT of 29 adults with hip dysplasia (lateral center-edge angle (LCEA) ≤ 25°) yielded 39 affected hips. LCEA, inclination (AI), anterior/posterior/horizontal acetabular sector angles (AASA, PASA, HASA), acetabular version (AV), extrusion index (EI), and total and loadbearing coverage were measured.
items.author: Hüsken MFT, Lissendorp F, Magré J, Willemsen K, Weinans H, Sakkers R, Nasrabadi J, Arbabi V, Bekkers J, Ten Ham AM, Schlösser TPC, Van der Wal BCH.

items.title: A randomized study on migration of the Spectron EF and the Charnley flanged 40 cemented femoral stems: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial using radiostereometric analysis (RSA) with 10 years' follow-up.
items.summary: Background and purpose Our primary aim was to compare the 10-year migration of the proximally roughened Spectron EF stem with the Charnley flanged 40 stems in cemented THA. Secondary aims were to assess the influence of polyethylene type on Spectron EF migration, and clinical outcomes. Methods In this randomized trial (NCT00698672), 150 patients (70% women; mean age 70 years) underwent cemented THA with either a Charnley stem (n = 30) or a Spectron EF stem (n = 120, 4 groups with different articulating surfaces). The articulations utilized conventional polyethylene (CPE) or highly crosslinked polyethylene (XLPE) cup liners combined with either cobalt-chromium (CoCr) or Oxinium (OxZr) femoral heads.
items.author: Johannessen HG, Hallan G, Furnes O, Fenstad AM, Lygre SH, Haugan K, Kadar T, Badawy M, Indrekvam K, Aamodt A, Høl PJ.

items.title: Harmonizing Dermato-Venereology Education in Europe: Digital Tools and a Scalable Learning Framework.
items.summary: Traditional models of medical education are increasingly challenged by structural and logistical constraints. In Dermato-Venereology, there is marked heterogeneity in undergraduate training across Europe, including substantial variation in curriculum structure and the perceived importance of the speciality. The aim of this study was to develop harmonized, structured and scalable educational tools for blended learning within an interactive "flipped classroom" framework. Within an EU-funded Erasmus+ project, supported by the European Dermatology Forum, key structural gaps in current training were identified, and a conceptual framework for restructuring undergraduate Dermato-Venereology education was developed. This framework emphasizes harmonization and standardization, scalability and integration into clinical practice.
items.author: Burg G, Gollnick H, Bagot M, White J, Darzina A, Djamei V.

items.title: Translation and cultural adaptation of the Oxford Shoulder Score to Swedish and validation of a new 7-day recall version in patients with a proximal humerus fracture.
items.summary: Background and purpose The Oxford Shoulder Score (OSS) is a widely applied patient-reported outcome measure (PROM) designed to assess function and pain in individuals with shoulder disorders. We primarily aimed to evaluate a translated and culturally adapted Swedish version of the original OSS and secondarily to evaluate a version with a 7-day recall period, intended for rapidly changing conditions such as the early phase following fractures and surgeries. Methods The OSS was translated according to Beaton's guidelines for cross-cultural adaptation. 246 patients with a nonoperatively treated proximal humerus fracture completed the Swedish OSS and the QuickDASH at 1 week (T1, 7-day recall period), 3 months (T2, 7-day recall period), and 12 months (T3, 4-week recall period).
items.author: Lundin PC, Sundh TFD, Adolfsson LE, Björnsson Hallgren HC.

items.title: Fundamental materials engineering of robust solid oxide electrolysis cells for terrestrial and space applications.
items.summary: In this work, a brief summary of the benefits of integrating Rh/Ce 1- x Gd x O 2- δ (CGO)-impregnated LSCT A- fuel electrode active layers into commercial standard solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) is provided, before presenting results pertaining to the optimisation of air electrode layers and high-conductivity perovskite electrode current collection layers, which better match the performance and stability of this novel fuel electrode. Firstly, results from solid-oxide electrochemical oxygen pump testing confirmed that 'traditional' (La 0.80 Sr 0.20 ) 0.95 MnO 3 (LSM)- and La 0.60 Sr 0.40 CoO 3 (LSC)-based air electrodes exhibit rapid degradation during oxygen evolution.
items.author: Price R, Sabey A, Irvine JTS.

items.title: Learning-associated flexibility of cortical taste coding is impaired in Shank3 knockout mice.
items.summary: The ability to update the valence of sensory perception to influence behavior is crucial for survival. A common phenotype in autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) is defects in sensory processing, but whether these defects impair flexible sensory encoding is largely unexplored. In particular, how genetic risk factors such as Shank3 deletion affect the adaptability of cortical taste processing and downstream behavior is unknown. To address this gap, we performed two-photon calcium imaging during a conditioned taste aversion (CTA) learning paradigm, an ethologically relevant form of associative learning that depends on taste processing in the gustatory cortex (GC), to examine how Shank3 knockout alters taste-related neuronal activity in GC and influences CTA learning.
items.author: Wu CH, Turrigiano GG.

items.title: Green-Lyte: A Multidisciplinary Quality Improvement Project to Optimize Electrolyte Replacement and Reduce Environmental Burden in ICUs at a Comprehensive Cancer Center.
items.summary: Background Electrolyte replacement therapies are commonly prescribed in ICUs. However, studies have shown that electrolytes are frequently administered to patients with no clear clinical indications and, in most cases, the IV route is used. In this study, we evaluated the impact of a multidisciplinary quality improvement project, Green-Lyte, on electrolyte replacement and on the environmental burden. Methods This was a quality improvement retrospective study conducted in the adult ICUs at a comprehensive cancer center comparing preimplementation (September 2024 to February 2025) and postimplementation (May 2025 to October 2025) phases of the Green-Lyte project. Green-Lyte consisted of defined criteria to guide both the indication and route of administration for potassium, magnesium, and phosphorus replacement, along with ongoing education and follow-up.
items.author: Khashashneh L, Kharabsheh A, Mahmoud N, Smadi M, Abdel-Haq T, Alessa L, Al-Jaghbeer M, Awad W, Said N, Mousa A, Nazer L.

items.title: Ventilator Modes Used to Facilitate Liberation From Mechanical Ventilation: A Scoping Review.
items.summary: Objectives Liberation from invasive ventilation involves gradual decrements in respiratory support, spontaneous breathing trials, or both. Although various ventilator modes have been studied to facilitate weaning, the approaches used across trials for the highest risk patients are not well summarized. We sought to summarize the different ventilator modes and liberation strategies that have been investigated in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of critically ill adults at risk for difficult or prolonged weaning from invasive ventilation. Data sources We searched MEDLINE, Embase, PubMed, and Cochrane Library databases from inception to January 2026.
items.author: Ho JC, Lewis K, Ranganath N, Piticaru J, Rajkumar S, Burns KEA, Bosma KJ, Brochard L, Rochwerg B, Chaudhuri D.

items.title: Soy foods, isoflavone intake, and diabetic kidney disease: The Fukuoka Diabetes Registry.
items.summary: Aims/introduction Soy foods are traditional components of the Japanese diet; however, evidence of their association with diabetic kidney disease remains limited. This study examined the association of soy food and isoflavone intake with decreased eGFR and albuminuria in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes. Materials and methods Overall, 4,922 individuals with type 2 diabetes were enrolled in this cross-sectional analysis. Soy food and isoflavone intakes were assessed using a self-administered diet history questionnaire. Odds ratios for decreased cystatin C-based eGFR (eGFR cys 2 ) and albuminuria (urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/g) were calculated using logistic regression. Results Frequent consumption of natto, miso soup, and tofu was associated with lower prevalence of decreased eGFR cys .
items.author: Ohkuma T, Iwase M, Higashi T, Sakamoto W, Fujihira M, Ago T.

items.title: Modelling and simulation of species transport in capillary-fed electrolysis cells.
items.summary: In so-called capillary-fed electrolysis cells (Hodges et al. , Nature Commun. , 2022, 13 , 1304), electrolyte is resupplied through capillary forces in a porous structure contained between the two electrodes. This configuration enables largely bubble-free operation, resulting in low cell potentials even at high current densities, and this approach is therefore highly promising for terrestrial as well as space applications. While sustained operation has been demonstrated experimentally, the mechanism enabling this remains unclear, especially given the expected rise in electrolyte concentration over time and the risk of salt precipitation in the porous separator. In this study, our goal is to identify possible mechanisms that could act to limit the maximum electrolyte concentration in the separator.
items.author: De Paoli M, Wood JA, Vreman AW, Krug D.

items.title: Cis -regulation and natural selection in the evolution of human DNA methylation.
items.summary: The vast collection of human-specific traits-such as our unique morphology, cognition, behavior, and diseases-has long been attributed to gene expression divergence between us and our closest living relatives, chimpanzees. Theory suggests that changes to cis -regulatory elements such as promoters and enhancers may drive evolutionary adaptation, and DNA methylation is a key factor in transcriptional cis -regulation. However, we still lack an understanding of (1) how species-specific methylation patterns arise; (2) their downstream effects; and (3) whether they are a common target of natural selection. In this study, we investigated these three questions. By combining a novel hypothesis testing framework with DNA methylation data from six human and chimpanzee cell types, as well as fused interspecies hybrid cells, we disentangled cis - vs.
items.author: Ma Z, Starr AL, Gokhman D, Fraser HB.

items.title: Rationally engineered polymeric interfaces for selective and dynamic recognition of vesicular agents.
items.summary: It is exceedingly hard to accurately identify and separate nanoscale vesicular entities such as extracellular vesicles (EVs), lipid-enveloped and membrane-associated viral particles, and lipid-based drug delivery nanoparticles. These systems have a membrane-bound structure, but their surface composition, mechanical properties, and molecular structures are diverse. This makes it challenging to differentiate them in complicated biological matrices. Molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs) are synthetic recognition materials that solve this problem by being selective, stable, and cost effective. This review provides a thorough analysis of rationally engineered MIP interfaces for the targeted detection of vesicular agents. We first analyze the physicochemical properties of vesicular surfaces; including lipid bilayer composition, surface protein and glycan profiles, charge distribution, and membrane mechanical characteristics.
items.author: Erdem Ö, Yilmaz EG, Genc S, Kılıç N, Inci F.

items.title: Potential effect of human chorionic gonadotropin-induced extracellular vesicle RNAs on mouse ovarian granulosa cells.
items.summary: Gonadotropins regulate granulosa-cell function during ovarian follicular development, and extracellular vesicles (EVs) are potential mediators of intercellular communication within the follicle. However, the regulation of EV RNA cargo following gonadotropin stimulation remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG)-responsive EV RNA profiles using three experimental models: two Lhcgr-expressing clones of a mouse granulosa-cell tumor-derived cell line and mouse ovaries. The cell models were treated with hCG, and immature mice were primed with serotropin, followed by hCG. EVs were isolated from these cells and ovaries and characterized by transmission electron microscopy and western blot analysis. Total RNAs from these EVs were analyzed by electrophoresis, suggesting global changes in their profiles with hCG.
