items.title: Inside the battery box: a cross-technology assessment of PFAS uses, functions, and substitution potential.
items.summary: Understanding where and why per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) are used in batteries is essential for evaluating their substitution potential, yet detailed information across battery technologies is scarce. We analyzed more than 5600 submissions to the Annex XV public consultation on the proposed universal PFAS restriction in the European Union and extracted information reporting use, associated substance(s), and stated function(s) of PFASs in batteries. 341 records were compiled into a database using our structured Battery Use & Function Framework that incorporates the Functional Substitution Framework. Among these records, 78 contained sufficient information to qualify as a potential PFAS use and were organized into 36 potential PFAS uses, accounting for overlaps.
items.author: Rensmo A, Miller AJ, Glüge J, Scheringer M, Wang Z, Lohmann R, Ng CA, Trier X, Cousins IT.

items.title: TREM2 + Macrophages Promote Immune Evasion in Endometriosis Through BAG3-Associated Regulation of CD8 + T Cell Autophagy.
items.summary: Macrophages are the most abundant immune cells in endometriotic lesions, but the roles of specific macrophage subsets in local immune dysfunction remain poorly understood. Here, combining single-cell RNA sequencing of 11 clinical samples with TREM2 knockout mouse models, co-culture experiments, and pharmacological intervention, we identify TREM2 + macrophages as an immunoregulatory population enriched in endometriosis. CD8 + T and natural killer (NK) cells in endometriotic lesions exhibited exhaustion-associated features and reduced cytotoxicity. Cell-cell communication analysis and functional experiments revealed that TREM2 + macrophages regulated CD8 + T cell activity through SPP1-CD44-associated communication and BAG3-associated autophagy regulation. In a mouse model of endometriosis, TREM2 deficiency enhanced CD8 + T and NK cell cytotoxicity and reduced ectopic lesion growth.
items.author: Yuan M, Jiao X, Xu L, Ren Q, Wang S, Zhong Z, Li N, Li Q, Meng X, Wang G.

items.title: Risk indicators and composite index for imported malaria re-establishment in Fuzhou, China: a 10-year study integrating case, vector, and meteorological surveillance data.
items.summary: Background Following China's malaria-free certification in 2021, imported malaria infections and the continued presence of Anopheles mosquitoes pose challenges for preventing local transmission in post-elimination settings. We integrated case, vector, and meteorological surveillance data to describe potential conditions for malaria re-establishment in Fuzhou, China. Methods We analyzed imported malaria cases reported during 2016-2025, vector surveillance records, and corresponding meteorological data. Five binary indicators-imported case presence, diagnostic delay, Anopheles presence, high Anopheles density, and favorable meteorological conditions-were combined into an exploratory monthly index. Risk scores were tabulated for the 60 months in the May-October surveillance seasons using the available routine surveillance information.
items.author: Liao Q, Wang J, Yang J, Zhang X, Wu Z.

items.title: A genome-wide association study and genetic risk score for age at diabetes diagnosis support beta-cell dysfunction in young-onset diabetes in Chinese.
items.summary: Background We investigated genetic variations driving young age-at-diabetes-diagnosis (ADD) and developed a genetic risk score (GRS) to identify Chinese individuals at risk of young-onset diabetes (YOD with ADD Methods We performed genome-wide association studies (GWAS) for ADD with internal and external replication in 22,611 individuals with type 2 diabetes (T2D, 20% with YOD) and identified Chinese-prioritized loci by conditioning on the polygenic risk score (PRS) of ADD constructed from publicly available datasets. We constructed ADD-GRS using genome-wide independent variants (p Results We identified three independent signals at genome-wide significance (P Conclusions Both known and novel T2D loci contribute to ADD in Chinese people and may be used to detect high risk individuals for early intervention to prevent or delay onset of YOD.

items.title: MAGR-TCM: a knowledge graph-powered multi-agent model for intelligent home health consultation and triage in TCM gynecology.
items.summary: Background Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) demonstrates distinct efficacy in managing gynecological disorders. However, accessing this specialized care in a home setting remains challenging due to the high cost of frequent hospital visits, privacy concerns, and a lack of immediate professional guidance. While general-purpose artificial intelligence offers a convenient alternative, the semantic gap between a patient's colloquial symptom descriptions and formal TCM diagnostic logic-compounded by the inherent 'hallucination' risks of large language models-prevents these tools from providing safe, actionable advice. To bridge this gap, this study proposes MAGR-TCM, an intelligent home health consultation and triage model. Methods Under expert supervision, a domain-specific knowledge graph was constructed, encompassing 10,231 entities and 32,051 relationships extracted from 741 high-quality clinical case records.
items.author: Lv M, Pan X, Li Y, Hu Y, Xu W, Jin L, Fang F.

items.title: Digenic inheritance of mutations in SPG7 and AFG3L2 causes late-onset ataxia with pyramidal signs.
items.summary: In this journal, Estiar et al. (2026) recently described 12 patients with digenic heterozygous variants in SPG7 and AFG3L2 genes, including one patient previously published by Magri et al. (2018). Patients had been identified from exome and genome data of cohorts with motor neuron disorder (MND), ataxia and rare/neurodegenerative diseases, and literature review. In a study that we published in 2023, we reported an additional patient with a deletion affecting the canonical acceptor splice-site c.1454_1462del p.(Arg485_Glu487del) (c.1450-1_1457delGGAGAGGCG) in SPG7 and a missense variant c.2105G > A p.(Arg702Gln) in AFG3L2. The patient had predominantly lower limb ataxia and hyperreflexia with a disease duration of 13 years at the time of assessment.

items.title: Linking dietary-derived arsenic exposure to blood serum arsenic burden, potential food sources, and breast cancer risk in the EPIC-Heidelberg cohort.
items.summary: Purpose Breast cancer is the most common cancer among women worldwide, yet the role of environmental toxicants remains unclear. Arsenic is an International Agency for Research on Cancer classified carcinogen linked to skin, lung, and bladder cancers. The relationship between dietary arsenic intake levels and blood arsenic concentrations, particularly across sexes, and the association between dietary arsenic intake and breast cancer remain understudied. This study aimed to address these gaps. Methods Measurements of arsenic in foods collected from 1995 to 2022 in the German monitoring programme were used to estimate long-term dietary intake. Serum arsenic levels were measured using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry.
items.author: Kipkoech M, Beck CM, Jaeger A, Blume K, Lubiński J, Marciniak W, Derkacz R, Johnson T, Kaaks R, Katzke VA.

items.title: Gut microbiome dysbiosis and associated metabolome changes in tuberculosis patients resolve partially post-therapy.
items.summary: Background Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection in the host and subsequent treatment with anti-tuberculosis drugs impact lung pathophysiology and influence the lung and gut microbiome. Elucidating the role of the gut microbiome and its metabolites in the perturbed metabolic and immune functions observed in tuberculosis (TB) might help design corrective prebiotic and probiotic mixtures. Methodology In this study, fecal samples (n = 107) of drug-naïve active TB patients (ATB) and controls (other respiratory disease: NTB and healthy) from the two clinical sites were analyzed for microbiota composition (16S rRNA sequencing), metabolites (GC-TOF-MS), and their correlation. In addition, a longitudinal follow-up study was conducted to understand the dynamics of the microbiota and metabolites during anti-TB treatment in a small cohort (n = 10).
items.author: Sahu S, Kaushik SR, Chaudhary S, Mohapatra AK, Kupa RU, Kapfo W, Saha S, Das R, Bhalla N, Kaur M, Sivaji Y, Das B, Das A, Khamo V, Nanda RK.

items.title: Topical 15% trichloroacetic acid versus silver nitrate cauterization in the management of idiopathic childhood epistaxis: a prospective randomized clinical trial.
items.summary: The purpose of the study is to compare the outcomes of trichloroacetic acid (TCA) to silver nitrate chemical cauterization in managing pediatric epistaxis. In this prospective randomized assessor-blinded clinical trial, of 172 randomized patients, 157 pediatric patients with idiopathic anterior epistaxis were divided into 2 groups in a ratio 1:1, where group (A) was treated with silver nitrate 25% after local anesthesia application and group (B) was treated with 15% TCA locally applied to the bleeder. Patients were assessed upon recurrence, pain, and crusting at 1st, 2nd, 4th, and 12th week post-intervention. The incidence of epistaxis was not significantly different between the two groups.
items.author: Gehad I, Elzayat S, Zaki Y, Kandil SE, Abdelhamid AS.

items.title: Photothermal CO 2 Hydrogenation to Multicarbon Products: Mechanisms, Catalyst Design, and Scale Demonstration.
items.summary: Photothermal CO 2 hydrogenation to multicarbon products presents a promising route to mitigate global climate change while simultaneously generating valuable C 2+ products for industrial use. However, realizing high activity and selectivity toward multicarbon products remains a significant challenge, primarily due to the intricate nature of reactant activation and the inherently sluggish kinetics of C-C coupling. This review elucidates the fundamental principles of photothermal catalysis, with a particular focus on the synergistic interplay between light and thermal energy. In addition, the activation pathways of CO 2 to C 1 intermediates and the subsequent mechanisms of C-C bond formation leading to multicarbon products are systematically examined.
items.author: Liao Y, Luo Y, Wang Z, Wang Q, He H.

items.title: Future directions of nanocatalysts in precision medicine: from catalytic therapy to intelligent nanozymes.
items.summary: The scope of nanomedicine may be broadened by nanocatalysts, which can actively modulate biochemical reactions in vivo. Of these nanocatalysts, nanozymes (nanomaterials with intrinsic enzyme-like activity) probably have received the most attention. Their activity can catalyze a reaction similar to peroxidase, catalase, oxidase, superoxide dismutase, or glutathione peroxidase, depending on composition, thus generating or scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS) depending on the microenvironment. This review sketches the evolution of this field from first generation iron oxide nanozymes to more recent stimuli-responsive multi-enzyme nanostructures. Moreover, selected experimental studies are examined, starting from in vivo Fenton and Fenton-like chemodynamic therapy and cascade catalysis and oxygen-releasing nanozymes in cancer, to antioxidant, antimicrobial, and immunomodulatory nanozymes in regenerative medicine, neurological, cardiovascular, and infectious disease models, respectively.
items.author: Raef NA, Hamedi F, Ghalari M.

items.title: Influence of stem undersizing during direct anterior approach for total hip arthroplasty on periprosthetic bone biomechanics : a finite element analysis.
items.summary: Aims Stem undersizing during cementless total hip arthroplasty (THA) may occur more frequently when the procedure is performed through the direct anterior approach (DAA) because of limited femoral exposure. Insufficient stem-bone contact may compromise primary stability and alter load transfer in the proximal femur. The aim was to investigate the biomechanical effects of femoral stem undersizing on periprosthetic bone using finite element analysis. A secondary objective was to evaluate whether the presence of a femoral stem collar modifies these biomechanical effects. Methods Patient-specific finite element models of the full femur were generated from CT data. Eight finite element models were analyzed, combining four implantation configurations of the AMIStem-P designs (Adequate Fit, Adequate Fit-Collared, Undersized, and Undersized-Collared) with two cancellous bone density conditions, representing 100% and 90% cancellous bone density.
items.author: Liskay J, Marcián P, Apostolopoulos V, Nachtnebl L, Tomáš T.

items.title: Sensitive detection of in vivo traumatic brain injury foci using magnetic particle imaging.
items.summary: Diagnosing traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains a major clinical challenge, particularly for mild to moderate cases, due to the limited sensitivity of conventional imaging modalities like magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT) in detecting subtle cerebrovascular damage early after injury occurs. Magnetic particle imaging (MPI) is a novel modality that offers high sensitivity, linear quantification, and unambiguous detection of superparamagnetic tracers such as iron oxide nanoparticles (IONPs). This study evaluates the capacity of MPI to detect and visualize cerebral bleeding resulting from TBI. A controlled cortical impact (CCI) closed-head TBI model was implemented using a calibrated electromagnetic impactor to induce moderate brain injury in C57BL/6 mice.
items.author: Good HJ, Tabatabaei M, Alzamora E, Eswaran N, Ali SR, Velazquez-Albino AC, Simon ZD, Febo M, Williams LN, Rinaldi-Ramos CM.

items.title: Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease: The Complete Molecular Architecture for the PKHD1 Gene and Its Protein.
items.summary: Fibrocystin/polyductin is a large single-pass transmembrane glycoprotein involved in tubulogenesis and maintenance of the epithelium, where disease-causing variants in its encoding gene PKHD1 cause autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease. While enormous experimental efforts have been taken to characterize proteins involved in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, the structural and molecular basis of fibrocystin has lagged behind with no known mechanistic models. Here, our study introduces the first idealized molecular model of fibrocystin, where we confirm the established domain architecture and refine the nomenclature of unresolved regions. Using our molecular model, we show that disease-causing missense variants tend to be buried and impose marked loss-of-function effects to the monomer.
items.author: Pillai JP, Puntambekar SN, Onuchic-Whitford AC, Ferreira F, Sampson MG, Onuchic LF, Sayer JA.

items.title: The impact of dietary vegetable oil sources with or without vitamin E supplementation on the productive performance and egg yolk lipids of quail breeders.
items.summary: The goal of the present study was to discover the probable impact of sunflower oil (SUNO), linseed oil (LINO), and canola oil (CANO) with or without vitamin E treatments on the productive parameters and egg yolk lipid metabolism of quail eggs. In a completely randomized design, this trial was conducted as a 3 × 2 factorial trial with three sources of vegetable oils (SUNO 3 %, LINO 3 %, and CANO 3 %) and two types of vitamin E (0 and 250 mg kg -1 diet) in six treatments. A total of 192 female Japanese quails, 10 weeks of age, were randomly allocated to six dietary treatments, with 32 quails per treatment.

items.title: Preoperative glycaemic control and severity of sternal wound infections after cardiac surgery: association of elevated Hemoglobin A1c with deep versus superficial infections.
items.summary: Sternal wound infections (SWIs), including superficial sternal wound infection (SSWI) and deep sternal wound infection (DSWI), are complications after coronary artery bypass grafting and other cardiac surgeries. Elevated preoperative HbA1c, suggesting poor glycaemic control, impairs wound healing and may escalate postoperative risk. This study evaluates the association between preoperative HbA1c levels and the anatomical severity (superficial versus deep) of SWIs among patients who develop postoperative wound complications. A 24-month retrospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary care cardiac surgery centre. Adult patients (≥18 years) going through elective or urgent isolated cardiac surgery with a preoperative HbA1c measured within 30 days were included.
items.author: Khan M, Lalani FK, Khan S, Batool S, Farwa U, Basharat S.

items.title: Plasma metagenomic cell-free DNA sequencing identifies clinically unsuspected cases of Toxoplasma gondii infection in immunocompromised patients: a single-centre experience.
items.summary: Toxoplasmosis can be challenging to diagnose, particularly in immunocompromised patients with nonspecific clinical presentations. We present a retrospective, single-centre case series of eight Toxoplasma gondii infections identified by plasma metagenomic cell-free DNA (cfDNA) sequencing in allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients. Nested within a larger cohort evaluating cfDNA utilization, this case series highlights a positive clinical impact of cfDNA testing in 5 out of 8 (62.5%) patients, including earlier diagnosis and changes in clinical management. These findings illustrate the potential utility of plasma cfDNA sequencing as a complement to conventional diagnostics across diverse clinical presentations of toxoplasmosis.
items.author: Goren LR, Lehman AC, Drozdov D, Thielen BK.

items.title: Mechanistic Insights into Delayed Bruise Clearance after Skin Booster Injection: Role of Blood-Polymer Complexation.
items.summary: Cutaneous injection of polycaprolactone-based skin boosters has emerged as a promising approach for facial rejuvenation, leveraging their long-lasting effects and ability to stimulate collagen regeneration. Despite clinical success, complications such as delayed bruise clearance remain poorly understood mechanistically. Here, we establish a controlled murine bruise model to investigate the impact of blood-polymer interaction and injection sequence on bruise persistence. To model distinct blood-polymer contact sequences, blood was administered before or after the polymer, while premixed blood-polymer formulations served as comparison groups. Bruise appearance was monitored and complemented by histological, spectroscopic, and colorimetric analyses of blood persistence, inflammatory responses, scaffold structure, and material degradation.
items.author: Roh S, Park SJ, Ye S, Jung Y, Lee C, Shestakova O, Malik BJ, Seo J, Kim H, Yoo J.

items.title: Data-Driven Virtual Reality Environment Recommendation for Long-Term Care Residents With Major Neurocognitive Conditions: Feasibility and Proof-of-Concept Study.
items.summary: Background Virtual reality (VR) comfort sessions are increasingly used in residential dementia care, but environment selection remains ad hoc-staff have no systematic way to identify which virtual experience best suits a given resident. Objective This feasibility and proof-of-concept study aimed to determine whether a pipeline integrating wearable physiological signals (heart rate variability and electrodermal activity), behavioral observations, and semantic environment characteristics can detect a person-specific, environment-level signal usable for between-session VR environment recommendation in long-term care and whether the resulting recommendations can be communicated to care staff and families through plain-language reports. Methods Twenty-one residents with major neurocognitive conditions received 420 immersive VR sessions (5 environments, 2 sessions per week, 10 weeks) in a long-term care facility.
items.author: Reyes-Consuelo A, Kiss J, Voisin J.

items.title: First Year Implementation and Performance of the Republic of Korea's National Antimicrobial Stewardship Program Pilot: Policy Directions for Sustainable Expansion.
items.summary: Objectives This report analyzes the implementation and performance of the first year of the Republic of Korea's National Antimicrobial Stewardship Program (ASP) pilot and proposes policy directions for its sustainable operation and a phased expansion. Methods We examined implementation data from 78 participating general and tertiary hospitals with having more than 300 beds from November 1, 2024, to December 31, 2025. Data collected through and annual reports, program guidelines, annual evaluations, and on-site inspection were reviewed to assess ASP infrastructure and major structural and process indicators. Results In all, 78 (45.9%) of 170 eligible institutions participated. These institutions created multidisciplinary ASP teams that included 695 personnel and developed 622 institution-specific antibiotic use guidelines.

items.title: Status of Notifiable Infectious Diseases Reporting in the Seoul Metropolitan Area, Republic of Korea, 2025.
items.summary: Objectives The Capital Regional Center for Disease Control and Prevention has jurisdiction over four cities and provinces (Seoul Metropolitan City, Incheon Metropolitan City, Gyeonggi province, and Gangwon State), which account for 53.9% of total population of the Republic of Korea. To analyze and summarize the prevalence and high incidence of notifiable infectious diseases reported in the Seoul Metropolitan Area in 2025. This study analyzes surveillance data to identify trends in infectious disease outbreaks in the Seoul Metropolitan Area and to inform the Capital Regional Center for Disease Control and Prevention's future policies on infectious disease prevention, management, preparedness, and response.
items.author: Kim S, Choo J, Kim H, Ko M, Kim J.

items.title: Educating Internal Medicine Residents About Breast Health Using a Jigsaw Teaching Strategy: An Interactive Curriculum Module.
items.summary: Introduction Education in women's health is lacking in internal medicine (IM) residency training despite women making up half the population. With increasing recognition of women's unique health care needs and recent guideline updates for breast cancer (BC) screening, we utilized an interactive teaching strategy, the Jigsaw Teaching Strategy (JTS), to increase resident comfort with BC screening at 2 large New York (NY) IM residency programs. Methods One hundred eighty-six IM residents across 2 residency programs participated in a one-hour JTS session in 2024. JTS is a cooperative teaching technique that assigns each learner to become an "expert" on one topic and then brings learners together in mixed groups to teach their individual topics to one another.
items.author: Zeidman R, Chen A, Patel Y, Conigliaro RL, Killian K, Shrivastava S.

items.title: Sequencing Meets Repetition Coding: Quadratic Substitution Error Suppression through Homotrimer Redundancy.
items.summary: Homotrimer unique molecular identifiers encode each nucleotide 3 times to suppress substitution errors. Here, we derive decoding-error probabilities for this quaternary repetition code under majority voting with uniform random tie-breaking. Under independent substitutions (base error probability) p , the decoding error probability is gp=7/3p2-4/3p3 . For nonuniform conditional substitution probabilities πi , it becomes gp,π=1-pp22+∑i=13πi2+p3 . Exhaustive enumeration and Monte Carlo simulations verify these results. This analysis quantifies the error suppression attributable to homotrimer redundancy under a specified local decoder, without modeling correlated errors, indels, or downstream molecular-counting accuracy.

items.title: Metasurfaces with Anisotropic Electric and Magnetic Conductivities: Parameter Retrieval for Arbitrary Incidence and Polarization
items.summary: Metasurfaces come in a great variety of unit cell geometries and material composition. A common approach for describing them relies on retrieving effective surface parameters (e.g., electric and magnetic conductivities) from plane-wave scattering data. Conventional retrieval methods are often limited to isotropic unit cells, a uniform host material, or lead to increased complexity by requiring reflection and transmission coefficients from both sides of the metasurface. Here, we derive analytical expressions for the equivalent surface conductivities of an electrically- and magnetically-polarizable anisotropic metasurface under oblique plane-wave incidence with arbitrary polarization. The proposed formulation does not require bidirectional scattering information, thus simplifying the process especially in experimental studies.
items.author: Dimitrios Chatzidimitriou, Alexandros Pitilakis, Odysseas Tsilipakos

items.title: Subwavelength registration of skull-compensating acoustic holograms via nonlinear parametric array feedback
items.summary: Realizing the potential of optimized acoustic holograms for applications like transcranial ultrasound requires sub-wavelength alignment accuracy (less than 1.5 mm at 1 MHz), which is difficult to achieve with current non-MRI optical neuro-navigation methods. To address the critical challenge of alignment, we leverage the parametric array (PA) signal as an alignment surrogate, a highly penetrative, low-frequency difference wave generated by the nonlinear mixing of two primary high-frequency beams. Simulations show that a misaligned skull-compensating lens increases the primary acoustic energy within the skull bone (volumetric energy trapping), which strengthens the nonlinear source of the PA signal. We also tested whether shear-mode conversion in bone contributes: 2D elastic simulations showed only a small (3-5%) increase in shear-type motion with misalignment, and the transmitted ex vivo bursts did not lengthen as a shear path would require.
items.author: Pradosh Pritam Dash, Costas D. Arvanitis

items.title: Learning a calibrated decision head from logged bandit feedback
items.summary: A decision head reads a state and a list of options and returns a probability per option in one forward pass. Once deployed, it usually observes only whether the option it chose was right: logged bandit feedback. We adapt such a head, LoRA on Qwen3-0.6B-Base and 1.7B-Base, from that feedback and report three results. First, the Brier or log score of the sampled action's own probability is not a usable REINFORCE reward: every wrong action earns at least gold's reward, with a mean baseline the lowest-probability wrong action gets the largest advantage, and at two options the signal is zero; in one run it cut accuracy on ordered-scale questions from .636 to .111.
items.author: Ye Yuan

items.title: TraceKV: Policy-Preserving Low-Rank KV Cache Compression for Reasoning Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Reasoning vision-language models (VLMs) impose substantial KV cache demands from both large multimodal contexts and growing reasoning traces. Low-rank KV compression has emerged as a promising paradigm that stores low-dimensional latents of KV states and can be combined with quantization. However, existing low-rank methods often induce growing predictive policy drift from the dense model when compressing reasoning KV states, resulting in reasoning failures. We identify two key causes of this degradation: calibration-state mismatch between static contexts and on-policy reasoning states, and unequal error sensitivity across KV states. To address these challenges, we propose TraceKV, a training-free low-rank KV compression framework that unifies on-policy calibration, sensitivity-aware SVD, and global rank allocation under a single policy-preserving principle, substantially reducing policy-KL divergence during reasoning.
items.author: Ke Li, Zishan Shao, Yiran Chen

items.title: Observations Drift, Structures Remain: Structural Pretraining with Time Alignment for Electromagnetic Signals
items.summary: Electromagnetic signal modeling is increasingly moving toward self-supervised pretraining on heterogeneous I/Q observations. However, an observed waveform is jointly shaped by signal generation, propagation environments, and acquisition processes, which mix reusable structural regularities with observation-specific variations. Existing methods usually pursue unified pretraining with reconstruction objectives on mixed observations. This heterogeneity creates two key mismatches for reconstruction pretraining: (1) appearance mismatch, induced by propagation-dependent waveform variations; and (2) temporal mismatch, induced by acquisition-dependent sampling coordinates. These mismatches make observation-specific appearances and sampling coordinates easier to reconstruct than stable signal structures, inducing observational shortcuts. We identify this failure mode as observation-biased pretraining.
items.author: Wenjin Gui, Junyu Shen, Haibo Xu et al.

items.title: Generalized Inverse Kinematics via Conditional Flow
items.summary: Inverse kinematics (IK) is a foundational primitive in robotics, mapping the task-space objectives expressed by higher-level planners to robot configurations that realize them. Traditional IK methods generally treat each query as an isolated pose-to-configuration problem, but planners often need a distribution over valid realizations that accounts for future reachability and preferences such as collision avoidance and stability. We introduce GenGenIK, a generative modeling approach that supports mobile bases, multiple end-effectors and targets, scene awareness, and preferences over robot behavior within a common interface. Experiments show that GenGenIK outperforms existing methods in both solve rate and runtime across tasks such as bimanual lift and flip-up, while allowing flexible control over the sampled distribution and remaining effective under partial scene observations.
items.author: Kaitlyn Zhang, Tomás Lozano-Pérez, Leslie Pack Kaelbling

items.title: What Conformal Selection Can Certify in CRISPR Off-Target Design:Benchmark Leakage, Free Baselines, and a Finite-Sample Cohort Requirement
items.summary: Conformal selection promises distribution-free, finite-sample control of the error rate of a decision, and has been proposed as a safety layer for machine-learning CRISPR guide design. We ask whether such a certificate is attainable from the validated off-target data that exist. The constraint is arithmetic: a conformal p-value cannot fall below one divided by the calibration cohort size plus one, so a Benjamini-Hochberg selection certifies a single candidate only when that cohort is at least the candidate pool size divided by the tolerated error rate. Public cohorts supply ten validated guides, whereas a pool of two thousand at a ten percent error rate needs twenty thousand; the accepted set is consequently empty in over ninety-six percent of splits.
items.author: Mohammad Malekpouri, Somayeh Lotfi

items.title: Testing Conversation Preservation Across LLM APIs: A Rule-Based Oracle for Detecting Silent Information Loss
items.summary: LLM applications increasingly rely on translators and compatibility layers to move conversations across APIs. Yet a translated request can be accepted by the target API while silently losing information about instruction roles, tool interactions, error states, or generation controls. We introduce isloss, a deterministic oracle for testing conversation-information preservation across LLM API translations. It maps source and translated requests and replies to a shared intermediate representation, ConvIR, and applies explicit rules to distinguish legitimate representation changes from information loss. Unlike schema validation or reference-based differential testing, isloss requires neither a reference translation nor additional model calls. It also distinguishes avoidable loss from degradation caused by target API limitations.
items.author: Xin Liu, Xu Han, Yuxin Wang et al.

items.title: Faithful in Steps: Improving Generalization and Citation in RAG via Query Decomposition
items.summary: Retrieval-augment generation is a prevalent strategy to mitigate hallucinations of LLMs. The attributable RAG (RAGQ) generates quotes for its answers. The quotes indicate which input contexts support the RAG to derive the answers, enhancing the answer's verifiability and trustworthiness. However, existing RAGQs exhibit significant degradation when dealing with questions that require multi-hop reasoning and multi-modal understanding, suffering from over-citation, implicit entity identification failure, and poor generalization. In this paper, we propose a novel RAGQ framework, namely QDRAG. QDRAG breaks down the input question into atomic subquestions to identify the implicit entities. Then, the reranker prunes context distractors to eliminate the downstream over-citation.
items.author: Yue Liu, Zhongying Ru, Shimin Di et al.

items.title: Analysis choices decide whether untrained networks beat trained ones at V1: a multiverse analysis of model-brain RSA
items.summary: Untrained convolutional networks have been reported to rival trained networks as models of visual cortex, and we had reported an untrained-network advantage over backpropagation at V1 in THINGS fMRI, together with a dependence on evaluation resolution. Under a pre-specified ridge readout, the untrained network scored below the trained one at every pooling grid (median r difference -0.043 at g = 4, 0 of 5 seeds positive), and also in MSE skill and per-fold r. In exploratory analyses, across 36 combinations of unit normalisation, distance measure and voxel normalisation (28 distinct analyses), the sign of the V1 contrast depended on the analysis (intervals above 0 in 5 and below 0 in 9 distinct analyses), and in our networks the resolution dependence of the original convention appeared in only one cell.
items.author: Nils Leutenegger

items.title: MAGIC: Modality-Aware Gini Inspection for Clinical Hallucination Detection in LMMs
items.summary: Recent advances in medical large multimodal models (LMMs) have brought promising progress to clinical decision support, yet hallucination, the generation of confident but clinically unverifiable outputs, poses a critical threat to the reliability demanded in high-stakes medical settings. Existing hallucination detection methods, predominantly designed for unimodal settings, fail to capture the visual-linguistic dynamics inherent to medical imaging. We formulate the problem of hallucination detection in LMMs as disproportionate distribution of attention weights across the modalities during answer token generation. We quantify modality-specific attention concentration across layers and heads using the Gini coefficient and demonstrate statistically significant redistribution of attention mass between visual and textual tokens in hallucinated responses.
items.author: Sachin Acharya, Niyoj Oli, Shishir Adhikari et al.

items.title: One Hierarchy, Many Sports: Hierarchy-Aligned Multi-Task Learning for Next-Shot Prediction
items.summary: Next-shot prediction in racket sports requires learning from event data with different match structures, recorded attributes, and label vocabularies. Table tennis, badminton, and tennis nevertheless share a hierarchy in which shots form rallies and rallies form higher scoring units. We present MT-HTA, a hierarchy-aligned multi-task Transformer that uses this structure to jointly predict the attributes of the next shot. A temporal Transformer captures event progression, a feature-token path models interactions among semantic fields rather than along the time axis, and task-specific attention retrieves information from hierarchical summaries and player context. The architecture supports three- and four-level hierarchies and sport-dependent task sets.
items.author: Chao-Wei Cai, Min-Te Sun, Sheng Kuang Wu et al.

items.title: Reading the Table: Sim-to-Real Game State Detection for the Chef's Hat Card Game
items.summary: Tabletop games offer a compelling scenario to study the interaction between artificial and human agents, combining social interaction with game state tracking and physical manipulation. To assess the game state, a robot needs to precisely detect closely related game objects, such as different card designs, requiring dedicated training data that is costly to annotate in the real world. Instead, we develop a fully automated synthetic data collection pipeline, using re-projection of known 3D coordinates to generate labels automatically and domain randomization to bridge the reality gap. This approach is used to collect a dataset of 25413 samples to finetune an object detection and a segmentation model, which are combined to assign detected cards to game-relevant zones and infer the game state.
items.author: Connor Gäde, Matthias Kerzel, Hauke Bünning et al.

items.title: An Approach to Hinton's Mother-Child Proposal: Neural Networks Learning and Preserving Care in a Finite World
items.summary: Hinton proposed that artificial intelligence should be given "maternal instincts" and relate to us as a mother to her child. We argue that care must first be learned, with the network itself as the child. We construct this upbringing in a finite world and study whether care survives the mother's departure, new situations and further learning. The mechanism combines a vocabulary of harm, a learned measure of future acceptability and an execution veto. A finite role certificate supports transfer within a declared world family. When the hidden representation changes, an update is accepted only if a care readout recovers the required judgements with a prescribed margin and bounded weights.
items.author: Csaba Balogh

items.title: GHAgentCI: A Dataset of Coding-Agent Invocations in CI Workflow Histories
items.summary: Coding agents are increasingly integrated into GitHub Actions to review pull requests, triage issues and modify code. Identifying these integrations is challenging because agentic workflows often resemble ordinary CI files, with evidence appearing in action references, shell commands and workflow conventions. We present GHAgentCI, a dataset of 15K+ workflow histories from 6K+ of 196K+ mined GitHub repositories, comprising 159K+ revisions and 205K+ agent-evidence records linked to workflow triggers and declared execution constraints. Our open-source extractor, cai-miner, detects agent-related evidence using an extensible catalogue. Manual validation of 576 stratified records confirmed 96.1% of dedicated-action matches and 98.8% of GitHub Agentic Workflow matches, with lower rates for other evidence kinds.
items.author: Daniel Ogenrwot, Jorge Gonzalo Delgado Cervantes, Woojoong Kim et al.

items.title: DecArena: Evaluating Large-Scale Decentralized Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.summary: Emerging personal AI agents raise fundamental scalability and privacy concerns for centralized multi-agent systems (MASs), which rely on a global orchestrator with broad access to agents, resources, and communication. In decentralized environments, global visibility is unavailable. Agents need to proactively discover non-local resources (e.g. tools, skills), and collaborate with other agents to solve tasks. We study decentralized multi-agent collaboration under graph-constrained communication, a natural reflection of human structures. Each agent observes only its local state and can interact only with neighboring agents. We introduce a benchmark with synthetic scalable distributed tool calling with 100K+ tools. Our experiments reveal that recent LLM agents struggle to discover non-local relevant resources and collaborate in decentralized setting.
items.author: Jiali Cheng, Oleg Rokhlenko, Joo-Kyung Kim et al.

items.title: Incentive-Responsive Agents: A Principal-Agent Framework, Metric Suite, and Runtime Architecture for Long-Lived Personal AI Agents
items.summary: Personal AI agents now persist: they hold accounts, mailboxes, long-term memory, and open-ended task streams, yet the dominant way to improve them remains capability-side: prompt engineering, larger models, longer thinking, and retrieval. We argue that long-lived agents are missing an incentive layer. We formalize an incentive not as text in a prompt but as a runtime contract over the agent's operating point (model tier, test-time compute, memory budget, tool authority, task priority, verification, and compensation) that the agent's policy must causally consume. We develop a principal-agent model with hidden effort, a contractible operating point, and costly verification. We derive (i) a non-consumption invariance principle separating genuine incentives from prompt-level persuasion, (ii) a persistence-as-discount theorem making identity continuity a precondition for sustained effort, (iii) an incentive-capability exchange-rate frontier yielding a per-task routing rule, and (iv) a Goodhart bound for multi-channel verification, plus a three-channel decomposition of mechanism gains (allocation, verification, continuation).
items.author: Jipu Su

items.title: ReShap: Interpretable Reinforcement Learning for High-Dimensional Multi-Action Settings
items.summary: Deep Reinforcement Learning (RL) plays a crucial role in tackling complex tasks, yet its reliance on deep neural networks makes the learned policies opaque. To enhance the trustworthiness of RL policies, existing work (e.g., the SILVER framework [Li et al., 2025]) has focused on Shapley-based interpretability, but is typically restricted to low-dimensional state spaces, binary-action settings, and a single class of linear surrogate. We propose ReShap, a policy-distillation framework that extends Shapley-based interpretability to high-dimensional, multi-action environments. ReShap extracts compact feature representations from raw image observations, performs SHAP-based feature attribution to characterize how each feature contributes to the policy's decisions, and distills the deep RL policy into an interpretable surrogate trained on the full set of (state, policy-action) pairs along the policy's visited distribution.
items.author: Yiyu Qian, Pengfei Guo, Liyuan Zhao

items.title: Virus-like particles enable highly efficient gene editing across porcine and avian in vitro , ex vivo , and in ovo models
items.summary: by Theresa M. Pauli, Theresa von Heyl, Beate Rieblinger, Sabrina Teresa Schleibinger, Wei Liang, Antonia Schmauser, Mithuoshni Arullmoli, Paul Derrer, Anika Eckstein, Sirradu Jagana, Camila Gatti Corrêa, Krzysztof Flisikowski, Tatiana Flisikowska, Benjamin Schusser Pigs and chickens are not only the most important livestock species for global food production but also serve as key model organisms in various research disciplines. The pig is widely used in translational research due to its anatomical and physiological similarity to humans, providing valuable insights into immunology, metabolism, and disease mechanisms. In contrast, the chicken has become an essential model for studies related to poultry health, animal welfare, and developmental biology.
items.author: Theresa M. Pauli, Theresa von Heyl, Beate Rieblinger et al.

items.title: A new asymmetry, an old toolkit: An emerging developmental enigma in appendage evolution
items.summary: by Caroline Schwaner, Tetsuya Nakamura Dorsoventral polarity is a key feature of paired appendages, yet its evolutionary origin is enigmatic as median fins, which predate paired appendages, are symmetric. A new PLOS Biology study shows lmx1b is dorsal in paired fin mesenchyme but posterior in median fins, implying genetic rewiring of an ancient toolkit. Dorsoventral polarity is a key feature of paired appendages, yet its evolutionary origin is enigmatic as median fins, which predate paired appendages, are symmetric. A new study shows that lmx1b is dorsal in paired fin mesenchyme but posterior in median fins, implying genetic rewiring of an ancient toolkit.
items.author: Caroline Schwaner, Tetsuya Nakamura

items.title: The single Cryptosporidium rhoptry sequentially drives invasion and host-parasite interface formation
items.summary: by Allison Cohen, Tim Bergner, Amandine Guérin, Maryse Lebrun, Michael Laue, Christian Klotz, Boris Striepen The apicomplexan parasite Cryptosporidium is a leading cause of diarrheal disease in young children. Within the intestinal epithelium, Cryptosporidium establishes a unique intracellular niche in the apical brush border of enterocytes. A structurally complex interface between host and parasite acts as a holdfast and enables protein and metabolite transport. How the parasite invades its host cell and builds the interface is poorly understood. Here, we reveal parasite invasion with high temporal and spatial resolution using rigorous molecular markers. We find that sequential discharge of specialized secretory organelles anchors the parasite within the host prior to internalization.
items.author: Allison Cohen, Tim Bergner, Amandine Guérin et al.

items.title: Pepti-DrugPhAI: Multimodal AI-evaluator for functional pharmacokinetics and toxicity of peptides
items.summary: by Elizaveta A. Bogdanova, Timofei F. Lukianov, Artem V. Chernukhin, Alexey K. Shaytan Peptide drugs exhibit exceptional selectivity for biological targets and high functional activity making them among the most promising therapeutic agents. However, unsatisfactory pharmacokinetic characteristics remain a critical barrier to their implementation. They often become the primary reason for the failure of promising candidates in preclinical and clinical trials. To address this issue, we present Pepti-DrugPhAI – a comprehensive algorithm for the precise prediction of the pharmacokinetics and toxicity of a wide range of peptide compounds. Unlike many existing solutions, the proposed algorithm is multimodal and can simultaneously process both SMILES representations of chemical structures and amino acid sequences.
items.author: Elizaveta A. Bogdanova, Timofei F. Lukianov, Artem V. Chernukhin et al.

items.title: Sphinx: An R package for adaptive spatial neighborhood modeling and functional analysis in spatial omics
items.summary: by Mengyi Yan, Xiaoxiu Tan, Zhenhao Liu, Siwen Zhang, Yiwen Du, Hong Li, Lanming Chen, Lu Xie Spatial omics enables analysis of tissue microenvironmental heterogeneity, but most spatial tools are optimized for transcriptomics and poorly suited to proteomics data. We developed Sphinx, an R package providing a comprehensive workflow for spatial proteomics, including preprocessing, cell annotation, adaptive spatial neighborhood modeling, and functional characterization. Importantly, it introduces an adaptive parameter selection framework guided by spatial statistical metrics and incorporates computational optimizations for large-scale datasets, enabling robust neighborhood modeling. Notably, Sphinx offers improved computational efficiency and scalability. Across lung adenocarcinoma, colorectal cancer, and mouse spleen datasets, Sphinx robustly identifies cell types and spatial functional units, including tertiary lymphoid structures.
items.author: Mengyi Yan, Xiaoxiu Tan, Zhenhao Liu et al.

items.title: Burst-to-burst information resetting in sequential rhythmic neural activity
items.summary: by Pablo Sanchez-Martin, Irene Elices, Alicia Garrido-Peña, Carlos Garcia-Saura, Rafael Levi, Francisco B. Rodriguez, Pablo Varona In multiple neural systems, networks of bursting neurons generate and coordinate robust sequential rhythms, such as those observed in central pattern generators (CPGs) that control motor activity. In this paper, we combine electrophysiological experiments and biophysical models of the pyloric CPG to investigate cycle-by-cycle coordination resetting in sequential rhythms. In particular, we focus our analysis on the variability constraints of sequence intervals defined by the burst onset and offset time references, which structure the timing of the rhythmic CPG sequence cycle-by-cycle. We identified the conditions under which sequential dynamical invariants emerge as robust relationships between specific intervals within the same cycle, and when such relations reset at each cycle or extend between intervals of consecutive cycles.
items.author: Pablo Sanchez-Martin, Irene Elices, Alicia Garrido-Peña et al.

items.title: An antigen-specific protein language model guides CDR optimization for antibody design
items.summary: by Faisal Bin Ashraf, Karen Paco, Sanaz Zebardast, Zihao Zhang, Ryan Mooney, Christian J. Dávila Ojeda, Mariana Paco Mendivil, Rashid M. Alam, Eva Chen, Iraneus Ogu, Jordan A. Lay, Tristan Y. Yang, Fernando L. Barroso da Silva, Malkiat Johal, Ilya Tolstorukov, Matthew H. Sazinsky, Animesh Ray, Stefano Lonardi The capacity of an antibody to recognize and bind an antigen with high specificity and strength (i.e., its binding affinity ) is a key determinant in the design and optimization of neutralizing antibodies against pathogenic targets. Here we introduce Ab-Affinity, a fine-tuned protein language model (PLM) that predicts the binding affinity of an antibody against a target peptide within the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein.
items.author: Faisal Bin Ashraf, Karen Paco, Sanaz Zebardast et al.

items.title: PhysInfer: A physics-constrained neural network for adaptive inference of transcriptional bursting from single-cell RNA-seq
items.summary: by Xiaodong Zeng, Jingwen Zhang, Shan Li, Haohua Wang Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has established that gene expression is driven by stochastic transcriptional bursting. However, inferring burst dynamics from static scRNA-seq snapshots is fundamentally constrained by parameter unidentifiability and model topology mismatch. Here, we propose PhysInfer, an unsupervised framework that integrates a physics-constrained neural network with adaptive model selection and parameter decoupling. A physics-informed loss function, combining stationary-distribution likelihood with zero-count anchoring, reparameterizes the optimization from unidentifiable microscopic rates to an interpretable macroscopic burst-quantity representation of burst size and burst frequency, thereby providing an interpretable parameterization for assessing practical recoverability in static data.
items.author: Xiaodong Zeng, Jingwen Zhang, Shan Li et al.

items.title: FDTest: Fluctuation-dissipation theorem as a test for memory effects in brain dynamics
items.summary: by Sebastian Manuel Geli, Juan Manuel Monti, Adrián Ponce-Alvarez, Gustavo Deco, Yonatan Sanz Perl A central challenge in neuroscience is to understand how the brain flexibly balances local and distributed information processing to support diverse cognitive and conscious states. We hypothesize that a key signature of this balance is the presence of memory effects, which arise when a brain region’s future activity depends not only on its current state, but also on past information fed back from the wider network. Here we introduce the FDTest, a method for assessing local memory effects in multidimensional systems by measuring violations of a generalized Fluctuation–dissipation theorem (FDT).
items.author: Sebastian Manuel Geli, Juan Manuel Monti, Adrián Ponce-Alvarez et al.

items.title: Tachykinin-like NLP-58 signaling through TKR-1 modulates thermotaxis behavior in Caenorhabditis elegans
items.summary: by Moon Sun Jang, Hironori J. Matsuyama, Ryoga Suzuki, King Chuen Law, Yukimasa Shibata, Xiaolin Zhang, Koutarou D. Kimura, Yukihiko Kubota, Masahiro Ito, Kiyoji Nishiwaki, Ikue Mori Neurokinin B (NKB) signaling plays a central role in mammalian thermoregulatory dysfunction associated with menopause, yet the underlying neural mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we establish Caenorhabditis elegans thermotaxis as a genetically tractable system for investigating conserved tachykinin signaling. We demonstrate that overexpression of nlp-58 , the C. elegans ortholog of mammalian NKB, induces abnormal thermotaxis behavior without impairing the temperature response of the thermosensory neurons. NLP-58 is expressed in multiple neurons, including the AIY interneurons, a central integrative node of the thermosensory circuit.
items.author: Moon Sun Jang, Hironori J. Matsuyama, Ryoga Suzuki et al.

items.title: Baloxavir and molnupiravir protect against severe influenza A(H5N1) infection in immunosuppressed hamsters
items.summary: by Andrea Arroyave, Henintsoa Rabezanahary, Ahmed Sahli, Mariana Baz Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) viruses continue to expand their geographic and host range, raising concerns about zoonotic transmission and pandemic preparedness. Immunocompromised individuals often develop severe and prolonged disease, yet evidence guiding antiviral therapy remains limited. Here, we characterized the pathogenesis and assessed direct-contact transmission of an influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b genotype D1.1 virus recently isolated from a human case in British Columbia, Canada, in cyclophosphamide-immunosuppressed hamsters, with normal hamsters included for comparison of infection outcomes and viral shedding kinetics. We also evaluated the antiviral efficacy of oseltamivir (20 mg/kg twice daily for 5 days), baloxavir (50 mg/kg, 2 doses), and molnupiravir (50 or 200 mg/kg twice daily) as monotherapies or in combination (oseltamivir with low-dose molnupiravir) in immunosuppressed hamsters.
items.author: Andrea Arroyave, Henintsoa Rabezanahary, Ahmed Sahli et al.

items.title: Nuclear egress complex promotes capsid nuclear egress during Kaposi’s Sarcoma-associated herpesvirus reactivation
items.summary: by Ariana C. Calkwood Calderon-Zavala, Olaide A. Adeyemi, Paula García-Valenciano Rodríguez, Alicia de Pablos Fernández, Nathalie R. Lavoie, Allison L. Didychuk, Ekaterina E. Heldwein During herpesvirus replication, newly assembled capsids exit the nucleus by nuclear egress, in which capsids bud at the inner nuclear membrane forming perinuclear enveloped virions that then fuse with the outer nuclear membrane, releasing capsids into the cytoplasm. This process is mediated by the nuclear egress complex (NEC), a conserved viral heterodimer of UL31 and UL34 homologs. Although prior studies demonstrated that overexpression of the NEC from Kaposi’s Sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) induces nuclear membrane vesiculation and proliferation in uninfected cells, its role during lytic replication remained undefined.
items.author: Ariana C. Calkwood Calderon-Zavala, Olaide A. Adeyemi, Paula García-Valenciano Rodríguez et al.

items.title: Swimming motility and type IV pili modulate phagocytosis by shaping physical interactions between Pseudomonas aeruginosa and macrophages
items.summary: by Tania Distler, Chia-Ni Tsai, Han-Yi Huang, Alice Pellegrino, Aaron Weimann, Zainebe Al-Mayyah, Lucas A. Meirelles, R. Andres Floto, Alexandre Persat During chronic lung infections, Pseudomonas aeruginosa diversifies under selection from antibiotics, metabolic constraints, and host defenses. Macrophages are key sentinels of the innate immune system and play a central role in clearing airway pathogens. Yet, how they process heterogeneous bacterial populations remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate how P. aeruginosa evades phagocytosis under conditions that resemble chronic infection. We use an attenuated mutant lacking a functional type III secretion system (T3SS), which reduces macrophage killing, allowing us to isolate determinants of bacterial susceptibility to phagocytosis.
items.author: Tania Distler, Chia-Ni Tsai, Han-Yi Huang et al.

items.title: The pore-forming protein APOL7C ruptures Leishmania major -containing parasitophorous vacuoles in dendritic cells to promote IL-12 production and the induction of T helper type 1 immunity
items.summary: by Gerone Gonzales, Liam Wilkinson, Eymi Cedeño, Song Huang, Cassandra M. Wood, Sidra Ajmal, Armaan Mohan, Neil McKenna, Robin M. Yates, Timothy E. Shutt, Matheus B. Carneiro, Nathan C. Peters, Johnathan Canton Classical dendritic cells (cDCs) are required for the efficient priming of T helper type 1 (Th1) immunity against Leishmania major infections in mice. They do so by producing large quantities of IL-12 in response to L. major infection. IL-12 in turn supports the generation of protective CD4 + Th1 cells. However, the mechanism(s) by which L. major instigates robust IL-12 production by cDCs has not been addressed. Here we show that expression of a pore-forming protein called APOL7C is induced in cDCs by L.
items.author: Gerone Gonzales, Liam Wilkinson, Eymi Cedeño et al.

items.title: What Makes a VLA Reactive? A Study of Execution Strategies for Dynamic Manipulation
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models predict chunks of future actions, and when objects move, those chunks go stale before they are executed. We study what makes a pretrained VLA reactive, using \pihalf{} on two dynamic simulation benchmarks and three real-robot tasks. We vary the prediction and execution horizons, compare synchronous and asynchronous inference, test methods that deliver actions sooner or keep successive chunks continuous, and adapt the policy with motion cues and latent-space reinforcement learning. The best prediction horizon is about one second, and the best execution horizon depends on the checkpoint. Short horizons help more with asynchronous execution, and methods that keep the trajectory continuous outperform those that only reduce latency.
items.author: Zhuoyue Li, Zhendong Han, Pankhuri Vanjani et al.

items.title: ActionCodec2: A Streaming Action Tokenizer
items.summary: Most action tokenizers for autoregressive vision language action (VLA) models compress motion into chunks that must be decoded in full before their actions become executable. We introduce ActionCodec2, a non-neural streaming tokenizer that releases actions incrementally while keeping trajectory reconstruction error within a prescribed tolerance. Its encoder quantizes each step relative to the decoder's reconstructed state, so the selected motion primitive corrects residual error rather than allowing errors from independently quantized increments to accumulate. Finding the smallest such primitive set is a geometric covering problem; we derive the exact minimum for translation and constant-factor-tight bounds for rotation. Set-BPE then losslessly merges co-occurring primitive symbols across coordinates and neighboring steps, without a fixed coordinate ordering.
items.author: Zibin Dong, Yicheng Liu, Shiduo Zhang et al.

items.title: FloCOS: Predicting Compact Forward Occupancy Sets of Surrounding Vehicles via Conditional Flow Matching
items.summary: Existing methods for predicting surrounding vehicles' forward occupancy may under-approximate the ground-truth occupancy, exposing the ego vehicle to collision risk, or produce overly conservative regions that unnecessarily restrict feasible space and cause planning failures. To address these issues, we propose FloCOS, a conditional flow-matching framework that predicts compact forward occupancy sets with high occupancy coverage. FloCOS represents the forward occupancy set as a time-varying union of half-space convex polygons parameterized by temporal basis coefficients. Conditional flow matching captures the conditional distribution of these coefficients to govern the temporal evolution of the convex components, trained under coverage and union-area losses that penalize missed occupancy and excess area.
items.author: Chuansheng Dong, Yinxiao Zhan, Zongdian Li et al.

items.title: Sparse, admissible and interpretable: discovery of isotropic limit surfaces with extended invariant libraries, physically gated mixtures of experts, and end-to-end structural identification
items.summary: Choosing and fitting a limit surface, a yield or failure criterion, to multiaxial strength tests is a model-selection problem with physical side conditions. The equivalent stress concept provides a catalogue of criteria with admissibility conditions: convexity, a unique surface definition, explicit solvability, and bounds on inelastic Poisson ratios. We recast the task as sparse, constrained, differentiable model discovery and compare three representations. The first is a library of invariant monomials I1^a q^m r3^c containing classical criteria as sparse members. The second extends this library by trigonometric Lode-angle terms, restricted by isotropy to cosine modes, and Podgorski-Bigoni-Piccolroaz (PBP) atoms with learnable shape parameters.
items.author: Michael A. Kraus

items.title: SPARC: RoboCup Standard Platform for Autonomous Rescue Competition with Initial Datasets, Software, and Simulation Environments
items.summary: The RoboCup Standard Platform for Autonomous Rescue Competition (SPARC) is a new competition under development of the RoboCup Rescue Robot League that uses the Unitree A2-W as a common robot platform. SPARC aims to make research on artificial intelligence for autonomous rescue robots accessible to a broader research community, including groups without expertise in developing and maintaining custom robot hardware. By providing a capable standard platform and established benchmark environments, researchers can focus on autonomous navigation, perception, manipulation, and embodied AI for challenging disaster-response scenarios. This paper introduces the SPARC competition, its benchmark environment, and the Unitree A2-W standard platform.
items.author: Yuezhong Wang, Bichi Zhang, Zhongli Yin et al.

items.title: Reinforcement learning to design near-perfect acoustic absorbers
items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) is proposed as a strategy for the multi-objective design of Helmholtz resonators with near-perfect acoustic absorption. The approach formulates resonator design as a sequential decision-making problem in which geometrical parameters are iteratively updated to balance competing objectives, including resonator volume, resonance frequency, and acoustic reflection. A Q-learning algorithm based on a neural network is developed to explore the design space and identify non-dominated solutions, providing a Pareto front of optimal configurations. The acoustic response is evaluated using a transfer matrix method that incorporates viscothermal losses and acoustic end corrections. Three representative designs are subsequently investigated using full-wave finite element simulations, showing good agreement in their absorption and reflection spectra and validating the accuracy of the reduced-order model.
items.author: M. Novelli, R. Arnau, L. M. Garcia-Raffi et al.

items.title: A Magnetic Neuroevolution Potential for Large Scale Spin-Lattice Simulations
items.summary: Accurately describing magnetic order, lattice vibrations, and their coupling at finite temperatures within a unified framework remains a major challenge in atomistic simulations of magnetic materials. In this work, we develop a magnetic neuroevolution potential that explicitly incorporates magnetic degrees of freedom, establishing a potential-energy description jointly determined by atomic structures and magnetic configurations and enabling unified predictions of atomic forces and magnetic energy gradients. Using CrN, Fe, and FeGe with collinear or noncollinear magnetic configurations as representative systems, we demonstrate that the model outperforms standard neuroevolution potentials without magnetic descriptors in predicting energies, atomic forces, and virials, while yielding equilibrium lattice constants consistent with experimental values.
items.author: Rongkun Chen, Junhan Li, Feng Xiao et al.

items.title: A physics-constrained deep reinforcement learning method for autonomous mission planning of Titan deep space probes
items.summary: Titan is a compelling target for future deep space exploration, while its extreme Earth-Titan distance and complex environment make continuous ground-in-the-loop planning impractical. Existing planning methods, primarily developed for Earth-observation scenarios, have limited generalizability to uncertain deep space conditions and adaptability to time-varying mission states. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a physics-constrained maskable proximal policy optimization (PCM-PPO) method for Titan autonomous mission planning. A Titan-specific discrete-time Markov decision process is established to characterize mission feasibility and resource constraints. A system dynamics and geometric model is incorporated to enhance physical representation, including central gravity, J2 perturbation, third-body attraction, and downlink occultation.
items.author: Hanmin Li, Tao Wang, Shuangliang Liu et al.

items.title: Actuation and Control of Passive Tendon-Driven Soft Extensions Through Rigid Manipulator Motion
items.summary: Industrial manipulators offer reach and precision but can damage nearby structures in confined spaces. Soft robots provide compliant contact but typically have limited reach. Rigid-soft systems combine their advantages, although they often require dedicated actuation and control hardware. We propose actuating a passive tendon-driven soft extension through manipulator joint motion. As the robot moves, the exterior spans of tendons anchored to upstream links change, altering tendon tension and deforming the extension. Inspection through narrow apertures, for example, constrains the motion of the end effector (EE). We develop a controller that regulates the soft tip while preserving such EE constraints. A differential model separates rigid transport from soft deformation, combining analytic arm and tendon kinematics with a locally identified span-to-deformation map.

items.title: Directed Domain Wall Motion by Radio-Frequency Currents
items.summary: Magnetic domain walls (DWs) are central to emerging spintronic technologies for memory, logic and neuromorphic computing, where their controlled displacement is a key functionality. While current-induced DW motion driven by spin-orbit torques is well established under direct currents, it remains unclear how radio-frequency (RF) currents couple to DWs and whether they can generate directed motion under a symmetric periodic drive. Here we show that RF currents drive DW oscillations, which can be rectified into directed motion through symmetry breaking. Using time-resolved and static magneto-optical Kerr microscopy, we demonstrate that RF spin-orbit torques efficiently excite low-frequency DW oscillations well below the ferromagnetic resonance frequency.
